final answer
I now have the complete picture across all three doctypes and the shared controllers/services. Here is the full trace. ## 1. Sales Order — commitment only, no stock, no GL **File:** `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` — class `SalesOrder(SellingController)`; mapper `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py` - A Sales Order is a *commitment* document: it creates **no Stock Ledger Entry (SLE)** and **no GL Entry**. Optionally it reserves stock via **Stock Reservation Entry** (handled by `SellingController.update_stock_reservation_entries`, `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:930`). - It seeds the linkage chain: `SalesOrder.__init__` sets up `self.status_updater` (line ~187) which tracks `delivered_qty` / `per_delivered` (fed by Delivery Note) and `billed_amt` / `per_billed` (fed by Sales Invoice) on each `Sales Order Item`. - `mapper.make_delivery_note()` (line 232) maps `Sales Order Item.name → so_detail` and `parent → against_sales_order`, copying only the unbilled/undelivered remainder (`condition` at line 296: `abs(doc.delivered_qty) < abs(doc.qty)`). `mapper.make_sales_invoice()` (line 425) covers direct SO→SI billing. ## 2. Delivery Note — stock leaves, and the *expense side* is decided here **Files:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py` — class `DeliveryNote(SellingController)`; GL composer `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py` — class `DeliveryNoteGLComposer(BaseStockGLComposer)` `DeliveryNote.on_submit()` (line 481) runs, in order: 1. `update_prevdoc_status()` → via the `status_updater` map built in `DeliveryNote.__init__` (line 155), bumps `delivered_qty` / `per_delivered` on the Sales Order Item (the `extra_cond` ensures a Sales Invoice with `update_stock=1` is counted as an alternative "second source", never both). 2. `update_billing_status()` → `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status` → `StockController.update_billing_percentage()` (`stock_controller.py:308`) maintains `billed_amt` / `per_billed`. 3. **`update_stock_ledger()`** (`selling_controller.py:676`) → `get_item_list()` → `get_sle_for_source_warehouse()` → `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries()` → `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py::make_sl_entries` — creates **outward SLEs** carrying `stock_value_difference` (the valuation), keyed to `voucher_type="Delivery Note"`, `voucher_detail_no=<row name>`. 4. **`make_gl_entries()`** (`stock_controller.py:178`) → `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries()` (line 433) → `DeliveryNoteGLComposer.compose()` → inherited `BaseStockGLComposer.compose()` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`). # Stock Item Lifecycle: Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice ## The class hierarchy that makes it all work `SalesOrder`, `DeliveryNote` and `SalesInvoice` all inherit from **`SellingController`** (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`), which inherits **`StockController`** (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`) → `AccountsController`. The stock/GL machinery lives in the controllers; each doctype only decides *whether* to invoke it. ## Stage 1 — Sales Order: a commitment, not an accounting event - **`SalesOrder(SellingController)`** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`, class at line 40). Its `on_submit` (line 450) does `update_prevdoc_status`, `check_credit_limit`, `update_reserved_qty` (→ `SalesOrderStockReservation`, line 544) and optionally creates **Stock Reservation Entries** (line 470–471). **No Stock Ledger Entries, no GL entries** — nothing can be double-booked at this stage. - **`make_delivery_note`** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py`, line 232) maps SO → DN via `get_mapped_doc`, carrying `so_detail` / `against_sales_order` into each Delivery Note Item. - When the DN submits, the **status_updater** configured in `DeliveryNote.__init__` (delivery_note.py lines 157–176) writes `Sales Order Item.delivered_qty`, `per_delivered`, and `delivery_status` ("Delivered"). ## Stage 2 — Delivery Note: stock moves and COGS is booked **`DeliveryNote(SellingController)`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`). `DeliveryNote.on_submit` (line 481) runs, in order: 1. **`update_prevdoc_status()`** — pushes delivered qty into the SO via `status_updater`. 2. **`update_billing_status()`** (line 645) — delegates to **`BillingStatusService`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/billing_status.py`), computing `per_billed`. 3. **`update_stock_ledger()`** — `SellingController.update_stock_ledger` (selling_controller.py lines 676–706) builds an outbound SLE per stock item via `get_sle_for_source_warehouse` (line 708, `voucher_detail_no` = the DN Item row name) and calls `StockController.make_sl_entries`. Each SLE records `stock_value_difference` — the valuation of what actually left the warehouse. 4. **`make_gl_entries()`** → `StockController.make_gl_entries` (stock_controller.py line 178, perpetual-inventory-gated) → `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries` (delivery_note.py line 433) → **`DeliveryNoteGLComposer`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`), a thin subclass of **`BaseStockGLComposer`** (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`). The COGS entry itself is `BaseStockGLComposer.compose()` (lines 45–98): it pulls the voucher's submitted SLEs via `doc.get_stock_ledger_details()` and, for each SLE, posts the pair: - **Debit** `sle.stock_value_difference` to the warehouse's *inventory account* - **Credit** the same amount to `item_row.expense_account` (the COGS account) Because the amount comes from the SLE, COGS is exactly the valuation of goods moved, tied to that one voucher. `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account` (line 438) may set `item.expense_account` to the **Stock Delivered But Not Billed** account (if "Enable Stock Delivered But Not Billed" is on), making the interim booking land there instead of COGS. ## Stage 3 — Sales Invoice: revenue only (normally), stock untouched - **`SalesInvoice(SellingController)`** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, class at line 62). - **`make_sales_invoice`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py`, line 62) maps DN → SI with the critical link: `"name": "dn_detail"`, `"parent": "delivery_note"` (lines 140–146), qty = pending unbilled qty (`get_invoiced_qty_map` / `get_pending_qty`). It does **not** map `update_stock`. - `update_stock` defaults to **0**, and in `sales_invoice.json` (line 716–728) it is even hidden when rows carry `dn_detail` (`depends_on: doc.items.every((item) => !item.dn_detail)`) — "Leave unchecked if a Delivery Note is created separately." - **`SalesInvoice.on_submit`** (line 421): `check_prev_docstatus()` (line 1016, throws if the DN isn't submitted), `update_prevdoc_status()`, **`update_billing_status_in_dn()`** (line 1084 — writes `billed_amt` on `Delivery Note Item` and calls `DeliveryNote.update_billing_percentage`), then: ```python if self.update_stock == 1: # line 443 — skipped for DN-billed invoices ... self.update_stock_ledger() ... self.make_gl_entries() # line 458 ``` - `make_gl_entries` → `SalesInvoice.get_gl_entries` (line 1070) → **`SalesInvoiceGLComposer`** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`): customer, taxes, and income entries always; the stock/COGS loop only conditionally: ```python # make_item_gl_entries, lines 374–375 if cint(doc.update_stock) and erpnext.is_perpetual_inventory_enabled(doc.company): gl_entries += super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries() ``` That `super(SalesInvoice, doc)` call re-binds the invoice instance to `StockController.get_gl_entries` → `BaseStockGLComposer` — the *same* COGS loop the DN used. With `update_stock = 0` the invoice books **revenue (credit income / debit Debtor) and nothing stock-related**. ## How "exactly once" COGS is enforced **1. Structural: one voucher moves the stock, and COGS derives from that voucher's SLEs.** COGS is not computed independently by each document — it is `Σ sle.stock_value_difference` for *that voucher's* SLEs. The invoice never generates SLEs for delivered goods (no `update_stock_ledger` call, no SLE → no `stock_value_difference` → no COGS entry). The inverse case is equally guarded: an invoice that *does* check Update Stock (drop-ship / direct dispatch, no DN) books stock+COGS itself, and then: **2. Hard validation — `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note()`** (sales_invoice.py lines 904–915, invoked from `validate` at line 335): *"If items are linked with a delivery note, stock cannot be updated again"* — it throws `Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes: …` if `update_stock` is checked while any item has `delivery_note` set. Both documents can never move the same stock. **3. Billing-integrity guards** (revenue side, which prevents duplicate *COGS-linked* consumption of delivered qty): - `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` (sales_invoice.py line 353; `erpnext/accounts/services/billing_validation.py` line 16) — blocks over-billing a DN row. - `check_prev_docstatus` (SI on_submit) requires the DN submitted; DN's `check_next_docstatus` (delivery_note.py line 623) blocks cancelling a DN with a submitted invoice. **4. The SDBNB reclassification — what happens when the DN is *way* ahead of the invoice.** With "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" enabled, the DN's COGS temporarily sits in the **SDBNB account** (set on DN items by `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account`). At invoice time, `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` (gl_composer.py lines 164–253) finds items with `dn_detail`, reads the DN's SLE (`stock_value_difference / actual_qty × stock_qty`) and posts a **reclassification pair: credit SDBNB → debit the item's real expense account (COGS)**. This is not a second expense — it relocates the already-booked amount to its final P&L account, so expense recognition still happens exactly once, just staged through the interim account until the invoice arrives. ## Summary table | | Sales Order | Delivery Note | Sales Invoice (from DN, `update_stock=0`) | |---|---|---|---| | Stock Ledger Entry | ✗ | ✓ (`SellingController.update_stock_ledger`) | ✗ (gated at sales_invoice.py:443) | | COGS / stock GL | ✗ | ✓ (`DeliveryNoteGLComposer` ← `BaseStockGLComposer`, from SLE `stock_value_difference`) | ✗ (gated at gl_composer.py:374); only SDBNB→COGS reclass if enabled | | Revenue GL | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ (income vs Debtor) | | Status | `delivered_qty`/`per_delivered` updated by DN | `per_billed` updated by SI (`update_billing_status_in_dn`) | `billed_qty` on SO Item |

Sales Order — a commitment, nothing financial `SalesOrder` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`) posts **no Stock Ledger Entries and no GL entries**. On submit it only runs status/billing bookkeeping via its `status_updater` config (`erpnext/controllers/status_updater.py` — updates `billed_amt`/`per_billed` on `Sales Order Item`) and optionally reserves stock via `Stock Reservation Entry`. Items flow downstream through two mappers in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py`: - `make_delivery_note()` — maps `Sales Order Item → Delivery Note Item` with the links `name → so_detail`, `parent → against_sales_order`. - `make_sales_invoice()` (line 425) — maps to `Sales Invoice Item` with `name → so_detail`, and `update_item()` deducts already-billed quantities via `get_billed_qty()`. ## 2. Delivery Note — where stock leaves AND COGS is booked `DeliveryNote.on_submit()` (`delivery_note.py:481`) does, in order: 1. `update_prevdoc_status()` — pushes `delivered_qty`/`per_delivered` back to Sales Order Item. 2. **`update_stock_ledger()`** (`delivery_note.py:511`) → `SellingController.update_stock_ledger` (`selling_controller.py:676`): for every row of `get_item_list()` that is `is_stock_item`, it builds outgoing `Stock Ledger Entry` dicts via `get_sle_for_source_warehouse()` / `get_sle_for_target_warehouse()`, then `make_sl_entries()` → `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:204`) → `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.make_sl_entries` (`stock_ledger.py:104`), which creates the SLEs, updates `Bin` quantities and re-posts subsequent valuation. 3. **`make_gl_entries()`** (`delivery_note.py:512`) → `StockController.make_gl_entries` (`stock_controller.py:178`), gated by `erpnext.is_perpetual_inventory_enabled(company)`. It fetches warehouse→inventory-account mappings via `get_inventory_account_map()` and calls `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries()` (`delivery_note.py:433`) → **`DeliveryNoteGLComposer`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py:7`), a thin subclass of **`BaseStockGLComposer`** (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py:12`). 4. `BaseStockGLComposer.compose()` (line 27) is where COGS physically happens: it pulls `sle_map = doc.get_stock_ledger_details()` — the SLEs of *this voucher*, keyed by `voucher_detail_no` — and for each item row × SLE appends exactly **two** GL entries: - **Inventory account** (e.g. Stock In Hand): `debit = sle.stock_value_difference` — negative on an outbound delivery, so the warehouse account is *credited* for the stock value; - **`item.expense_account`** (the COGS account on `Delivery Note Item`): `debit = -1 × stock_value_difference` — the **COGS debit**, validated by `check_expense_account()` (line 259). The `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` docstring confirms it: *"Delivery Note posts the standard stock ↔ expense (COGS) entries produced by the base stock GL loop and adds no voucher-specific rows."* So after DN submission: inventory down, COGS booked, stock value settled — even though the customer hasn't been invoiced yet. ## 3. Sales Invoice — pure billing (usually) `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py::make_sales_invoice` (line 62) maps `Delivery Note Item → Sales Invoice Item` with `name → dn_detail`, `parent → delivery_note`, plus `so_detail`/`sales_order`; `get_pending_qty()`/`get_invoiced_qty_map()`/`get_returned_qty_map()` compute only the un-invoiced remainder. **Crucially, it does not set `update_stock`** — the invoice is born as a billing document. `SalesInvoice.validate()` (`sales_invoice.py:289`) runs the guards, and `SalesInvoice.on_submit()` (`sales_invoice.py:421`) runs: - `check_prev_docstatus()` (line 1016) — throws if the referenced Delivery Note isn't submitted. - `BillingValidationService(self).validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` (line 353; service at `erpnext/accounts/services/billing_validation.py:16`) — sums billed amounts per `dn_detail` row *including other submitted invoices* (`get_already_billed_amount`) and throws "Cannot overbill…" beyond the allowance — one delivered row can only be billed once. - `update_billing_status_in_dn()` (line 440, def at 1084) — writes billed amounts back to the Delivery Note so its status becomes "Billed/Completed". - `self.make_gl_entries()` (line 458) → `SalesInvoiceGLComposer` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py:19`). In `make_item_gl_entries()` (line 346), the invoice books **income only** (`_append_item_income_gl_entry` → credit `income_account`). The stock/COGS block runs **only** under: ```python if cint(doc.update_stock) and erpnext.is_perpetual_inventory_enabled(doc.company): gl_entries += super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries() # line 374-375 ``` That `super()` call routes back to `StockController.get_gl_entries` → `BaseStockGLComposer` — but it composes from the *invoice's own SLEs*, which exist only when `update_stock=1`. With `update_stock=0`, the invoice's GL is simply Dr Debtors / Cr Income (+ taxes) — **no inventory or COGS rows are generated at all**. # How ERPNext guarantees COGS is booked exactly once 1. **COGS is SLE-driven, not invoice-driven.** `BaseStockGLComposer.compose()` only produces inventory↔expense pairs from `stock_value_difference` of the voucher's *own* Stock Ledger Entries (`get_stock_ledger_details()`). A non-stock-updating Sales Invoice has zero SLEs, so it is *structurally incapable* of producing a second COGS entry. The move is owned by whichever voucher created the SLE — the Delivery Note. 2. **`SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note()`** (`sales_invoice.py:904`) — the explicit hard guard, with the docstring *"If items are linked with a delivery note, stock cannot be updated again."* If `update_stock` is checked while any item row carries a `delivery_note` reference, submission throws: *"Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes: …"*. The two delivery paths (DN vs stock-updating SI) are mutually exclusive per row. 3. **The mapper defaults to the safe path.** DN→SI mapping never enables `update_stock`; it wires `dn_detail` links instead. And the reverse mapper `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/mapper.py::make_delivery_note` (line 33) filters rows with `condition: not doc.dn_detail and doc.qty - doc.delivered_qty > 0` — an invoice-first flow only generates a DN for rows not already delivered via stock. 4. **Delivered-qty accounting counts each movement once.** `SellingController.get_already_delivered_qty()` (`selling_controller.py:442`) sums `Delivery Note Item.qty` **plus** `Sales Invoice Item.qty` only `WHERE si.update_stock == 1` — a stock-updating invoice counts as a delivery, a billing-only one doesn't, so over-delivery checks against the SO never double-count. Likewise `SalesInvoice.update_status_updater_args()` (`sales_invoice.py:594`) marks SO items "Delivered" only with the `extra_cond: update_stock = 1`. 5. **Revenue is also once per delivered row**, enforced by `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing` against `dn_detail` (over-billing beyond allowance is blocked unless the user has `role_allowed_to_over_bill`). 6. **Ordering is enforced both ways**: `check_prev_docstatus()` blocks invoicing an un-submitted DN, and `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` → `check_next_docstatus()` (`delivery_note.py:519`) blocks cancelling a DN already referenced by a submitted invoice. # The "well before" gap: Stock Delivered But Not Billed For the period between DN submission and invoicing, ERPNext optionally uses the **"Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB)** account type (Company field `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed`). If the DN's item expense account is of account type `Stock Delivered But Not Billed`, the COGS value sits in that balance-sheet suspense account at delivery. When the Sales Invoice is finally submitted, `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries()` (`gl_composer.py:164`) and its helpers `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` (line 174) / `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` (line 222) perform a **reclassification, not a second booking**: they look the valuation up from the DN's own SLE (`Stock Ledger Entry` filtered by `voucher_no = delivery_note`, `voucher_detail_no = dn_detail` → `valuation_rate = stock_value_difference / actual_qty`), then credit SDBNB and debit the real COGS `expense_account` for `valuation_rate × item.stock_qty`. The expense is computed from the delivery's valuation exactly once and merely moved from suspense to P&L at billing time. (Conversely, when no DN exists — POS or `update_stock=1` invoicing — the SI takes over the entire `update_stock_ledger()` → `make_gl_entries()` path itself, lines 443–461 of `sales_invoice.py`, and then a later DN creation is prevented by the mapper condition above.) **Summary of the invariant:** the COGS debit is bound to the Stock Ledger Entry created by the stock-affecting voucher. `DeliveryNoteGLComposer`/`BaseStockGLComposer` turn each outbound SLE into exactly one inventory-credit + one COGS-debit pair at DN submission; `SalesInvoiceGLComposer` only reaches that same composer when `update_stock=1`, and `validate_delivery_note()` forbids that combination for DN-linked rows — so the "goods-out" cost is recognized exactly once, no matter how long the invoicing gap is.

I now have the complete picture. Here is the full trace of the subcontracting flow in ERPNext. ## Overview of the object graph `Purchase Order (is_subcontracted)` → **Subcontracting Order** (+ child `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`) → **Stock Entry** (purpose `Send to Subcontractor`) → **Subcontracting Receipt** (+ child `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item`) → optional billing `Purchase Receipt`. The base class shared by SCO/SCR is `SubcontractingController` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`, which holds the mapping dict `subcontract_data` (`order_doctype: "Subcontracting Order"`, `order_field: "subcontracting_order"`, `rm_detail_field: "sco_rm_detail"`). ## Stage 1 – Defining what raw material to supply (Purchase Order → Subcontracting Order) - `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/services/subcontracting.py` — class `SubcontractingService`: `validate_fg_item_for_subcontracting()` (FG must be `is_sub_contracted_item` with BOM), `set_service_items_for_finished_goods()` (service item via `Subcontracting BOM`), `auto_create_subcontracting_order()` (if Buying Settings `auto_create_subcontracting_order`). - `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/mapper.py` — `make_subcontracting_order()` / `get_mapped_subcontracting_order()` maps PO → SCO (calls `SubcontractingOrder.populate_items_table()`). - `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` — class `SubcontractingOrder`: - `validate()` → inherited `SubcontractingController.validate()` → `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")` → `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()` → `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items()` → `_get_materials_from_bom()` explodes the FG's BOM into the **`Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`** child table (`rm_item_code`, `main_item_code`, `required_qty`, `reserve_warehouse` set by `__update_reserve_warehouse()`). - Cost preview: `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount()` (rm_cost_per_qty from BOM), `calculate_service_costs()`, `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`. - `on_submit()`: `update_status()` (→ "Open"/"Material Transferred"…), `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po()` (writes `subcontracted_qty` on `Purchase Order Item`), `reserve_raw_materials()` (creates Stock Reservation Entries via `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reservation_entry/stock_reservation_entry.py`). - `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` → `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py` reserves RM in the reserve warehouse. ## Stage 2 – Moving RM from your warehouse to the supplier (Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor") - `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` — **`make_rm_stock_entry()`** (whitelisted): maps SCO → Stock Entry, `post_process` sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"`, and per RM row sets `s_warehouse` = supplied item's `warehouse/reserve_warehouse` (your company warehouse), `t_warehouse` = SCO `supplier_warehouse`, and crucially `sco_rm_detail` = the `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` name + `subcontracted_item` = FG code. This row-level link is what tracks the transfer against the SCO. (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py::get_items_from_subcontract_order` is the Stock-Entry-side wrapper.) - `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` — `_configure_purpose_class()` maps purpose → **`SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`**; `set_stock_entry_type()` picks the standard Stock Entry Type "Send to Subcontractor" (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry_type/stock_entry_type.py`); the generic SLE builder posts the transfer (company warehouse out, supplier_warehouse in) with `make_package_for_transfer` for serial/batch bundles. - `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` — class `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`: - `validate_subcontract_order()` honors Buying Settings **`backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`** (`"BOM"` vs `"Material Transferred for Subcontract"`) and `over_transfer_allowance`; `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom()` / `_validate_transfer_qty()` / `get_total_supplied_qty()` / `get_total_returned_qty()` cap over-transfer against the SCO's supplied items. - `on_submit()/on_cancel()` → `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items()` → `get_supplied_items()` aggregates submitted Stock Entries per `sco_rm_detail` and writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty`, `total_supplied_qty` back into `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`; `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` releases bins. - `StockEntry.update_subcontracting_order_status()` (stock_entry.py) flips SCO status to "Material Transferred"/"Partial Material Transferred" via `set_subcontracting_order_status` in `subcontracting_order.py`. - Unused RM comes back via `get_materials_from_supplier()` → `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract()` + `add_items_in_ste()` (subcontracting_controller.py), which builds an `is_return` Material Transfer from the supplier warehouse, keyed by the same `sco_rm_detail`. ## Stage 3 – Subcontracting Receipt: backflush, reconciliation, cost roll-up - Mapping: `make_subcontracting_receipt()` / `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt()` in `subcontracting_order.py` (maps `subcontracting_order_item`, BOM, pending qty, process-loss qty). - `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py` — class `SubcontractingReceipt`, with `status_updater` pushing `received_qty` into `Subcontracting Order Item` and `per_received` on the SCO. - Backflush/reconciliation (all in `SubcontractingController`): - `validate()` → `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")` → `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()` → `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items()`: - `get_available_materials()` → `__get_transferred_items()` queries submitted Stock Entries with purpose `Send to Subcontractor` (or return `Material Transfer`) tied to the SCO, builds `available_materials` keyed `(rm_item_code, main_item_code, subcontracting_order)` with serial/batch data (via `get_voucher_wise_serial_batch_from_bundle`), then `__update_consumed_materials()` subtracts what previous Subcontracting Receipts already consumed (`__get_received_items` / `__get_consumed_items` on `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item`). - `__set_supplied_or_received_items()` fills consumed qty: BOM mode (`_get_materials_from_bom` × `qty_consumed_per_unit × received_qty`) or "Material Transferred" mode (`__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer`, proportional to what was actually sent). - `__add_supplied_or_received_item()` appends `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item` rows with `consumed_qty`, sets `subcontracting_order`, and assigns serials/batches via `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle()` (`SerialBatchCreation` in `erpnext/stock/serial_batch_bundle.py`) or `set_batch_for_supplied_items()` when `use_serial_batch_fields`. - `__validate_supplied_or_received_items()` (`__validate_batch_no`, `__validate_serial_no`) throws if you consume batches/serials never supplied against the SCO. - Cost roll-up: - `set_rate_for_supplied_items()` / `set_valuation_rate_for_rm()` re-price each consumed RM row with `get_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py`) against the **supplier warehouse** valuation at posting time; `__set_rate_for_serial_and_batch_bundle()` uses the bundle `avg_rate`. - `SubcontractingReceipt.set_missing_values()` → `set_available_qty_for_consumption()` (available = `total_supplied_qty − consumed_qty` from SCO supplied items) and **`calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`** — the roll-up: `item.rm_supp_cost` = Σ consumed RM amounts; `rm_cost_per_qty = rm_supp_cost / received_qty`; FG `rate = rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed_cost_voucher_amount`; amount adjusted by BOM `cost_allocation_per`. - `validate_bom_required_qty()` + `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty()` enforce consumed RM ≥ BOM requirement (`BOMQuantityError`); secondary/scrap handled by `get_secondary_items()` / `remove_secondary_items()` / `validate_secondary_items()`. - `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit()`: - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()` → `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()` writes `consumed_qty` back into `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` (closing the tracking loop), and `set_subcontracting_order_status()` updates each SCO's status. - `update_stock_ledger()` (overridden in `SubcontractingController`): posts SLEs for accepted FG at `set_warehouse` with `incoming_rate = item.rate` and `recalculate_rate = 1` (i.e., the rolled-up cost becomes the FG's stock valuation), rejected qty to `rejected_warehouse`, then **`make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse()`** posts negative `actual_qty = -consumed_qty` at `supplier_warehouse` — physically consuming the RM sitting with the supplier. `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty()` refreshes SCO bins. - GL entries: `get_gl_entries()` → **`SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer`** (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`, extends `erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`): debits FG inventory with the SLE `stock_value_diff`, credits service cost (`service_cost_per_qty × qty`), reclassifies consumed RM value (`rm_supp_cost`) out of supplier-warehouse inventory into expense, books additional costs, LCV (`_make_item_gl_entries_for_lcv`) and any `divisional_loss` (`item.amount − stock_value_diff`). - Billing: `auto_create_purchase_receipt()` → `make_purchase_receipt()` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py` (creates the `Purchase Receipt` against the PO with `is_subcontracted=1`; also `make_subcontract_return()` / `make_subcontract_return_against_rejected_warehouse()` for returns). ## Key knobs Buying Settings: `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on` ("BOM" vs "Material Transferred for Subcontract" — decides whether SCR consumption is derived from the BOM or from actual transfers), `over_transfer_allowance`, `validate_consumed_qty`, `auto_create_subcontracting_order`, `auto_create_purchase_receipt`. Helper report: `erpnext/buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred/`. In short: **`SubcontractingOrder`** defines RM per BOM (`Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` + `sco_rm_detail` links) → **`make_rm_stock_entry`** + **`SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`** physically move RM to `supplier_warehouse` and record `supplied_qty`/`total_supplied_qty` on the SCO → **`SubcontractingReceipt`** backflushes `consumed_qty` from that same link, validates it against what was transferred/ordered, re-prices it at the supplier warehouse (`get_incoming_rate`), rolls `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty (+LCV)` into the FG rate (`calculate_items_qty_and_amount`), posts the FG SLE at that rolled-up rate while crediting the supplier-warehouse RM out (`make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse`), mirrors it all in GL via `SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer`, and writes `consumed_qty` back to the SCO.

Here's the full trace of the subcontracting flow. # The Subcontracting Flow in ERPNext Everything hangs off one shared base class — **`SubcontractingController`** in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` (extends `StockController`). Its `__init__` (lines 28–47) sets a `subcontract_data` dict that parameterizes the whole flow: `order_doctype: "Subcontracting Order"`, `order_field: "subcontracting_order"`, `rm_detail_field: "sco_rm_detail"`, `order_supplied_items_field: "Subcontracting Order Supplied Item"`, `receipt_supplied_items_field: "Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item"`. (The same class also serves the legacy Purchase-Order-based flow and `Subcontracting Inward Order`.) ## Stage 0 — Subcontracting Order builds the "Raw Materials Supplied" list - `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`, class **`SubcontractingOrder(SubcontractingController)`**. Created from a subcontracted Purchase Order (`validate_purchase_order_for_subcontracting`, line 134); `populate_items_table()` (line 238) pulls FG items/service items and picks the BOM (`Subcontracting BOM` or item default). - `SubcontractingController.validate()` (lines 58–68) calls **`create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")`** (line 1103) → `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()` (line 1094) → `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items()` (line 1039). For the order doctype itself, `__set_supplied_or_received_items()` (line 932) explodes the BOM via **`_get_materials_from_bom()`** (line 560) and `__add_supplied_or_received_item()` (line 695) to fill the **`Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`** child table with `required_qty`, `reserve_warehouse` (the company warehouse RMs will be drawn from), and alternative-item handling. - Cost preview: `SubcontractingOrder.set_missing_values()` (line 183) → `calculate_service_costs()` (`service_cost_per_qty` from service items), `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount()` (`rm_cost_per_qty` from BOM), `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`. - `on_submit()` (line 125): `update_status()`, `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po()`, `reserve_raw_materials()` (Stock Reservation Entries), and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` (line 229) → `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting`. ## Stage 1 — RM transfer: Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor" - The UI button calls **`make_rm_stock_entry(subcontract_order, rm_items, order_doctype)`** — whitelisted, `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` lines 1343–1466. It maps the SCO into a **Stock Entry** with `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"`, `subcontracting_order` link, and one row per RM with: - `s_warehouse` = the RM's `reserve_warehouse` (company's own warehouse), `t_warehouse` = SCO's `supplier_warehouse` (stock physically moves into a "Supplier" warehouse), - `sco_rm_detail` = the `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` row name (the tracking link), `subcontracted_item` = the FG item, - over-transfer capped by `Buying Settings.over_transfer_allowance`. - Dispatch: `StockEntry._configure_purpose_class()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` (lines 196–209) maps `"Send to Subcontractor"` → **`SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`, extends `BaseStockEntry`). - Validation before transfer: `validate_subcontract_order()` branches on `Buying Settings.backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`: - **"BOM"** → `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` / `_get_required_qty_for_bom` / `_validate_transfer_qty`, which total previously supplied qty via `get_total_supplied_qty()` / `get_total_returned_qty()` (queries submitted SEs joined on `subcontracting_order` + `sco_rm_detail`); - **"Material Transferred for Subcontract"** → `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` + `_link_rm_detail_if_missing`/`get_order_rm_detail`. - On submit/cancel: `on_submit()` → **`update_subcontract_order_supplied_items()`** (line 172) → `get_supplied_items()` (module function, lines 214–249: aggregates `transfer_qty` of all submitted SEs per `sco_rm_detail`, netting out `is_return` rows) → `_update_supplied_items_in_order()` writes **`supplied_qty` / `returned_qty` / `total_supplied_qty` back onto `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`**; `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` releases the bin reservation. Return transfers (leftover RM coming back) also funnel through here via `MaterialTransferStockEntry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py`, lines ~170–172). - Visibility of what's still to be sent: report `erpnext/buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred.py` (`get_order_items_to_supply` reads the supplied-item table; pending = `required_qty − transferred − returned`). ## Stage 2 — Creating the Subcontracting Receipt - **`make_subcontracting_receipt()` → `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt()`** in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` (lines 440–491): maps SCO → **`Subcontracting Receipt`**, `Subcontracting Order Item` → `Subcontracting Receipt Item`, carrying `subcontracting_order`, `subcontracting_order_item`, `bom`, pending qty (`qty − received_qty`), and BOM `process_loss_percentage`. It also carries `service_cost_per_qty` forward (same field name on both tables). - Doctype class **`SubcontractingReceipt(SubcontractingController)`** in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. Its `status_updater` (`__init__`, lines 101–116) pushes `received_qty` back to `Subcontracting Order Item.received_qty` and `Subcontracting Order.per_received` on submit; `update_status_updater_args()` (line 651) adds return-qty updaters when `is_return`. ## Stage 3 — Reconciliation (backflush) of consumed RM against what was transferred - On validate (`SubcontractingController.validate` → `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")`): 1. `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items()` (1039–1047) → `initialized_fields()` (reads the backflush setting) → `__get_subcontract_orders()` → `__get_pending_qty_to_receive()` → **`get_available_materials()`** (463–535): - `__get_transferred_items()` (312–358) queries all submitted Stock Entries with `subcontracting_order` in scope and purpose `"Send to Subcontractor"` (or return `Material Transfer`), returning RM qty, rate, serials/batches, `sco_rm_detail`, `subcontracted_item`; - builds `available_materials` keyed `(rm_item_code, main_item_code, subcontracting_order)`, merging serial/batch data via `get_voucher_wise_serial_batch_from_bundle`; - **`__update_consumed_materials("Subcontracting Receipt")`** (398–461) subtracts what earlier submitted receipts already consumed (read from `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item.consumed_qty` via `__get_received_items`/`__get_consumed_items`), including per-serial/per-batch netting. 2. `__set_supplied_or_received_items()` (932–976): with backflush = **"Material Transferred for Subcontract"**, each FG row consumes from `available_materials` (qty prorated by `__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer`, 911–930), creating `supplied_items` rows with `consumed_qty` and serial/batch picks; with backflush = **"BOM"** (or returns), it derives consumption from `_get_materials_from_bom()`. 3. `__validate_supplied_or_received_items()` (1076–1092) → `__validate_batch_no` / `__validate_serial_no`: you can only consume batches/serials that were actually transferred against that SCO. - `SubcontractingController.set_valuation_rate_for_rm()` (70–100) then re-prices each supplied row with `get_incoming_rate` against the **supplier warehouse** — i.e., RM cost = the weighted-average value of the stock sitting at the supplier. ## Stage 4 — Cost roll-up on the FG - `SubcontractingReceipt.set_missing_values()` (455–458) runs: - `set_available_qty_for_consumption()` (460–494): per RM, `available_qty = SCO total_supplied_qty − consumed_qty`; - `SubcontractingController.calculate_additional_costs()` (1243–1271): distributes the `additional_costs` table (by Qty or Amount) into `additional_cost_per_qty`; - **`SubcontractingReceipt.calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`** (496–562), the roll-up itself: - `supplied_items.amount = consumed_qty × rate`, summed per FG row into `rm_supp_cost` / **`rm_cost_per_qty`**; - secondary/scrap item costs (rows from `get_secondary_items()`, 377–445, which also allocates cost by BOM `cost_allocation_per`) → `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`; - FG rate = `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed_cost_voucher_amount/qty`, adjusted for BOM allocation % and process loss (`qty = received_qty − process_loss_qty`); sets `total_qty`/`total`. - Pre-submit validation: `validate_bom_required_qty()` (603–641) with `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty()` — errors if consumed RM falls short of BOM requirement (governed by `validate_consumed_qty` in Buying Settings). ## Stage 5 — Submission effects `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit()` (168–185): 1. `validate_closed_subcontracting_order()`, `validate_bom_required_qty()`; 2. status updater → SCO Item `received_qty`/`per_received` (+ returns), then `set_subcontracting_order_status()` (controller, 1232–1241) refreshes SCO status; 3. **`set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()`** (controller, 1128–1142) → recomputes consumed materials and `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()` (1110–1126) writes **`consumed_qty` back onto `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`** — closing the SCO-side tracking loop; 4. serial/batch bundles (`make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields`), stock reservation updates; 5. `update_stock_ledger()` (1181–1221): SLEs for FG receipt into `set_warehouse` (rejected qty to `rejected_warehouse`) plus **`make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse()`** (1163–1179), which issues the consumed RM **out of `supplier_warehouse`** at negative `actual_qty` (reversing the earlier transfer); 6. `make_gl_entries()` → **`SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer`** (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`); `repost_future_sle_and_gle`; `update_status()`; 7. `auto_create_purchase_receipt()` → `make_purchase_receipt` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py` (billing the service), `update_job_card()`. `on_cancel()` (192–210) mirrors all of this. ## Stage 6 — Returning leftover material **`get_materials_from_supplier()`** (whitelisted, controller lines 1536–1557): re-computes `get_available_materials()` and calls `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract()` (1489–1533) + `add_items_in_ste()` (1469–1486) to build a return Stock Entry (purpose `Material Transfer`, `is_return`) moving un-consumed RM from `supplier_warehouse` back to the company warehouse — these returns are the rows netted in `__get_transferred_items()` and `get_supplied_items()`. ## Key settings (`Buying Settings`) `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on` ("BOM" vs "Material Transferred for Subcontract"), `over_transfer_allowance`, `validate_consumed_qty`, `auto_create_purchase_receipt` — read in `onload`/`validate_subcontract_order`/`validate_bom_required_qty`/`get_secondary_items` respectively. **Summary of files:** `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` (shared engine: mapping, backflush, consumption reconciliation, cost helpers), `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` (order + RM list + SCR mapper), `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` + `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` (transfer + supplied-qty sync), `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py` + `.../services/gl_composer.py` + `.../mapper.py` (receipt, roll-up, GL, billing), and `erpnext/buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred/` (pending-transfer report).

I've traced the full flow. Here's the complete answer. ## Overview The core files are: - `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py` (class `LandedCostVoucher` + helpers `get_pr_items`, `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount`, `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`) - `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py` (`update_valuation_rate`, `update_stock_ledger`, `validate`) - `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` (`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer`) - `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py` + `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py` (SLE cancel/repost machinery) - `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py` + `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py` (GL cancel/reverse) ## 1. Redistributing charges across PR line items 1. **`LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()`** (landed_cost_voucher.py:59, triggered by the "Get Items from Purchase Receipts" button wired in `landed_cost_voucher.js`) calls **`get_pr_items()`** (:426), which joins the `Purchase Receipt Item` table against `Item` and pulls only stock/fixed-asset rows, appending one `Landed Cost Item` child row per PR item, carrying `receipt_document`, `purchase_receipt_item` (the exact PR child-row name), qty, rate and amount. 2. **`LandedCostVoucher.set_applicable_charges_on_item()`** (:207) does the pro-rata split: with `distribute_charges_based_on` = "Qty" or "Amount", `based_on_field = frappe.scrub(...)` and each row gets `applicable_charges = item[based_on_field] × (total_taxes_and_charges / Σ item costs)`, with the rounding remainder added to the last row. If set to "Distribute Manually", the user fills `applicable_charges` per row, and **`validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`** (:237, called from `on_submit`) enforces Σ charges == `total_taxes_and_charges` within field precision (auto-adjusting the last row for rounding). 3. `validate_receipt_documents()` (:124) guarantees the referenced PRs are already **submitted (docstatus 1)** and belong to the same company — this is what makes "retroactive" possible. ## 2. Retroactive update of a submitted PR — `on_submit` → `update_landed_cost()` (:311) For each row in `purchase_receipts`: **a. Push the LCV amount onto the submitted PR's rows.** - **`set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`** (:532) sums `applicable_charges` from all submitted `Landed Cost Item` rows matching `receipt_document == doc.name` and `purchase_receipt_item == d.name`, writing `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` (and back-filling `cost_center` via `db_set`). - **`doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`** — `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` (buying_controller.py:414) recomputes each item's rate as `(net_rate + item_tax_amount + flt(landed_cost_voucher_amount) + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom` (:481‑486). So the freight/customs charge is baked into the PR's valuation rate. - Each row is persisted directly with **`item.db_update()`** (:329-330) — no parent re-save, so the already-submitted PR's child rows get the new `valuation_rate` and `landed_cost_voucher_amount` in-place. (`BuyingController.validate` also calls `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(self)` at buying_controller.py:66 so the amounts survive later re-saves.) **b. Simulate cancel-then-resubmit of the PR (in-memory docstatus flip) — second loop (:340-355).** The PR is never actually cancelled in the DB; the LCV sets `doc.docstatus = 2`, replays the cancellation effects, then sets `doc.docstatus = 1` and replays submission: - **Cancel leg:** - `doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` → `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` (buying_controller.py:754); since docstatus==2, `StockLedgerService.get_sl_entries` marks the dicts `is_cancelled=1` (stock_ledger_service.py:99), and `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py: make_sl_entries` (:104) calls **`set_as_cancel()`** (stock_ledger.py:241) to flag the PR's old SLEs as cancelled and post reversal entries. `repost_current_voucher` skips re-valuation of the cancelled pass (`if not (args.get("is_cancelled") and via_landed_cost_voucher)`, stock_ledger.py:177). Here's the complete answer. ## Overview The whole mechanism lives in **`erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`** (the `LandedCostVoucher` class plus module-level helpers `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` and `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`), and works by *re-writing history* of the already-submitted Purchase Receipt: it stamps the distributed charges onto the PR's item rows, then temporarily flips the PR's `docstatus` to cancelled and re-submits it in-memory so the Stock Ledger Entries and GL Entries are regenerated with the new valuation. ## 1. Distributing charges across PR line items - **`LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()`** (line 59, whitelisted, triggered by the "Get Items from Purchase Receipts" button in `landed_cost_voucher.js:47`) calls the module-level **`get_pr_items(purchase_receipt)`** (line 426), which queries `Purchase Receipt Item` joined with `Item` for rows where `is_stock_item = 1 OR is_fixed_asset = 1`. Each row becomes a **`Landed Cost Item`** child storing `item_code`, `qty`, `rate`, `amount` (`base_amount`), `cost_center`, and the exact row reference `purchase_receipt_item` (= the PR Item row `name`). Only *submitted* receipts of the same company are allowed (**`validate_receipt_documents`**, line 124; Purchase Invoices must have `update_stock` enabled). - The charge rows go into the `taxes` table; **`set_total_taxes_and_charges`** (line 204) sums their `base_amount`. - **`LandedCostVoucher.set_applicable_charges_on_item()`** (line 207) does the proportional split: for `distribute_charges_based_on` = `"Qty"` or `"Amount"` (everything except `"Distribute Manually"`), each item gets `applicable_charges = item[qty|amount] × total_taxes_and_charges ÷ Σ item[qty|amount]`, and any rounding remainder is dumped on the **last row** (lines 233–235). The client-side mirror is `set_applicable_charges_for_item` in **`landed_cost_voucher.js`** (lines 75–106). Taxes/totals are first normalized by **`init_landed_taxes_and_totals`** (imported from `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py`). - At submit, **`validate_applicable_charges_for_item`** (line 237) asserts `Σ applicable_charges == total_taxes_and_charges` (within field precision, adjusting the last row) — otherwise it throws. ## 2. Pushing the charges into the submitted PR (`on_submit` → `update_landed_cost`) `on_submit` (line 294) runs `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` → **`update_landed_cost()`** (line 312) → `update_claimed_landed_cost()`. `on_cancel` (line 299) re-runs `update_landed_cost()` — since `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` only sums `docstatus == 1` LCV rows, cancelling an LCV automatically removes its amount. In the first loop of `update_landed_cost`, per receipt document: 1. **`set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`** (line 532): for *each PR Item row*, sums `applicable_charges` of all submitted `Landed Cost Item` rows matching `purchase_receipt_item == row.name` into the PR item's `landed_cost_voucher_amount` field (so multiple LCVs against one PR accumulate). It also back-fills the item's `cost_center`. 2. **`doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`** — `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` in **`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`** (line 414) recomputes each item's valuation rate as `(base_net_rate + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom` (lines 481–486). 3. **`item.db_update()`** (lines 329–330): the changed `landed_cost_voucher_amount` / `valuation_rate` are persisted straight to the database **without touching the submitted PR's docstatus**. 4. For serialized non-asset items, **`update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items`** (line 395) rewrites `Serial No.purchase_rate` to the new valuation rate; for fixed assets, `doc.update_assets()` (`purchase_receipt.py:499`) rewrites `net_purchase_amount`/`purchase_amount`. ## 3. Retroactively re-posting Stock Ledger Entries Second loop of `update_landed_cost` (lines 340–355) — the PR document object is mutated in memory, never re-saved as cancelled: - `doc.docstatus = 2` → **`doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`buying_controller.py:754`) posts the *reversal* SLEs, then **`doc.make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`** (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:281`) reverses the original GL entries. - `doc.docstatus = 1` → **`make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** re-attaches the existing Serial/Batch bundles (so `get_package_for_target_warehouse` reuses them instead of creating duplicates, `buying_controller.py:895`), then `update_stock_ledger(...)` again posts **fresh SLEs** with `incoming_rate = d.valuation_rate` (line 833) — i.e., the rate that now includes the LCV amount. - The `via_landed_cost_voucher` flag threads through `StockController.make_sl_entries` → `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:204`) → `make_sl_entries` / `make_entry` in **`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`** (lines 104, 252), which sets `sle.via_landed_cost_voucher`. Its purposes: - **`repost_current_voucher`** (line 172) skips running the full valuation engine on the *cancelled* SLE (`if not (args.get("is_cancelled") and via_landed_cost_voucher)`, line 177) — the −ve LCV SLE only shifts future balances via `update_qty_in_future_sle` and is balanced by the +ve reposted SLE. - **`update_entries_after`** (`stock_ledger.py:572`, constructor takes `via_landed_cost_voucher=True`) relaxes validations during the repost (e.g., skipping the serialized negative-stock raise at line 1022, and `allow_negative_stock=True`). - Because the SLE is posted with `recalculate_rate = 1`, **`update_entries_after.get_dynamic_incoming_outgoing_rate`** (line 1372) re-pulls the incoming rate from the source document via `get_incoming_outgoing_rate_from_transaction` (line 1395), which for a non-return Purchase Receipt reads `valuation_rate` from the `Purchase Receipt Item` row (lines 1473–1487) — that's how the new LCV-inclusive rate propagates into FIFO/moving-average valuation. (For internal-transfer receipts, `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer` at line 2540 explicitly adds `landed_cost_voucher_amount ÷ qty` to the mirrored incoming rate.) ## 4. Retroactively re-posting GL Entries **`doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** → `StockController.make_gl_entries` (`stock_controller.py:178`) → `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries(...)` (`purchase_receipt.py:478`) → **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose`** in **`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`** (line 23). In `_make_item_gl_entries` (line 39): - The stock account is debited with the *new, larger* `stock_value_diff` (read live from the reposted SLE via **`get_stock_value_difference`**, `purchase_receipt.py:544`), while the Stock Received But Not Billed credit is unchanged — the supplier side of the original receipt must not move. - The LCV portion is booked by the nested **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries(item)`** (line 166): it credits each LCV tax row's `expense_account` (freight/customs account) with that item's share, against the stock account. The per-item, per-account amounts come from **`doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()`** (`stock_controller.py:267`, delegating to the LCV module's **`get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)`**, line 562): it loads every submitted LCV touching the PR and, per item row × expense account, accumulates `account.base_amount × item[based_on] / total_item_cost` (falling back to `item.applicable_charges` for manually-distributed LCVs). Net effect: the freight/customs expense is capitalized into inventory value, and the debit/credit stays balanced. - The same composer is reused by Purchase Invoice (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/gl_composer.py:140`), Stock Entry and Subcontracting Receipt composers, since LCVs also target those doctypes. ## 5. Ripple-forward to later transactions Finally, **`doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`stock_controller.py:360` → `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `stock_ledger_service.py:219`) creates **`Repost Item Valuation`** documents (or, with `item_based_reposting` enabled, item-warehouse pairs via **`create_item_wise_repost_entries`**, `stock_controller.py:820`) so every SLE/GL posting *after* the PR's timestamp is revalued with the new incoming rate. A backdated LCV therefore cascades through deliveries, transfers and consumption that happened after the original receipt (see `TestPurchaseReceipt.test_purchase_receipt_with_backdated_landed_cost_voucher` and `test_valuation_taxes_lcv_repost_after_billing` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/test_purchase_receipt.py`). ## Key files/functions summary | Concern | File | Function(s) | |---|---|---| | Item pull & distribution | `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py` | `get_items_from_purchase_receipts`, `get_pr_items`, `set_applicable_charges_on_item`, `validate_applicable_charges_for_item` | | Client mirror | `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.js` | `get_items_from_purchase_receipts`, `set_applicable_charges_for_item` | | Stamp + repost engine | same `.py` | `on_submit`, `on_cancel`, `update_landed_cost`, `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount`, `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries` | | Valuation rate | `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py` | `update_valuation_rate`, `update_stock_ledger` | | SLE reposting | `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py` | `make_sl_entries`, `make_entry`, `repost_current_voucher`, `update_entries_after`, `get_dynamic_incoming_outgoing_rate`, `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer` | | GL reposting | `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` | `make_gl_entries`, `make_gl_entries_on_cancel`, `repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`; `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose/_make_item_gl_entries/make_landed_cost_gl_entries` | | Orchestration from PR | `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py` | `get_gl_entries`, `get_stock_value_difference`, `make_lcv` (whitelisted helper that pre-fills an LCV from a PR) |

I now have the full picture. Here's the complete answer. ## Overview The whole mechanism lives in **`erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`** (class `LandedCostVoucher`), with the receiving side in **`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`**, **`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`**, **`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`**, and **`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`**. ## 1. Pulling PR line items into the LCV - `LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` (L59) loops over the `purchase_receipts` child table (`LandedCostPurchaseReceipt` rows pointing at a submitted Purchase Receipt / Purchase Invoice w/ Update Stock / Stock Entry / Subcontracting Receipt) and calls the module-level helper **`get_pr_items(purchase_receipt)`** (L426) — a querybuilder join of `<DocType> Item` with `Item` filtered to `is_stock_item = 1 OR is_fixed_asset = 1`. Each stock/asset line becomes a **`Landed Cost Item`** child row storing `item_code`, `qty`, `base_rate`/`base_amount`, and crucially the child-row link `purchase_receipt_item` (the `Purchase Receipt Item.name`). - Validation (`validate()`, L82) via `validate_receipt_documents()` enforces the receipt must be **docstatus 1 (already submitted)** and belong to the same company — this is what makes the LCV purely retroactive. ## 2. Distributing the charges across items - Charges are entered in the `taxes` table (`LandedCostTaxesandCharges`, each with an `expense_account`, `amount`, `exchange_rate`); totals come from `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` (L204) plus **`init_landed_taxes_and_totals`** imported from `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py` (L1341). - **`set_applicable_charges_on_item()`** (L207) does the proration: for `distribute_charges_based_on` = `"Qty"` or `"Amount"` (scrubbed to `based_on_field`), each item gets `applicable_charges = item.get(based_on_field) × total_taxes_and_charges / Σ item costs`, and the rounding remainder is dumped on the last row (L233–235). `"Distribute Manually"` leaves user-entered values untouched. - **`validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`** (L237, called from `on_submit`) re-checks that Σ `applicable_charges` equals `total_taxes_and_charges` to field precision, nudging the last row by the rounding diff or throwing. - Vendor freight bills can be pulled via `get_vendor_invoice_amount()` / `get_vendor_invoices()` / `get_vendor_invoice_query()` (L407–529), which compute each non-stock Purchase Invoice's `unclaimed_amount = base_total − claimed_landed_cost_amount`; on submit **`update_claimed_landed_cost()`** (L303) stamps `claimed_landed_cost_amount` back onto those PIs (zeroed on cancel). ## 3. Retroactively updating the submitted Purchase Receipt **`LandedCostVoucher.on_submit()`** (L294) → **`update_landed_cost()`** (L312). For every row in `purchase_receipts`: **Phase A — rewrite item valuation in place:** 1. `validate_asset_qty_and_status()` (L357) — fixed-asset guard (all linked Assets must be draft and cover the qty). 2. Module-level **`set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`** (L532): for each `Purchase Receipt Item`, it sums `applicable_charges` of **all submitted `Landed Cost Item` rows matching that `purchase_receipt_item` across every LCV**, and writes it into `Purchase Receipt Item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` (backfilling `cost_center` via `db_set`). This is the join that makes an old PR inherit the new charge. 3. **`doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`** — `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py` (L414). The key formula (L481–486): `valuation_rate = (base_net_rate + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom` — the LCV amount is stacked **on top of** the PR's own taxes. (For Subcontracting Receipt, `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` is used instead, adding `lcv_cost_per_qty = landed_cost_voucher_amount / qty` — `subcontracting_receipt.py` L537.) 4. **`item.db_update()`** per row (L329–330) persists `landed_cost_voucher_amount` and `valuation_rate` straight into the DB — the PR stays submitted, no full save. Note the same `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` is also invoked from `BuyingController.validate()` (L66), so any later re-validation of the PR keeps it in sync. 5. `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` (L395) pushes the new `valuation_rate` into `Serial No.purchase_rate` for serialised, non-asset items. **Phase B — simulate cancel + resubmit of the receipt's ledgers (L340–355):** - `doc.docstatus = 2` (temporary): `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` cancels the old Stock Ledger Entries, and `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` (`StockController`, `stock_controller.py` L281) reverses the old GL entries. The `via_landed_cost_voucher` flag bypasses negative-stock and serial-no checks during this synthetic cancel (`stock_ledger.py` L177, L1022). - `doc.docstatus = 1` again: `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` (reuses the existing serial/batch bundles instead of creating new ones — `serial_batch_bundle_service.py` L186–213), then `update_stock_ledger(...)` re-posts SLEs with **`incoming_rate = d.valuation_rate`** (`buying_controller.py` L833) — now including the LCV amount. - **`doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** → `StockController.make_gl_entries` (L178) → `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries` (`purchase_receipt.py` L478) → **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose`** (`gl_composer.py` L23). Inside `_make_item_gl_entries`: - the warehouse/asset account is debited with `stock_value_diff` (from `get_stock_value_difference`, i.e., the SLE-derived stock value that now includes the LCV amount) against *Stock Received But Not Billed* for the invoice value; - **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries(item)`** (L166) then **credits each LCV `expense_account`** with the item's share and debits the stock account — so the capitalised freight/customs is funded by the LCV expense account, not SRNB. The per-item, per-account split comes from **`get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)`** (landed_cost_voucher.py L562): it finds all submitted `Landed Cost Purchase Receipt` rows for the doc, loads each parent LCV, and prorates each tax row's `amount`/`base_amount` by the same `based_on_field` (falling back to `applicable_charges` for manual distribution / zero totals). Fixed assets additionally trigger `doc.update_assets(d, d.valuation_rate)` (L343–344). - **`doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`stock_controller.py` L360 → `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py` L219) queues `Repost Item Valuation` docs with `via_landed_cost_voucher = 1`, so all downstream SLEs (Stock Entries, Delivery Notes, Sales Invoices…) and their GL entries are re-valued with the new rates. For internal transfers the new incoming rate also adds the LCV share via `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer()` (`stock_ledger.py` L2540, reads `landed_cost_voucher_amount` from the voucher detail row at L2561). **Cancellation** is symmetric: `on_cancel` (L299) re-runs `update_landed_cost()`; since the cancelled LCV's rows no longer match the `docstatus == 1` filter in `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount`, the items' `landed_cost_voucher_amount` collapses to 0 and the SLE/GL repost restores the original valuation. **Guard helper:** `has_landed_cost_amount()` (L554) short-circuits the LCV GL lookup when no item carries an amount. The same `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries` plumbing (exposed via `StockController.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`, L267) is reused by the Purchase Invoice, Stock Entry, and Subcontracting Receipt GL composers, so LCV costs flow identically into those voucher types' accounting.

I now have the full picture. Here's the complete flow: # Landed Cost Voucher (LCV): distribution + retroactive reposting ## 1. How charges are distributed across receipt line items **File: `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`** 1. **Pulling receipt lines** — `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:59`, the *Get Items from Purchase Receipts* button) iterates the `purchase_receipts` child table and calls `get_pr_items(pr)` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:426`), a pypika query joining the receipt-item table (`Purchase Receipt Item` / `Purchase Invoice Item` / `Stock Entry Detail` / `Subcontracting Receipt Item`) with `Item`, filtered to `is_stock_item=1 OR is_fixed_asset=1`. One `Landed Cost Item` child row is appended per receipt line, storing `receipt_document_type`, `receipt_document`, `rate`, `amount`, and — critically — the child-row link `purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item`), which is the anchor for all later updates. 2. **Tax rows** — the `taxes` table (`Landed Cost Taxes and Charges` child, `expense_account` + `amount`, e.g. freight/customs). `init_landed_taxes_and_totals(self)` (class at `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py:1341`) sets account currency/exchange rate and computes `base_amount`; `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:204`) sums `base_amount` into `total_taxes_and_charges`. 3. **Apportionment** — `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:207`): unless *Distribute Manually* is chosen, `based_on_field = frappe.scrub(self.distribute_charges_based_on)` (e.g. `qty`, `amount`, `gross_profit`); each row's `applicable_charges = item[based_on_field] × total_taxes_and_charges / Σ item[based_on_field]`, with any rounding remainder dumped on the last row (lines 233–235). In manual mode the user fills `applicable_charges` directly. 4. **Enforcement at submit** — `on_submit()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:294`) calls `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:237`): total `applicable_charges` must equal `total_taxes_and_charges` within field precision (last row absorbs sub-precision diffs), otherwise it throws. Then it calls `update_landed_cost()` and `update_claimed_landed_cost()` (marks `claimed_landed_cost_amount` on the vendor invoices). ## 2. Retroactive update of already-submitted receipts **`update_landed_cost()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:312`)** — this is the heart of the retroactivity. It loops the referenced receipts **twice**, never calling `save()`/`validate()` — it mutates fields in place and toggles `docstatus` *in memory* to force cancel/repost behavior: **Pass 1 — revalue the receipt items:** - `validate_asset_qty_and_status()` (line 357) blocks if submitted Assets exist. - `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` (module function, `landed_cost_voucher.py:532`): for each item row, queries `SUM(applicable_charges)` from **all submitted** `Landed Cost Item` rows matching `receipt_document` + `purchase_receipt_item`, and writes it onto `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` (also back-fills `cost_center`). Because it's a SUM over submitted LCVs, multiple LCVs accumulate correctly. - For Purchase Receipts: `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` — **`BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:414`)** recomputes: ``` valuation_rate = (net_rate + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom ``` (lines 481–486) — i.e., the distributed LCV amount is folded straight into the valuation rate. - Each modified row is persisted individually via `item.db_update()` (lines 329–330), avoiding a full document save/validation. For serial items, `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` (line 395) rewrites `Serial No.purchase_rate`. **Pass 2 — reverse and re-post both ledgers** (the doc object is reused with `docstatus` flipped): - **`doc.docstatus = 2` (simulated cancel):** `doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` — `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` (`buying_controller.py:754`) builds reversal SL entries with `recalculate_rate`; the flag threads through `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:204`) into `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py: make_sl_entries/make_entry/repost_current_voucher` (`make_entry` sets `sle.via_landed_cost_voucher`, line 257; it also relaxes validations such as the negative-stock check for serials at line 1022). Then `doc.make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:281`) reverses the old GL entries. - **`doc.docstatus = 1` (simulated re-submit):** `doc.make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` (`stock_controller.py:207`) rebuilds Serial/Batch bundles reusing the original serial/batch fields; `update_stock_ledger(...)` runs again, now posting SLEs with the **new `valuation_rate` as `incoming_rate`** (line 833). - **`doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`StockController.make_gl_entries`, `stock_controller.py:178`) → for a Purchase Receipt, `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()` (**`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py:23`**), whose `_make_item_gl_entries()`: - debits the stock/asset account with `stock_value_diff` from `get_stock_value_difference()` — the *actual* stock-ledger delta, now reflecting the new rate (fixed assets: `base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount`, lines 303–307); - **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries()`** (line 166) consumes `doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` (`stock_controller.py:267` → **`get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` in `landed_cost_voucher.py:562`**), which maps each LCV item row to `{expense_account: amount}` by splitting each LCV tax row's `amount` across items using the LCV's own `distribute_charges_based_on` basis — and **credits each LCV expense account** against "Stock Received But Not Billed", so the capitalized freight/customs cost hits the correct expense account per item; - `make_expenses_added_to_stock_entries()` (line 194) books the LCV amount into "Expenses Included in Valuation"-style accounts when enabled; - `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry()` (line 233) books any gap between the document valuation (incl. LCV amount) and the actual stock-value diff to the divisional-loss / purchase-price-variance account. - **`doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`stock_controller.py:360` → `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `stock_ledger_service.py:219`): if `future_sle_exists()` (i.e., later transfers/deliveries/sales consumed this stock), it queues a **Repost Item Valuation** document (`erpnext/stock/doctype/repost_item_valuation/repost_item_valuation.py`, which even has a `via_landed_cost_voucher` field) via `create_repost_item_valuation_entry` / `create_item_wise_repost_entries` (`stock_controller.py:~815–853`), cascading the corrected valuation rate and GL entries forward through all subsequent vouchers. `on_cancel()` of the LCV simply calls `update_landed_cost()` + `update_claimed_landed_cost()` again (lines 299–301) — since `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` sums only `docstatus=1` LCV rows, cancelling one LCV automatically removes its share and re-reposts the receipts. **Key design point:** the receipt document is never saved/re-validated — only targeted `db_update`/`db_set` writes plus in-memory `docstatus` toggling — which is how an LCV can modify an already-submitted Purchase Receipt's valuation (`landed_cost_voucher_amount`, `valuation_rate`), its Stock Ledger Entries, and its GL entries after the fact, while `validate_receipt_documents()` (line 124) guarantees only *submitted* receipts can be referenced.

final answer
## Mechanism: the `methods` parameter of `@frappe.whitelist()` In ERPNext, a Python function becomes an HTTP endpoint (`/api/method/<dotted.path>`) only when it is decorated with `@frappe.whitelist()`. By default (bare `@frappe.whitelist()`, used ~726 times in this repo) the endpoint is reachable with any HTTP method, including GET. State‑changing endpoints therefore **opt in to POST‑only access by passing `methods=["POST"]` to the decorator**: ```python @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"]) def some_mutating_endpoint(...): ... ``` How the restriction is enforced: 1. **Declaration (erpnext side):** `frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` records the allowed HTTP verbs on the decorated function object (the decorator stores them as attributes on the function, e.g. its `http_methods`). ERPNext itself never inspects `frappe.request.method` — I verified there is no such check anywhere in the repo's Python code. 2. **Enforcement (Frappe framework side, upstream of this repo):** when a request arrives, Frappe's dispatcher (`frappe.handler.execute_cmd` → `frappe.handler.is_whitelisted`) resolves the command to the function, then validates the incoming request's HTTP method against the methods declared on the whitelisted function **before** calling it. A `GET /api/method/...` targeting a POST-only endpoint is rejected with a "method not allowed"-type error and the function body never runs. So a CSRF-style link/image tag, browser prefetch, or any GET navigation cannot trigger document creation/submission. 3. **Read endpoints are deliberately different:** pure queries either stay bare (`@frappe.whitelist()`) or explicitly declare `methods=["GET"]` — e.g. `get_older_unreconciled_transactions` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py:388`. Every restricted endpoint in the codebase uses exactly `["POST"]`; there are no multi-verb declarations (`["PUT"]`, `["DELETE"]`, mixed lists) anywhere. The pattern is widely applied: **73 `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` declarations across 43 files**. ## Concrete POST-only endpoints (with files) | Endpoint (function) | File : line | What it mutates | |---|---|---| | `make_quality_inspections` | `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:658` | Creates Quality Inspection documents | | `update_company_master_and_address` | `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:1654` | Updates Company doc + Address (checks write permission) | | `make_purchase_receipt` | `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py:25` | Creates, and optionally **saves/submits**, a Purchase Receipt (`save=True, submit=True` args) | | `create_supplier_quotation` | `erpnext/buying/doctype/request_for_quotation/mapper.py:58` | Creates a Supplier Quotation from the supplier portal | | `set_work_order_ops` | `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py:1083` | `frappe.get_doc("Work Order", ...)` → `set_work_order_operations()` → `po.save()` | | `add_node` | `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py:1012` | Inserts a new Company tree node | | `make_work_orders` | `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py:843` | Creates Work Orders against a Sales Order | | `update_bank_transaction` | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py:119` | Edits and saves a Bank Transaction (one of 9 POST-only endpoints in that file) | | `mark_issues_as_resolved`-style mutators, e.g. `issue.py:276` | `erpnext/support/doctype/issue/issue.py` | Mutates Issue docs | A guest-accessible example showing the two flags combined: `get_context_for_dev` in `erpnext/www/banking.py:32` — `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"], allow_guest=True)`. ## Summary The restriction is declarative, not procedural: ERPNext marks every endpoint that creates/saves/submits documents with `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])`, and the Frappe framework's request handler refuses any GET request to such functions before execution (returning a 405-style error). GET remains reserved for side-effect-free reads, which are either undecorated-method-wise (`@frappe.whitelist()`) or explicitly `methods=["GET"]`.
