## The mechanism: `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` ERPNext exposes server functions over HTTP by decorating them with `@frappe.whitelist()`. By default a whitelisted function accepts **all** standard HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). For any endpoint that mutates data, the code passes a `methods` argument to the decorator, e.g.: ```python @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"]) def make_work_orders(items, sales_order, company, project=None): """Make Work Orders against the given Sales Order for the given items""" ``` This is the repo-wide convention for state-changing endpoints — 73 such decorators across 43 files, and in every case in this codebase the value is exactly `["POST"]` (there are no multi-verb variants; a handful of strictly read-only endpoints instead declare `methods=["GET"]` for symmetry). ### How the restriction is enforced The enforcement lives in the **Frappe framework** (the `frappe` package dependency, not vendored in this repo): 1. The `frappe.whitelist` decorator marks the function as HTTP-accessible (`fn.is_whitelisted`, `fn.allow_guest`) and stores the permitted HTTP verbs on the function object. 2. Every request to `/api/method/<dotted.path>` (or desk `frappe.call` targets) goes through `frappe.handler.execute_cmd`, which resolves the command to the function, runs auth/guest checks (`is_whitelisted`), and then validates the incoming request method (`frappe.local.request_method`) against the function's allowed-verb list before invoking it. 3. A `GET` request to a POST-only endpoint therefore **never reaches the function body** — the dispatcher aborts with an "Method Not Allowed" (HTTP 405) error. This complements CSRF protection: Frappe validates CSRF tokens only on non-GET requests, so a mutating endpoint reachable via GET would be CSRF-exploitable (GETs can be fired cross-origin from links/`<img>` tags with no token). Pinning writers to POST keeps them on the CSRF-protected channel, while the desk client is unaffected because `frappe.call`/`frappe.xcall` in JS always uses POST. ### Concrete POST-restricted endpoints | Endpoint | File (line) | What it does | |---|---|---| | `make_work_orders` | `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py:843` | Creates Work Orders from a Sales Order | | `create_supplier_quotation` | `erpnext/buying/doctype/request_for_quotation/mapper.py:58` | Creates a Supplier Quotation from an RFQ | | `raise_work_orders` | `erpnext/stock/doctype/material_request/material_request.py:514` | Creates Work Orders from a Material Request | | `update_bank_transaction`, `create_journal_entry_bts`, `create_payment_entry_bts`, `create_internal_transfer`, `create_bulk_internal_transfer`, `create_bank_entry_and_reconcile`, `reconcile_vouchers`, … (10 total) | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py` (lines 119, 149, 308, 503, 459, 673, 1060, …) | Updates/creates/reconciles bank transactions, JEs, payment entries | | `make_payment_request` | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py:722` | Creates a Payment Request | | `create_payment_entries` | `erpnext/accounts/bulk_payment.py:12` | Bulk-creates payment entries against invoices | | `create_user` | `erpnext/setup/doctype/employee/employee.py:435` | Creates a User record for an Employee | | `create_transaction_deletion_request` | `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py:1123` | Queues bulk deletion of a company's transactions | | `make_quality_inspections` | `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:658` | Creates Quality Inspections for stock documents | | `create_opening_voucher` / `set_customer_info` | `erpnext/selling/page/point_of_sale/point_of_sale.py:350` / `:441` | POS opening cash voucher; customer edits | | `split_batch` | `erpnext/stock/doctype/batch/batch.py:304` | Splits a stock batch | | `set_work_order_ops` | `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py:1083` | Rewrites Work Order operations | | `set_multiple_status` (Task / Opportunity) | `erpnext/projects/doctype/task/task.py:372`, `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/opportunity.py:392` | Bulk status changes | | `build_tree`, `bisect_left`, `bisect_right`, `move_up` | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bisect_accounting_statements/bisect_accounting_statements.py` (124, 187, 201, 215) | Delete/insert "Bisect Nodes" during statement bisection | Note the instructive contrast in `bank_reconciliation_tool.py`: purely read-side helpers `get_older_unreconciled_transactions` (line 388) and `search_for_transfer_transaction` (line 900) are declared `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["GET"])`, while every sibling that inserts or reconciles vouchers is `methods=["POST"]` — showing the convention is deliberately applied per-endpoint based on side effects.

## The mechanism ERPNext (pinned to `frappe >=17.0.0-dev,<18.0.0` in `pyproject.toml`) exposes Python functions over HTTP through the Frappe framework's `@frappe.whitelist()` decorator — those functions become callable as `/api/method/<dotted.path>` (and via the newer `/api/v2` routes and `frappe.call` from the desk). By default a whitelisted function accepts **both GET and POST**. The restriction is declared **in the decorator itself**: the `methods` argument of `frappe.whitelist()`. A state-changing endpoint declares `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` (optionally combined with `allow_guest=True`). When a request arrives, Frappe's dispatcher that resolves the `cmd` (i.e. `frappe.handler.execute_cmd` → `frappe.get_attr(cmd)` → `frappe.is_whitelisted(...)`) records the allowed verbs at module-load time from the decorator and compares them against the incoming `frappe.request.method`; a GET against a POST-only endpoint is rejected with **HTTP 405 (Method Not Allowed)** before the function body runs. Notably, ERPNext contributes **no manual checks of its own** — a grep for `frappe.request.method` across `erpnext/**` returns zero matches — so the decorator declaration is the sole, declarative mechanism. The convention is applied symmetrically: pure-read endpoints are pinned the other way, e.g. `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["GET"])` on `get_older_unreconciled_transactions` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py:388`), `search_for_transfer_transaction` (same file, :900), `get_list` / `get_closing_balance_as_per_statement` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_account/bank_account.py:140,181`), and `get_statement_details` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_statement_import_log/bank_statement_import_log.py:1125`). Scale: **73 occurrences of `frappe.whitelist(methods=...)` across 43 files.** ## Concrete POST-restricted, state-changing endpoints **Bank reconciliation / payments (the heaviest concentration — 12 in one file):** `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py` - `update_bank_transaction` (:119), `create_journal_entry_bts` (:149), `create_payment_entry_bts` (:308), `create_bulk_internal_transfer` (:459), `create_internal_transfer` (:503), `create_bulk_bank_entry_and_reconcile` (:580), `create_bank_entry_and_reconcile` (:673), `create_bulk_payment_entry_and_reconcile` (:771), `create_payment_entry_and_reconcile` (:867), `reconcile_vouchers` (:1060) — all create/cancel Payment or Journal Entries and mutate the Bank Transaction. **Document creation (mapper-style endpoints):** - `make_work_orders` — `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py:843` (creates Work Orders from a Sales Order) - `raise_work_orders` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/material_request/material_request.py:514` - `make_quality_inspections` — `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:658` - `make_payment_request` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py:722` - `create_bank_entries` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_transaction/bank_transaction_upload.py:37` - `unreconcile_transaction_entry` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_transaction/bank_transaction.py:400` - `create_payment_entries` — `erpnext/accounts/bulk_payment.py:12` - `make_lead_from_communication` — `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/mapper.py:113`; `make_opportunity_from_communication` — `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/mapper.py:127`; `make_issue_from_communication` — `erpnext/support/doctype/issue/issue.py:276` **Document mutation / admin actions:** - `revise_budget` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py:881` - `create_user` — `erpnext/setup/doctype/employee/employee.py:435` (creates a User for an Employee) - `create_transaction_deletion_request` — `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py:1123`; `add_node` — same file :1012 - `split_batch` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/batch/batch.py:304` - `update_company_master_and_address` — `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:1654` - `create_opening_voucher` and `set_customer_info` — `erpnext/selling/page/point_of_sale/point_of_sale.py:350,441` - Tree `add_node` endpoints: `erpnext/stock/doctype/warehouse/warehouse.py:194`, `erpnext/setup/doctype/department/department.py:98`, `erpnext/assets/doctype/location/location.py:227`, `erpnext/projects/doctype/task/task.py:455` (also `add_multiple_tasks`, task.py:468) - Status setters: `set_multiple_status` — `erpnext/projects/doctype/task/task.py:372` and `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/opportunity.py:392`; `set_project_status` — `erpnext/projects/doctype/project/project.py:812` - Whitelisted **docmethods** work identically: `start_job` / `complete_job` — `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/workstation/workstation.py:226,236`; `split_issue` — `erpnext/support/doctype/issue/issue.py:120`; `get_customer_group_details` — `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:206`; `insert_transactions` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_statement_import_log/bank_statement_import_log.py:489` **Guest-accessible POST endpoints** (anonymous users can never mutate via GET): `get_context_for_dev` — `erpnext/www/banking.py:32` (`methods=["POST"], allow_guest=True`), and `send_message` — `erpnext/templates/utils.py:11` (`allow_guest=True, methods=["POST"]`, further hardened with `@rate_limit`). **Summary:** the restriction is a single declarative pattern — `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` — placed on every mutating whitelisted function; Frappe's request dispatcher enforces it by returning 405 for disallowed verbs, so state changes can only be triggered by deliberate POST calls (which the client-side `frappe.call` always uses), never by GET links, prefetches, or crawlers.

final answer
## The mechanism: the `methods=` argument of `frappe.whitelist()` ERPNext doesn't implement this check itself — it's declared entirely through the `frappe.whitelist()` decorator that comes from the Frappe framework (frappe core, `frappe/whitelist.py`). ERPNext's role is purely declarative: ```python @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"]) # HTTP verb allow-list def make_quality_inspections(...): ``` How it works: - **Bare `@frappe.whitelist()`** registers the function so it can be invoked over *any* of GET, POST, PUT, DELETE via the `/api/method/<dotted.path>` RPC route. - **`@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])`** narrows that registration to only the listed verbs. The framework's HTTP dispatch layer (the RPC handler that resolves the dotted path and executes it) compares the incoming request's HTTP method against the allow-list registered by the decorator and **refuses to execute the function** when the verb doesn't match — so a GET request to a POST-only endpoint is rejected before the function body runs. The same mechanism is also used in reverse: a few explicitly read-only endpoints are locked to `methods=["GET"]`. - This is safe for the desk UI because the JS client (`frappe.call` / `frappe.xcall`) sends its RPCs as POST anyway; the restriction exists to block GET-triggered invocations (which lack POST's CSRF protections, can be fired cross-site via `<img src=...>`-style tags, get URLs cached/logged, etc.). Scale of usage in this codebase: **73 `@frappe.whitelist(methods=...)` decorators across 43 files** (versus ~726 plain `@frappe.whitelist()` for read-only/query endpoints). Every `methods=` usage here is single-verb — `["POST"]` for mutating endpoints, `["GET"]` for a handful of read-only ones; no multi-verb lists are used. ## Concrete POST-only (state-changing) endpoints | Endpoint | File : line | What it mutates | |---|---|---| | `update_company_master_and_address` | `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:1654` | Updates Company master/Address | | `make_quality_inspections` | `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:658` | Creates Quality Inspection docs | | `create_supplier_quotation` | `erpnext/buying/doctype/request_for_quotation/mapper.py:58` | Creates a Supplier Quotation from the supplier portal | | `unreconcile_transaction_entry` | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_transaction/bank_transaction.py:400` | Cancels vouchers / removes payment entries from a Bank Transaction | | `make_work_orders` | `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py:843` | Creates Work Orders from a Sales Order | | `make_purchase_receipt` | `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py:25` | Creates a Purchase Receipt | | `revise_budget` | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py:881` | Revises a Budget document | | `create_user` | `erpnext/setup/doctype/employee/employee.py:435` | Creates a User (+ permission) for an Employee | | `create_transaction_deletion_request` | `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py:1123` | Deletes a company's transaction data | | `create_opening_voucher` | `erpnext/selling/page/point_of_sale/point_of_sale.py:350` | Creates a POS Opening Entry | | `set_project_status` / `set_multiple_status` | `erpnext/projects/doctype/project/project.py:812`, `erpnext/projects/doctype/task/task.py:372`, `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/opportunity.py:392` | Status changes on multiple docs | | `make_issue_from_communication` / `split_issue` / `make_lead_from_communication` / `make_opportunity_from_communication` | `erpnext/support/doctype/issue/issue.py:276` and `:120`, `erpnext/crm/doctype/lead/mapper.py:113`, `erpnext/crm/doctype/opportunity/mapper.py:127` | Creates/splits support & CRM docs | | Bank Reconciliation Tool — nearly all its API | `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py:119, 149, 308, 459, 503, 580, 673, 771, 867, 1060` | Reconciles/unreconciles bank transactions (mutating) | It works on document-class methods too, e.g. `Customer.get_customer_group_details` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:206`), `BisectAccountingStatements.build_tree` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/bisect_accounting_statements/bisect_accounting_statements.py:124` — it deletes "Bisect Nodes" docs), and `StockRepostingSettings.convert_to_item_wh_reposting` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reposting_settings/stock_reposting_settings.py:72`). It can also be combined with guest access, e.g. `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"], allow_guest=True)` on `get_context_for_dev` in `erpnext/www/banking.py:32`. ## The inverse (read-only endpoints pinned to GET) For contrast, explicitly read-only helpers are pinned the other way: - `get_older_unreconciled_transactions` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_reconciliation_tool/bank_reconciliation_tool.py:388` (just a `frappe.db.count`) - `get_list` / `get_bank_accounts` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_account/bank_account.py:140` and `:181` - an import-status checker — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/bank_statement_import_log/bank_statement_import_log.py:1125` **In short:** the restriction is a declarative per-endpoint HTTP-verb allow-list — `@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])` — enforced by the Frappe framework's RPC dispatcher before the endpoint function executes. ERPNext applies it to every whitelisted endpoint that creates, saves, submits or deletes documents (and uses `methods=["GET"]` for the few endpoints that must remain strictly read-only).

final answer
## Summary ERPNext tracks progress per **required item row** (`Work Order Item.transferred_qty`), and the work‑order‑level field `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` is recomputed from those accumulated item-level transfers every time a "Material Transfer for Manufacture" Stock Entry is submitted/cancelled. There are two computation modes depending on whether the transfer entry carries `fg_completed_qty`. ## How the progress is computed **Trigger chain (on Stock Entry submit/cancel):** 1. `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.on_submit()` / `on_cancel()` → `update_job_card_and_work_order()` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py:365-390`. It calls `wo_doc.run_method("update_work_order_qty")` (only when `fg_completed_qty` is set) and always `wo_doc.run_method("update_status")`. 2. `StatusService.update_status()` — `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/status.py:88-105` — first calls `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` (fresh progress for the status decision), then `update_required_items()`. 3. `RequiredItemsService.update_transferred_qty_for_required_items()` — `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py:133-150` — queries **all submitted** Stock Entries with `purpose = "Material Transfer for Manufacture"` against the WO via `_material_transfer_qty_by_item()` (line 201; `SUM(transfer_qty)` grouped by `(item_code, original_item)` so alternative/substitute items are credited to the required item). It `db_set`s each row's `transferred_qty`, then calls `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()`. Because the query re-aggregates *all* submitted transfer entries each time, partial batches simply accumulate row by row. **`recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()`** — `required_items.py:162-194`: - Skipped if `transfer_material_against == "Job Card"` (tracked on the Job Card instead) or `skip_transfer`. - **Classic flow** (`fg_completed_qty > 0` on each transfer entry): field = `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty("Material Transfer for Manufacture", ...)` = `SUM(fg_completed_qty)` of submitted transfer entries (status.py:267-283). - **Pick-list flow** (`fg_completed_qty = 0`, set in `update_stock_entry_based_on_work_order()`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/pick_list/mapper.py:411-420`): computes per-item fraction `transferred_qty / required_qty` for every `include_item_in_manufacturing` row, takes the **minimum fraction across all required items (the bottleneck)**, caps it at 1.0, and sets the field to `min_fraction × wo.qty`. So if item A is fully transferred but item B only half, the WO shows half-progressed, not fully transferred (see `test_material_transferred_min_fraction_on_partial_pick_list`, `test_work_order.py:1492-1527`). Status interplay: `StatusService._has_transferred_material()` (status.py:146) detects pick-list/MR-sourced transfers so the WO still flips from "Not Started" to "In Process" even when the min-fraction keeps the field at 0 (`_submitted_status`, status.py:129). ## What prevents over-transferring 1. **Capped suggested quantities:** - `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.get_items()` → `get_pending_raw_materials()` / `_calculate_item_transfer_qty()` / `_resolve_transfer_qty()` — `material_transfer.py:257-300, 477-481`: desired qty (`fg_completed_qty × required_qty / wo.qty`) is capped at `pending_to_issue = required_qty − transferred_qty`, unless over-transfer is allowed via `_is_overproduction_allowed()` (uses Manufacturing Settings `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order` / `transfer_extra_materials_percentage`). Items fully transferred are dropped with "All items have already been transferred for this Work Order." - Pick list: `create_pick_list()` → `_pick_list_mapping` (condition `transferred_qty < required_qty`) and `_set_pick_list_item_qty()` — `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/mapper.py:470-515` — same pending cap; `Pick List.get_pending_work_orders()` (`pick_list.py:1335`) only lists WOs with `qty > material_transferred_for_manufacturing`; the Pick List form prompt caps "Qty of Finished Goods Item" at `qty − material_transferred_for_manufacturing` (`pick_list.js:197-208`); Stock Entries from a pick list only take `picked_qty − transferred_qty` (`get_pending_transfer_stock_qty`, `pick_list/mapper.py:474`). 2. **Hard validation at Stock Entry submit:** - `_validate_no_excess_transfer()` — `material_transfer.py:193-244`: for entries without `fg_completed_qty` (pick-list flow), throws **"Excess Material Transfer"** if the summed entry qty of any item (mapping alternatives via `original_item`) exceeds `Σ(required_qty − transferred_qty)`. Deliberately relaxed when backflush is "Material Transferred for Manufacture" or for returns. - `StatusService._update_qty_for_purpose()` — `status.py:208-226`: throws `StockOverProductionError` if `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` exceeds `wo.qty + allowance%` (same two settings). - `WorkOrder.validate_additional_transferred_qty()` — `work_order.py:586-601`: caps the separate `additional_transferred_qty` (entries flagged `is_additional_transfer_entry`) by `transfer_extra_materials_percentage`. - Optional strict BOM check: `validate_component_and_quantities()` → `_check_bom_component_qty()` (`material_transfer.py:184-191`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/manufacturing.py:367, 877`) when "Validate Components Quantities per BOM" is enabled. Non-BOM "additional" items transferred along the way are appended to `required_items` as `is_additional_item` rows by `RequiredItemsService.add_additional_items()` (`required_items.py:263-301`) unless that strict setting is on.

I now have the complete picture across the Work Order, Stock Entry, and Pick List sides. Here's the full answer. ## How the "Material Transferred for Manufacturing" progress is computed The field is `Work Order.material_transferred_for_manufacturing`, recomputed every time a Stock Entry with purpose **"Material Transfer for Manufacture"** is submitted or cancelled against the WO: **Trigger chain:** - `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.on_submit()/on_cancel()` → `update_job_card_and_work_order()` → `wo_doc.run_method("update_status")` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py:365-390` - `StatusService.update_status()` (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/status.py:88-105`) first calls `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` (stub at `work_order.py:1016`), then `update_required_items()`. - Both land in `RequiredItemsService` (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`), which sets each row's `transferred_qty` (`update_transferred_qty_for_required_items`, line 133) and the WO-level progress. **Two computation paths in `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` (lines 162-194):** 1. **Sum-of-`fg_completed_qty` path** — via `StatusService.get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty("Material Transfer for Manufacture", ...)` (status.py:267-283), which sums `Stock Entry.fg_completed_qty` over submitted entries for the WO. Used whenever that sum is non-zero (classic flow and direct/excess-transfer entries). 2. **Min-fraction path (the partial-batch case)** — the Pick List flow sets `stock_entry.fg_completed_qty = 0` (see `update_stock_entry_based_on_work_order`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/pick_list/mapper.py:420`), so progress is derived from *actual item-level transfers*: - `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)` (line 201) sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` per item (grouped by `item_code, original_item`, so substitutes credit the original item) over all submitted transfer entries for the WO (`_material_transfer_filter`, line 228). - For each manufacturing item it computes `transferred / required_qty`, takes the **minimum fraction across all items**, caps it at 1.0, and sets `material_transferred_for_manufacturing = min_fraction × wo.qty`. The comment explains why: *"use min-fraction of actual item transfers so partial availability does not prematurely mark the work order as fully transferred."* E.g., a WO for 10 units needing 20×A and 30×B, with partial batches of 10×A and 12×B, shows min(10/20, 12/30) = 0.4 → **4** units transferred — progress is limited by the least-served component, not inflated by one fully-transferred item. This value drives the progress bar in `work_order.js::show_progress_for_items` (line 484) and status decisions in `StatusService._submitted_status()` (status.py:129-144), with `_has_transferred_material()` (line 146) catching pick-list/MR-sourced entries that legitimately leave the field at 0 so the WO still becomes "In Process". ## What prevents transferring more than the WO requires Several layered guards: 1. **Hard validation on submit/save** — `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.validate()` → `validate_component_and_quantities()` → `_validate_no_excess_transfer()` (material_transfer.py:193-244). For non-return entries (skipped when backflush is based on "Material Transferred for Manufacture"), it computes per-item pending = Σ(`required_qty − transferred_qty`) from the WO's required rows, sums the entry's rows per item (resolving substitutes via `original_item`), and throws **"Excess Material Transfer — Cannot transfer X; Maximum transferable quantity is Y"** if exceeded. Since row `transferred_qty` is refreshed after each partial batch, each subsequent entry only gets the remaining allowance. 2. **Capping the suggested quantities** — the whitelisted `StockEntry.get_items()` (stock_entry.py:1366) → `add_items()` → `get_pending_raw_materials()` (material_transfer.py:257) → `get_work_order_required_items()`/`_add_required_item()` (line 323) only includes items where `required_qty (+ transfer_extra_materials_percentage) > transferred_qty`, and `_calculate_item_transfer_qty()` (line 292) caps qty at `pending_to_issue = required_qty − transferred_qty` via `_resolve_transfer_qty()` (line 477) — unless `_is_overproduction_allowed()` (line 278) permits extras per `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order`/`transfer_extra_materials_percentage` in Manufacturing Settings. (With `fg_completed_qty` set, `_check_bom_component_qty` in `services/manufacturing.py` validates components against the BOM instead.) 3. **Post-submit rollup guard** — `StatusService.update_work_order_qty()` → `_update_qty_for_purpose()` (status.py:208-226) throws `StockOverProductionError` if the rolled-up transferred qty exceeds `qty + allowance%`. 4. **Pick List layer** (the partial-fulfillment entry point): - `get_pending_work_orders()` (`pick_list.py:1335`) only offers WOs with `qty > material_transferred_for_manufacturing`. - WO → Pick List: `create_pick_list()` / `_set_pick_list_item_qty` (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/mapper.py:470-515`) maps only rows with `transferred_qty < required_qty` and caps each row at `pending_to_issue`; `pick_list.js::work_order` (line 197) caps `for_qty` to `qty − material_transferred_for_manufacturing`. - Pick List → Stock Entry: `update_stock_entry_based_on_work_order()` (`pick_list/mapper.py:411`) skips locations with no pending qty (`get_pending_transfer_stock_qty()`, line 474: `picked_qty − transferred_qty`) and sets `fg_completed_qty = 0`. 5. **Job Card variant** — when `transfer_material_against == "Job Card"`, `JobCard.validate_over_transfer()` (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/job_card/job_card.py:1227`) blocks transfers exceeding the Job Card Item's `required_qty` (subject to the `job_card_excess_transfer` setting).

## How `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` is computed The Work Order field `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` is not incremented per transfer — it is **recomputed from all submitted Stock Entries** against the WO every time one is submitted or cancelled: **1. Trigger chain (Stock Entry → Work Order)** - `StockEntry._configure_purpose_class()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py:196`) maps purpose `Material Transfer for Manufacture` → `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry` (line 201); `on_submit`/`on_cancel` (lines 331/354) delegate to it. - `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.on_submit()` → `update_job_card_and_work_order()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py:365-390`) calls `wo_doc.run_method("update_work_order_qty")` (when `fg_completed_qty` is set) and `wo_doc.run_method("update_status")`. **2. Aggregate rollup — `StatusService.update_work_order_qty()`** (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/status.py:193`) - `_update_qty_for_purpose()` (L208) → `get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty()` (L267) does `SUM(fg_completed_qty)` over submitted Stock Entries filtered by `work_order`, `docstatus=1`, `purpose="Material Transfer for Manufacture"` (`_stock_entry_filter`, L285; `is_additional_transfer_entry` splits off `additional_transferred_qty`). **3. Item-level recompute for partial/pick-list transfers — `RequiredItemsService`** (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`) - `update_required_items()` (L30) → `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items()` (L133) sets each `required_items.transferred_qty` from `_material_transfer_qty_by_item()` (L201), which sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` grouped by `(item_code, original_item)` (so alternative/substitute items credit the required item). - **The partial-batch rule** is `recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` (L162): pick-list-driven entries set `fg_completed_qty = 0`, so the SUM route is skipped and instead `min_fraction = min over required items of (transferred_qty / required_qty)`, capped at 1.0, and `material_transferred_for_manufacturing = min_fraction * wo.qty`. So with several partial batches, WO progress is governed by the **least-fulfilled component**, preventing a WO from showing 100% transferred when one raw material is still short. - `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing()` (L152) is called from `StatusService.update_status()` (status.py L94) so the "Not Started" → "In Process" flip happens immediately after each partial transfer (`_submitted_status`, status.py L129). **4. Pick-list partial flow** — `create_stock_entry()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/pick_list/mapper.py:284`) → `update_stock_entry_based_on_work_order()` (L411): sets `fg_completed_qty = 0` (L420) and appends only rows where `get_pending_transfer_stock_qty()` (L474, `picked_qty − transferred_qty`) > 0, so each repeat Stock Entry carries only the remaining picked qty. `StockEntry.on_submit` → `update_pick_list_status()` (`pick_list.py:935`) tracks `Pick List Item.transferred_qty` and status (Partially Transferred/Completed). Behaviour is covered by `test_pick_list.py:1243`. ## What prevents over-transfer 1. **At entry creation**: `get_pending_raw_materials()` (`material_transfer.py:257`, invoked via `StockEntry.get_items()` → `add_items()`, stock_entry.py:1365) caps each item at `required_qty − transferred_qty` in `_calculate_item_transfer_qty()` (L292); `_add_required_item()` (L323) skips fully transferred items unless backflush mode is "Material Transferred for Manufacture"; `_is_overproduction_allowed()` (L278) allows exceeding only by the `transfer_extra_materials_percentage` / `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order` allowance from Manufacturing Settings. 2. **At validation/submit**: `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.validate()` → `validate_component_and_quantities()` (L184) → `_validate_no_excess_transfer()` (L193): builds `pending_by_item = required_qty − transferred_qty` and **throws "Excess Material Transfer — Maximum transferable quantity is X"** (L228-244) if the entry's rows exceed pending; quantities are summed per item across rows, so splitting an item over multiple rows doesn't bypass it. 3. **Aggregate WO cap after submit**: `StatusService._update_qty_for_purpose()` (status.py L208) throws `StockOverProductionError` (defined in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py:78`) if total transferred exceeds `wo.qty + allowance%` (`_qty_allowance`, L235). 4. **Additional (extra) transfers**: `WorkOrder.validate_additional_transferred_qty()` (work_order.py L586) caps `material_transferred_for_manufacturing + additional_transferred_qty` at `qty + transfer_extra_materials_percentage%`. 5. Client-side, the "Start" button in `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.js:803-832` only offers further transfer while some `transferred_qty < required_qty` (or up to the extra-materials allowance). `_validate_work_order()` (`stock_entry/services/stock_entry_base.py:29`) additionally blocks transfers against draft/stopped Work Orders.

I now have the complete picture. Here's how it works: # How "Material Transferred for Manufacturing" is computed ## The trigger chain When a Stock Entry with purpose **"Material Transfer for Manufacture"** is submitted: `StockEntry.on_submit` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py:331`) → `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry.on_submit` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py:365`) → **`update_job_card_and_work_order`** (same file, :371), which validates the WO via `BaseStockEntry._validate_work_order` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/stock_entry_base.py:29` — WO must be submitted, not Stopped), then runs `wo_doc.update_work_order_qty()` and `wo_doc.update_status()`. `update_status` → `WorkOrder.update_required_items()`. ## Two progress regimes (the partial-batch case is the second one) **1. Aggregate regime — `StatusService.update_work_order_qty`** (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/status.py:193`) Iterates `_QTY_PURPOSES` (:18), mapping purpose `"Material Transfer for Manufacture"` → fields `material_transferred_for_manufacturing` and `additional_transferred_qty`. `_update_qty_for_purpose` (:208) gets the qty from **`get_transferred_or_manufactured_qty`** (:267), which sums `Stock Entry.fg_completed_qty` over all submitted entries filtered by `_stock_entry_filter` (:285): `work_order = WO`, `purpose = "Material Transfer for Manufacture"`, `docstatus = 1`, and `is_additional_transfer_entry = 0/1` (separating normal vs. excess entries). Result is `db_set` on the field. **2. Min-fraction regime for partial/pick-list transfers — `RequiredItemsService.recompute_material_transferred_for_manufacturing`** (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py:162`) This is the heart of the partial-batch question. Pick-list-driven transfer entries are created with `fg_completed_qty = 0`, so the SUM above is 0. The code then falls back to an item-level computation: - `_material_transfer_qty_by_item(is_return=0)` (:201) sums `Stock Entry Detail.transfer_qty` across **all** submitted, non-return transfer entries for the WO, grouped by `(item_code, original_item)` — so multiple partial batches accumulate, and substitute items are credited to the required item via `original_item`. - `update_transferred_qty_for_required_items` (:133) writes each accumulated total into `required_items.transferred_qty` per row. - Then `recompute_...` (:188-194) computes: ```python min_fraction = min(transferred_by_item / required_by_item for each required item) min_fraction = min(min_fraction, 1.0) material_transferred_for_manufacturing = min_fraction * wo.qty ``` i.e. the WO counts as "transferred" only to the extent of the **least-transferred required item** (the bottleneck). If a pick list could only partially fulfill one component, that component's fraction caps the whole WO's progress — partial availability never marks the WO as fully transferred. (This recompute is also exposed as `refresh_material_transferred_for_manufacturing` (:152), which `StatusService.update_status` calls at :94 before deciding status, precisely so pick-list transfers are reflected immediately.) The status itself: `StatusService._submitted_status` (:129) sets "In Process" when `material_transferred_for_manufacturing > 0`; `_has_transferred_material` (:146) additionally checks for any submitted pick-list/MR-sourced transfer entry, since the min-fraction rule can legitimately leave the field at 0. # What prevents over-transferring Multiple layered guards: 1. **Per-item guard at validate time — `MaterialTransferForManufactureStockEntry._validate_no_excess_transfer`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py:193`): for entries with no `fg_completed_qty` (the partial/pick-list flow), it computes `pending_by_item = required_qty − transferred_qty` from the WO's `required_items`, sums the entry's qty per item, and throws **"Excess Material Transfer"** ("Maximum transferable quantity is X") if any item exceeds its pending qty. Skipped for returns and when `backflush_raw_materials_based_on == "Material Transferred for Manufacture"`. 2. **Capping when auto-fetching items — `get_pending_raw_materials` / `_calculate_item_transfer_qty`** (same file, :257 and :292): `pending_to_issue = required_qty − transferred_qty`; the suggested qty is capped at pending unless `_is_overproduction_allowed` (:278) — i.e. `wo.qty + (transfer_extra_materials_percentage or overproduction_percentage_for_work_order)% ≥ material_transferred + fg_completed_qty`. If everything is already transferred, it msgprints "All items have already been transferred for this Work Order." 3. **Aggregate guard on submit — `StatusService._update_qty_for_purpose`** (status.py:208): throws `StockOverProductionError` (defined `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py:78`) if the recomputed total exceeds `wo.qty + allowance%`, where the allowance comes from `_qty_allowance` (status.py:235) — `overproduction_percentage_for_work_order`, falling back to `transfer_extra_materials_percentage` for the transfer purpose. 4. **Excess handled explicitly via `additional_transferred_qty`**: extra-beyond-WO-qty entries are flagged `is_additional_transfer_entry = 1`, tracked separately, and validated by `WorkOrder.validate_additional_transferred_qty` (work_order.py:586) against `qty + qty × transfer_extra_materials_percentage/100` ("Transfer Extra Raw Materials to WIP" in Manufacturing Settings). Items not in the BOM are appended to `required_items` as `is_additional_item` rows by `RequiredItemsService.add_additional_items` (required_items.py:263) / removed on cancel by `remove_additional_items` (:257). 5. **Consumption can't outrun transfers — `ManufactureStockEntry.add_raw_materials_based_on_transfer`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/manufacturing.py:542`): `pending_qty_to_mfg = material_transferred_for_manufacturing − produced_qty`; it returns early when ≤ 0, so the Manufacture entry can only backflush against material actually sitting in WIP (`prepare_available_materials_based_on_transfer` :613 sums prior transfer entries minus consumption). 6. **Partial fulfillment of a prior transfer entry**: `_validate_item_transferred_qty` (material_transfer.py:92) rejects receiving more against an outgoing entry than its `transfer_qty`, and `update_transferred_qty` (:68) rolls the partial receipts into the source entry's `transferred_qty` and `per_transferred` percent — this is how a pick-list-driven partial pick updates the outbound document. **Key files**: `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/status.py`, `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/required_items.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/manufacturing.py`, `erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/work_order.py` (delegating wrappers at :997-1047).

## What `make_gl_entries` does today **Location/definition:** `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`, lines 34–74: ```python def make_gl_entries(gl_map, cancel=False, adv_adj=False, merge_entries=True, update_outstanding="Yes", from_repost=False): ``` It is the single posting sink for all ERPNext vouchers. Both branches (submit and cancel) eventually funnel into `make_entry()` (line 377), which creates a `GL Entry` doc, sets flags (`adv_adj`, `update_outstanding`, `from_repost`, `ignore_links` when cancelled or immutable ledger) and calls `gle.submit()`. ### Submit path (`cancel=False`) 1. **Budget validation** — `BudgetValidation(gl_map=gl_map).validate()` unless Accounts Settings has `use_legacy_budget_controller` or the voucher is a Period Closing Voucher. 2. **Dimension offsetting** — `make_acc_dimensions_offsetting_entry(gl_map)` (line 77): if an Accounting Dimension has "automatically post balancing entry" enabled and the map uses >1 value of it, extra rows against the offsetting account are appended. 3. **List-level validations** (from `erpnext/accounts/services/gl_validator.py`): `validate_accounting_period` (throws `ClosedAccountingPeriod`), `validate_disabled_accounts`. 4. **`process_gl_map(gl_map, merge_entries, from_repost)`** (line 141): - `distribute_gl_based_on_cost_center_allocation` (skipped for PCV): splits each row across Cost Center Allocation percentages, runs `validate_expense_against_budget` per row, and pins the round-off account row to the main cost center. - **Merge/dedup** — if `merge_entries`, `merge_similar_entries()` (line 226): - Rows with truthy `_skip_merge` bypass merging (only producer today: `PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer.add_supplier_gl_entry`, `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/gl_composer.py:123`). - Merge key = tuple of `get_merge_properties()` (line 282): `account, cost_center, party, party_type, voucher_detail_no, against_voucher, against_voucher_type, project, finance_book, voucher_no, advance_voucher_type, advance_voucher_no` **plus all accounting dimensions**. Same-key rows get debit/credit (in company, account and transaction currency) summed. - Zero-value rows are dropped (both debit and credit = 0 at GL precision), **except** Journal Entries of type "Exchange Gain Or Loss". - `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative()` (line 316): flips negative debit/credit pairs to the opposite side; nets both sides when `post_net_value` is set. 5. **Row-count guard:** if only one entry survives processing, it throws "Incorrect number of General Ledger Entries found…"; otherwise it calls `create_payment_ledger_entry(...)` (skipped for PCV) and `save_entries(...)`. 6. **`save_entries()`** (line 359): - `validate_cwip_accounts` (unless `from_repost`), `check_freezing_date` (frozen ledger), `validate_against_pcv` (Period Closing Voucher vs opening entries), `validate_allowed_dimensions` per row. - **`process_debit_credit_difference()`** (line 397) — the round-off logic: - Computes the debit−credit diff at GL precision (`get_debit_credit_difference`); allowance from `get_debit_credit_allowance` = `5.0 / 10^precision` for Journal Entry and Payment Entry, else `0.5`. Diff above allowance → throws "Debit and Credit not equal…" (excused for JE "Exchange Gain Or Loss"). - If the diff is ≥ `10^-precision`, `make_round_off_gle()` (line 475) posts it: picks `round_off_account`/`round_off_cost_center`/`round_off_for_opening` from Company (fallback: `default_expense_account`; prefers the voucher's parent cost center; throws if unset). If the map already has a row on the round-off account, the diff is **absorbed into that row** (and the row is removed if the residual becomes negligible); otherwise a new row is appended with party/against_voucher cleared and dimensions backfilled via `update_accounting_dimensions`. - `make_entry()` per row → `GL Entry.submit()`, then per-row `validate_expense_against_budget` (unless `from_repost`). ### Cancel path (`cancel=True`) Delegates to **`make_reverse_gl_entries()`** (line 607): loads the voucher's existing non-cancelled GL rows if none supplied, runs `create_payment_ledger_entry(cancel=1)`, `validate_accounting_period`, `check_freezing_date`, `validate_against_pcv`, marks the originals `is_cancelled=1` (supports `partial_cancel` keyed on `voucher_detail_no` for the "Advance in separate account" feature), then posts mirrored rows (debit↔credit swapped, `is_cancelled=1`, or `posting_date`-dated rows under immutable ledger). --- ## What a signature / merge-behavior change would affect **Direct callers of `erpnext.accounts.general_ledger.make_gl_entries`** (what breaks if the signature or merge semantics change): | Module / Document types | Call pattern | |---|---| | `accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:1045` (+ `SalesInvoiceGLComposer`) | `merge_entries=False`, `update_outstanding` = "No" for POS/write-off/loyalty; pre-merges itself via `merge_similar_entries()` in `services/gl_composer.py:49` | | `accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/purchase_invoice.py:678` (+ `PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer`) | `merge_entries=False`, `from_repost`; uses `_skip_merge` on supplier entry and calls `merge_similar_entries()` directly (`services/gl_composer.py:42`) | | `accounts/doctype/payment_entry/payment_entry.py:1298, 1316` | passes `merge_entries` from Accounts Settings `merge_similar_account_heads`, plus `cancel`, `adv_adj`, `update_outstanding`; also pre-calls `process_gl_map()` (line 1297) | | `accounts/doctype/journal_entry/journal_entry.py:878` | `cancel`, `adv_adj`, `merge_entries` from settings, `update_outstanding="No"` for Deferred Revenue/Expense voucher types | | `accounts/doctype/period_closing_voucher/period_closing_voucher.py:475` and `process_period_closing_voucher/process_period_closing_voucher.py:438` | `merge_entries=False` (PCV rows also skip budget/payment-ledger/PCV checks internally) | | `accounts/doctype/process_deferred_accounting/process_deferred_accounting.py:54` | `make_gl_entries(gl_map=…, cancel=1)` — keyword `gl_map` | | `accounts/deferred_revenue.py:580` | its own wrapper also named `make_gl_entries`; calls the GL one with `merge_entries=True`, `cancel=(doc.docstatus == 2)` | | `accounts/doctype/invoice_discounting/invoice_discounting.py:190` | `cancel=(docstatus==2)`, `update_outstanding="No"` | | `controllers/stock_controller.py:205` | one shared entry point for **Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry, Stock Reconciliation, Subcontracting Receipt** (+ Landed Cost Voucher via repost in `landed_cost_voucher.py:352`); passes `from_repost` | | Stock GL composers | `stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py:162`, `stock_entry/services/gl_composer.py:51`, `purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py:37`, `subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py:31` call `process_gl_map()` **directly** (pre-processing before make_gl_entries) | | `assets/doctype/asset/asset.py:981` (CWIP booking), `asset_capitalization.py:390` (`merge_entries=False, from_repost`), `asset_repair.py:315` (positional `make_gl_entries(gl_entries, cancel)`) | asset module | | `accounts/doctype/repost_accounting_ledger/repost_accounting_ledger.py:192-213` | calls doc-level `make_gl_entries(cancel=…)`/`make_gl_entries(1)` for invoices, PE, JE, Expense Claim and hook-registered doctypes | | `accounts/utils.py:1705` (repost of stock vouchers) | `voucher_obj.make_gl_entries(gl_entries=expected_gle, from_repost=True)` | | Patches | `patches/v12_0/repost_stock_ledger_entries_for_target_warehouse.py`, `patches/v13_0/modify_invalid_gain_loss_gl_entries.py`, `patches/v15_0/repost_gl_entries_with_no_account_subcontracting.py` | | Preview | `controllers/ledger_preview.py:43` — dry-run `doc.make_gl_entries()` inside a savepoint for GL preview | | Tests | `journal_entry/test_journal_entry.py:570,618` call `process_gl_map(gl_map, False)` positionally | **Behavioral coupling to be careful about when changing merge behavior:** - The **"more than one entry" guard** (line 56) throws if merging/distribution leaves a single row — any new merge key logic changes which vouchers hit this. - **Round-off absorption** (`make_round_off_gle`) scans the *already-merged* map for a round-off-account row; different merge granularity changes which row absorbs the diff and whether it is removed or appended. - **Merging is dedup-sensitive for reporting**: the merge key includes `against_voucher`, `voucher_detail_no`, party and dimensions — payment ledger entries (`create_payment_ledger_entry`), AR/AP outstanding updates (`GL Entry.submit` → `update_outstanding_amt`, gated on the `update_outstanding` flag), and reconciliation by `against_voucher` depend on the resulting row granularity. - The `_skip_merge` escape hatch and the settings toggle `merge_similar_account_heads` (only honored by Payment Entry and Journal Entry today — invoices always bypass it) are the existing merge-behavior control points. - Tests directly pinning current behavior: `test_journal_entry.py` (`process_gl_map`), `test_period_closing_voucher.py` (imports `make_reverse_gl_entries`), plus the doctype test suites for the vouchers listed above.

A new merge key or default silently changes allocation granularity in `create_payment_ledger_entry`. 3. **`_skip_merge`** must keep being honored, or advance-in-separate-party-account rows will collapse. 4. **Merge-before-round-off ordering:** merged totals feed `process_debit_credit_difference`; a looser/tighter merge changes the round-off residual, can newly trigger `raise_debit_credit_not_equal_error` (allowance is only 0.5 for invoices), or produce a round-off entry where none existed. 5. **The >1-entry guard (`:56-72`)** will start throwing for legitimately single-account vouchers if new merge/filter logic shrinks the map to one entry. 6. **Exchange Gain/Loss carve-out** (`:266-277`) and the "skip PCV" special cases must be preserved or zero-value JEs and year-end closing break. 7. **Cancel asymmetry:** submit-side merging is fine because cancellation reverses DB rows, but any merge change must not assume cancel-side maps were built by the same pipeline (`make_reverse_gl_entries` never merges). 8. **Payment Entry double-processing** (`process_gl_map` at `payment_entry.py:1297` then again inside `make_gl_entries`) — idempotence of the new merge logic is not guaranteed (e.g., a second `distribute_gl_based_on_cost_center_allocation` pass would re-split already-split rows), so a signature/merge refactor should make the pipeline explicitly idempotent or remove the duplicate pass.

## What `make_gl_entries` does today **Location & signature** — `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py:34`: ```python def make_gl_entries(gl_map, cancel=False, adv_adj=False, merge_entries=True, update_outstanding="Yes", from_repost=False): ``` It is the single funnel that turns a composed voucher GL map into persisted `GL Entry` (and Payment Ledger Entry) docs. ### Submit path (`cancel=False`), in order 1. **Budget validation** (lines 43–49): `BudgetValidation(gl_map=gl_map).validate()` — skipped when cancelling, when Accounts Settings `use_legacy_budget_controller` is set, or for `Period Closing Voucher`. 2. **Dimension offsetting** — `make_acc_dimensions_offsetting_entry(gl_map)` (line 77): for every Accounting Dimension with an offsetting account, it clones each row and adds mirrored debit/credit rows against the offsetting account. 3. **Validations** — `validate_accounting_period(gl_map)` and `validate_disabled_accounts(gl_map)` from `erpnext/accounts/services/gl_validator.py`. 4. **`process_gl_map`** (line 141), which does three things: - `distribute_gl_based_on_cost_center_allocation` — splits each row across sub cost centers per an active `Cost Center Allocation`, running `validate_expense_against_budget` on the main cost center; the row on the round-off account is passed through untouched; skipped for `Period Closing Voucher` and cached via `@request_cache` on `get_cost_center_allocation_data`. - **Merging** — if `merge_entries`, calls `merge_similar_entries` (see below). - `toggle_debit_credit_if_negative` — flips negative debits/credits into the opposite side (and nets out when `post_net_value` is set). 5. **Guards** — if the processed map has ≤1 row it throws *"Incorrect number of General Ledger Entries found. You might have selected a wrong Account in the transaction."*; otherwise `create_payment_ledger_entry(...)` (skipped for PCV) and `save_entries(...)`. 6. **`save_entries`** (line 359): `validate_cwip_accounts` → `process_debit_credit_difference` → `check_freezing_date` (frozen accounts) → `validate_against_pcv` → per-row `validate_allowed_dimensions` → `make_entry`, which builds a `GL Entry` doc with flags (`ignore_permissions`, `from_repost`, `adv_adj`, `update_outstanding`, `ignore_links` when immutable ledger/cancelled), submits it, then re-runs `validate_expense_against_budget`. ### Cancel path (`cancel=True`) Delegates entirely to `make_reverse_gl_entries` (line 607), which loads the original (non-cancelled) `GL Entry` rows if none were passed, calls `create_payment_ledger_entry(cancel=1)`, re-validates the accounting period and frozen date (honoring immutable-ledger posting date overrides), and re-books the entries with swapped debit/credit. ### Merging / deduplication — `merge_similar_entries` (line 226) - Rows with `_skip_merge` set are passed through untouched. - Merge key = tuple of `get_merge_properties`: `account, cost_center, party, party_type, voucher_detail_no, against_voucher, against_voucher_type, project, finance_book, voucher_no, advance_voucher_type, advance_voucher_no` **plus** every active accounting dimension (`get_merge_key`/`check_if_in_list`). - Matching rows are summed across six fields: `debit/credit`, `..._in_account_currency`, `..._in_transaction_currency`. - Zero-value rows are dropped at GL Entry `debit` field precision — except `Journal Entry` of subtype `Exchange Gain Or Loss` (kept even if zero, because the JE header depends on it). - Precision comes from `get_field_precision` of the GL Entry `debit` field vs the company currency. ### Round-off handling Two layers: - **Upstream**: voucher composers add an explicit round-off row using `get_round_off_account_and_cost_center` (Company `round_off_account`, `round_off_cost_center`, `round_off_for_opening`; fallback to `default_expense_account`; parent cost-center preference; throws if unset — imported e.g. by `accounts_controller.py:33` and `purchase_invoice.py`). - **Inside `make_gl_entries`**: `save_entries → process_debit_credit_difference` (line 397). It computes the debit−credit difference via `get_debit_credit_difference` (which *also mutates the caller's map*, rounding every `debit`/`credit`/transaction-currency field in place). Allowance = `5/(10**precision)` for `Journal Entry`/`Payment Entry`, else `0.5`. If the diff exceeds the allowance (and it's not an Exchange Gain Or Loss JE) → `raise_debit_credit_not_equal_error`. If it's between `1/(10**precision)` and the allowance → `make_round_off_gle` (line 475) appends or *updates an existing* round-off row: uses `round_off_for_opening` when opening entries exist (throws if unset), strips a pre-existing round-off row if the residual becomes negligible, nulls `party`/`against_voucher`, copies voucher header fields, fills accounting dimensions (`update_accounting_dimensions`), then re-checks the balance and throws if still unbalanced. **Note the ordering: merge happens before round-off**, so the residual diff that gets rounded (or rejected) depends on the merge behavior. ## What a signature / merge-behavior change would affect ### Callers (the blast radius) **Controller hubs** (everything below routes through these): - `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py` — base class for all accounting doctypes (imports `get_round_off_account_and_cost_center`). - `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:178,205,281` — `StockController.make_gl_entries`/`make_gl_entries_on_cancel` → affects **Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry, Stock Reconciliation, Subcontracting Receipt, Landed Cost Voucher** (perpetual inventory), plus `erpnext/controllers/ledger_preview.py:43` (GL preview runs `doc.make_gl_entries()` in a sandbox). - `erpnext/accounts/utils.py:1705` — repost plumbing calls `voucher_obj.make_gl_entries(gl_entries=..., from_repost=True)`. **Document types calling the module-level function** (mostly via their own same-named method — changing the free function's params keeps those methods, but every method body funnels in): | DocType / module | Call pattern | |---|---| | Sales Invoice (`sales_invoice.py:1045` + `services/gl_composer.py`) | `merge_entries=False`, conditional `update_outstanding` | | Purchase Invoice (`purchase_invoice.py:671` + composer; also imports `merge_similar_entries` directly) | merge flag via Settings | | Payment Entry (`payment_entry.py:1292–1316`) | `merge_entries` from Accounts Settings `merge_similar_account_heads`; **note it calls `process_gl_map` and then `make_gl_entries(..., merge_entries=...)` — merging is applied twice here**, so new merge semantics hit this path twice | | Journal Entry (`journal_entry.py:866`) | merge flag from Settings; allowance is JE-specific | | Period Closing Voucher (`period_closing_voucher.py:475`) | `merge_entries=False` | | Process Period Closing Voucher (`:438`) | `merge_entries=False` | | Process Deferred Accounting (`:54`) | `make_gl_entries(gl_map=..., cancel=1)` | | Deferred revenue/expense (`accounts/deferred_revenue.py:580`) | `merge_entries=True`, per-entry commit + rollback/flag error handling | | Invoice Discounting (`:190`) | `update_outstanding="No"` | | Asset depreciation (`asset.py:981`) | bare positional `make_gl_entries(gl_entries)` | | Asset Repair (`asset_repair.py:315`) | **`make_gl_entries(gl_entries, cancel)` — the only positional second argument; renaming/reordering params breaks this** | | Asset Capitalization (`:390`) | `merge_entries=False` | | Repost Accounting Ledger (`:200–210`) | drives other doctypes' methods with `from_repost`/`cancel` | **Patches** (frozen historical code — a breaking signature change silently breaks upgrades): `patches/v12_0/repost_stock_ledger_entries_for_target_warehouse.py`, `patches/v13_0/modify_invalid_gain_loss_gl_entries.py`, `patches/v14_0/single_to_multi_dunning.py`, `patches/v15_0/repost_gl_entries_with_no_account_subcontracting.py`. **Tests**: `test_journal_entry.py`, `test_period_closing_voucher.py`, `test_repost_item_valuation.py`, `test_invoice_discounting.py` and ~20 more transitively (per the call graph). ### Behavior couplings to watch when changing merge logic - **Receivable/Payable rows must not merge**: `party`, `party_type`, `against_voucher`, `against_voucher_type`, `voucher_detail_no` are in the merge key precisely so payment reconciliation, PLE (`create_payment_ledger_entry`) and outstanding amounts stay row-aligned. Weakening the key breaks allocation/reconciliation; strengthening it explodes row counts and changes the residual fed to `make_round_off_gle` (more balance-diff throws, since the round-off row is generated *after* merge). - **Hardcoded `merge_entries=False` callers** (Sales/Purchase Invoice, Asset Capitalization, Period Closing Voucher, Process Period Closing Voucher) depend on per-line rows surviving; changing the default or the semantics of the flag changes their ledger presentation. - **Settings-driven callers** (Journal Entry, Payment Entry) read `merge_similar_account_heads` and pass it explicitly — a rename of `merge_entries` breaks them, and Payment Entry's double `process_gl_map` must be re-audited. - **Zero-filter + Exchange Gain Or Loss exception** and the single-row "Incorrect number of GL Entries" guard are part of the merge contract; Journal Entry cancel/posting relies on both. - The module-level `make_gl_entries` name is shadowed by same-named *methods* on 8 `AccountsController`/`StockController` subclasses (dispatch noted by the call graph) — those methods are unaffected by a signature change, but they are the real transit path for every doc type listed above, so parameter additions need sensible defaults to keep `self.make_gl_entries(...)` → module call sites working.

## Short answer No — the report does not break. The shared engine has an explicit empty‑result guard that silently skips that combination, so the report still renders (the based‑on parent row just appears without a child row for that group value). ## Where and how The whole engine lives in **`erpnext/controllers/trends.py`** and is consumed by all the Trends reports (`sales_order_trends.py`, `purchase_order_trends.py`, `quotation_trends.py`, `sales_invoice_trends.py`, `purchase_invoice_trends.py`, `delivery_note_trends.py`, `purchase_receipt_trends.py` — each just calls `get_columns()` + `get_data()` from this module). When both filters are set, `get_data()` (line 77) takes the grouped path (`if filters.get("group_by"):` at line 107): 1. **Outer query `data1`** (lines 128–148): one aggregated row per distinct *based‑on* value, `GROUP BY conditions["group_by"]` (the `based_on_group_by` built in `based_wise_columns_query()`). 2. **Parent row emitted first** (lines 150–154): for each `data1[d]`, `dt.insert(ind, "")` inserts a blank cell at the group‑by column index `ind = conditions["columns"].index(conditions["grbc"][0])` (line 109) and appends it — so the based‑on header row is always present regardless of what happens next. 3. **Distinct group values** (lines 157–177): `SELECT DISTINCT(sel_col) … AND based_on_key = %s`, where `based_on_key = conditions["group_by"].split(",")[0].strip()` (line 119) — i.e. the detail queries are keyed off the *based‑on* value of the current outer row. 4. **Detail query `row1`** (lines 183–208): aggregates per period, filtered by **both** `sel_col = %s` (the group value) **and** `based_on_key = %s` (the based‑on value). 5. **The guard** (lines 210–211): ```python if not row1: continue ``` If the detail query for that group value × based‑on row returns nothing, the loop just `continue`s: no child row is built, no exception is raised, and the next group value is processed. ## Why this guard matters Without it, the very next statements — `des[ind - 1] = row1[0][0]` (line 214) and `des[j + inc] = row1[0][j]` (line 217) on an `as_list=1` result — would raise `IndexError: tuple index out of range` and the report *would* crash. The `if not row1: continue` is precisely what prevents that. This empty case is realistically reachable because of SQL NULL semantics: the `DISTINCT(sel_col)` list can contain a `NULL` group value (e.g. an item/customer with no customer set), but the detail query's `sel_col = %s` equality predicate never matches `NULL`, so `row1` comes back empty for that entry. ## Net effect on the rendered report - The based‑on parent row still appears with its period totals (qty/amt) and a **blank group‑by cell**. - The empty combination simply contributes no detail row. - `calculate_total_row(data1 …)` / `calculate_total_row(data …)` (lines 221 and 246) still appends the `'Total'` row, and totals stay correct since nothing empty was added. - Downstream charting is also safe: e.g. `sales_order_trends.get_chart_data()` explicitly skips rows whose group‑by cell is blank (`row[group_by_col_idx] == ""` → `continue`, lines 50–51) and skips the Total row, so an orphaned parent row is never double‑counted. One related protection: `validate_filters()` (line 65) throws `"'Based On' and 'Group By' can not be the same"` if the two filters collide, so the two column sets never overlap in the first place. The behavior is covered by tests in `erpnext/selling/report/sales_order_trends/test_sales_order_trends.py` (e.g. `test_report_executes_with_group_by`, `test_group_by_single_group_value_not_zeroed`), which exercise the full group‑by path of `get_data()`.

Nothing crashes, and the rest of the report (the based‑on aggregate row, the grand Total row, and the chart) is unaffected. ## What actually happens, step by step When `group_by` is set, `get_data(filters, conditions)` (`erpnext/controllers/trends.py:77-249`) runs three levels of queries: 1. **Outer aggregate query** (`data1`, lines 128–148): one row per *Based On* key, grouped by `conditions["group_by"]` (the `based_on_group_by` key from `based_wise_columns_query()`, e.g. `t2.item_code` for `based_on="Item"`), with period‑wise `SUM(CASE ...)` columns from `period_wise_columns_query()`. 2. **Header row is appended before any detail work** (lines 150–154): for each based‑on row `dt = data1[d]`, an empty string is inserted at the group‑by column index `ind = conditions["columns"].index(conditions["grbc"][0])` (the placeholder column produced by `group_wise_column()`), and the row is appended to `data`. So the based‑on row always exists in the output, even if every detail query beneath it comes back empty. 3. **Distinct group values** (`row`, lines 157–177): `SELECT DISTINCT(sel_col) ... AND <based_on_key> = %s` for that based‑on row (`data1[d][0]`), where `sel_col` is `t2.item_code` / `t1.customer` / `t1.supplier` depending on `filters.group_by`. 4. **Detail query per (group value, based‑on row) pair** (`row1`, lines 183–208): currency + period‑wise sums with `sel_col = %s AND <based_on_key> = %s`, grouped by `t4.default_currency, sel_col`. 5. **The guard** (lines 210–211): ```python if not row1: continue ``` If that detail query finds no matching data, the sub‑row is skipped entirely. This matters because the very next lines dereference `row1[0][0]` (`des[ind] = row[i][0]`, `des[ind - 1] = row1[0][0]`, lines 213–214) — without the guard, an empty `row1` would raise `IndexError: tuple index out of range` and the report would fail for all seven callers (`SalesOrderTrends`, `QuotationTrends`, `PurchaseOrderTrends`, `SalesInvoiceTrends`, `PurchaseInvoiceTrends`, `DeliveryNoteTrends`, `PurchaseReceiptTrends` `execute()`). ## Net effect on output (no breakage) - The (group value, based‑on value) combination just gets **no sub‑row** — the blank‑cell header row for the based‑on value (step 2) still appears with its period totals. - The grand **Total row** is computed from the aggregate rows, not the detail rows: `calculate_total_row(data1, ...)` at line 221 — so totals don't go missing or double‑count regardless of skipped sub‑rows. - The **chart** in each report wrapper (e.g. `get_chart_data` in `erpnext/selling/report/sales_order_trends/sales_order_trends.py:21-69`, identical pattern in quotation/purchase variants) is also safe: it skips the Total row by label, skips rows where the group‑by cell is `""` (the header rows), and only iterates rows that actually exist — an empty `row1` produces no row at all. Note also that `validate_filters()` (`trends.py:65-66`) throws if `based_on == group_by`, so the two filters always play distinct roles. The combined‑filter path is explicitly covered by regression tests in `erpnext/selling/report/sales_order_trends/test_sales_order_trends.py` (e.g. `test_group_by_single_group_value_not_zeroed`, `test_group_by_chart_matches_table_total_with_mixed_group_sizes`, `test_group_by_swapped_roles_based_on_customer_group_by_item`) and the mirrored `test_quotation_trends.py`, which assert the table total equals the chart total when based‑on rows have differing numbers of group values — exactly the mixed/empty-detail scenario.

## Short answer No — the report does not break. The shared engine has an explicit empty-result guard for exactly this case: in `get_data()` in `erpnext/controllers/trends.py`, the per-group-value detail query is checked with `if not row1: continue` (lines 210–211), so an empty detail result just causes that sub-row to be skipped and the loop to move on to the next distinct group value. ## How the code gets there All the Trends reports (`sales_order_trends.py`, `purchase_order_trends.py`, `quotation_trends.py`, `sales_invoice_trends.py`, `purchase_invoice_trends.py`, plus delivery-note/receipt trends) do the same thing: `conditions = get_columns(filters, trans)` then `get_data(filters, conditions)` — e.g. `erpnext/selling/report/sales_order_trends/sales_order_trends.py:14-15`. When **both** `based_on` and `group_by` are set (`validate_filters()` at `trends.py:65-66` enforces they can't be equal), `get_data()` (`trends.py:107-222`) runs a three-level nested query pattern: 1. **Block query** (`data1`, lines 128–148): one aggregate row per distinct *based-on* value, grouped by `conditions["group_by"]` (the `based_on_group_by` from `based_wise_columns_query()`, e.g. `t2.item_code, t4.default_currency`). For each row, a blank is inserted at the group-by column position (`dt.insert(ind, "")`, lines 150–154) to serve as the based-on header row. 2. **Distinct-values query** (`row`, lines 157–177): `DISTINCT(sel_col)` where `based_on_key = data1[d][0]` — i.e. which group-by values (Item/Customer/Supplier) exist under that based-on row. 3. **Detail query** (`row1`, lines 183–208): the aggregates filtered by **both** `sel_col = %s` (this group value) **and** `based_on_key = %s` (this based-on row). ## The failure case you're asking about If query 3 returns no rows for that particular (group value, based-on row) combination, line 210–211 fires: ```python if not row1: continue ``` This guard is what prevents a crash — without it, the very next statements (`des[ind - 1] = row1[0][0]` at line 214 and the fill loop at 216–217) would raise `IndexError: tuple index out of range` on the empty result set and blow up the whole report render. Instead: - The empty sub-row is silently skipped; the loop continues with the next distinct group value `i`, then the next based-on row `d`. - The based-on header row (already appended at line 154, carrying the based-on-level aggregates from `data1`) still appears in the output. - Execution always reaches `calculate_total_row(data1, ...)` (line 221), the `Total` row is appended, and `get_data()` returns normally. ## When row1 can legitimately be empty - **NULL group values**: `row` returns `DISTINCT(sel_col)`, which can include `NULL`; the detail query builds `sel_col = %s` (bound to `None` → `= NULL`), which matches nothing under SQL three-valued logic, so `row1` is empty and the row is skipped. - **Non-transactional reads**: the three queries are separate `frappe.db.sql` round trips, so a document cancelled/deleted between query 2 and query 3 can make `row1` empty. ## Cosmetic (not fatal) side effect Because the skip is silent, you can end up with a based-on header row that has aggregates but fewer (or zero) breakdown rows beneath it — a minor display inconsistency, not an error. Callers handle this fine: e.g. `get_chart_data()` in `sales_order_trends.py:46-51` explicitly skips the total row (`row[0] == "'Total'"`) and rows whose group-by cell is `""` (the blank header rows), so the chart isn't distorted either. So: empty detail query → `continue` → report renders completely, ending with the grand-total row.

## Short answer No — the report does not break. The shared engine has an explicit defensive guard for exactly that case: when the per-group-value detail query returns nothing, the code **silently skips that sub-row** (`if not row1: continue`) and keeps building the rest of the report, including the group header row and the Total row. ## Where this lives The shared engine is `erpnext/controllers/trends.py`. All seven Trends reports call the same two functions via `from erpnext.controllers.trends import get_columns, get_data`: - `erpnext/selling/report/sales_order_trends/sales_order_trends.py` - `erpnext/selling/report/quotation_trends/quotation_trends.py` - `erpnext/buying/report/purchase_order_trends/purchase_order_trends.py` - `erpnext/accounts/report/sales_invoice_trends/sales_invoice_trends.py` - `erpnext/accounts/report/purchase_invoice_trends/purchase_invoice_trends.py` - `erpnext/stock/report/delivery_note_trends/delivery_note_trends.py` - `erpnext/stock/report/purchase_receipt_trends/purchase_receipt_trends.py` Each report's `execute()` just does `conditions = get_columns(filters, trans)` then `data = get_data(filters, conditions)` — no per-report error handling is involved. ## The Group By + Based On flow in `get_data()` (trends.py:77–249) When `filters.get("group_by")` is set (line 107), the engine runs a three-level nested query cascade: 1. **Group summary query `data1`** (lines 128–148): aggregates `based_on_select + period_wise_select` grouped by `conditions["group_by"]` — which is the based-on key plus currency (set at the end of `based_wise_columns_query`, lines 563–564: `based_on_group_by += ", t4.default_currency"`, with `tabCompany t4` joined via `t1.company = t4.name`). One row per distinct based-on value × currency. 2. **Per based-on row**, the header row is appended with a blank inserted at the group-by column position `ind = conditions["columns"].index(conditions["grbc"][0])` (lines 109, 152–154). Then a **DISTINCT query** (lines 157–177) fetches the distinct values of `sel_col` — the Group By field (`t2.item_code`, `t1.customer`/`t1.party_name`, or `t1.supplier`, lines 111–116) — constrained to that based-on key (`based_on_key = conditions["group_by"].split(",")[0].strip()` matched against `data1[d][0]`). 3. **Per distinct group value**, a blank placeholder row `des = [""] * len(conditions["columns"])` is created (line 180), and the **detail query `row1`** (lines 183–208) fetches the period-wise `SUM(t2.stock_qty)` / `SUM(t2.base_net_amount)` for `sel_col = %s AND based_on_key = %s`, grouped by currency and `sel_col`. ## The exact behavior when the detail query is empty Lines 210–211: ```python if not row1: continue ``` If the detail query finds no matching data, the placeholder `des` is simply discarded and the loop moves on to the next distinct group value. Concretely: - **No exception is raised** — `frappe.db.sql` returns an empty list, which is falsy, so the guard triggers. - **No malformed/partial row is appended** — the all-blank `des` list is never populated or added to `data`. - The based-on **header row already appended at lines 152–154 stays**, all other distinct group values still produce their detail rows, and `calculate_total_row()` (line 221, appending at line 222) still emits the **Total row**. The report renders normally; the only observable effect is that the (based-on value × group value) sub-row is omitted — which is harmless since an empty detail contributed zero to every aggregate anyway. ## Why the guard is genuinely load-bearing Note what sits immediately after the guard (lines 213–217): ```python des[ind] = row[i][0] des[ind - 1] = row1[0][0] # would be an IndexError if row1 were [] for j in range(1, len(conditions["columns"]) - inc): des[j + inc] = row1[0][j] ``` Without the `if not row1: continue` guard, an empty detail result would raise `IndexError: list index out of range` at `row1[0][0]` and the whole report would fail for every filter combination touching that group. And empty results are realistically reachable: the DISTINCT query can yield a `NULL` group value, and SQL's `sel_col = %s` with `NULL` never matches anything, so `row1` comes back empty for that value. (`validate_filters`, lines 65–66, at least prevents the degenerate case where Based On equals Group By.) So: combined Group By + Based On is fully supported, and a data-less detail query degrades gracefully to a skipped sub-row rather than breaking the report.

## Summary ERPNext has **two parallel budget-check implementations** that both compute the "requested amount" as a single SQL aggregate — the sum of *per-row* (pending qty × rate) products across every matching Material Request line item: **1. New controller — `BudgetValidation` in `erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py`** Triggered on submit: `MaterialRequest.on_submit` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/material_request/material_request.py:240`) and `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:386`) call `BuyingController.validate_budget()` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978-983`), which instantiates `BudgetValidation(doc=self)` unless `Accounts Settings.use_legacy_budget_controller` is set. - `build_item_keys()` (lines 133–150) buckets the document's own rows by key `(dimension_type, dimension, expense_account)`, e.g. `(cost_center, "CC-1", "Stock Expense - C")`; `build_budget_keys()` (lines 110–127) builds matching budget keys (expanding group Cost Centers to leaf nodes via `get_child_nodes`). Only the intersection (`overlap`) is validated. - `validate_for_overbooking()` (line 83–98) then calls `get_requested_amount(key)` (lines 239–271), which runs **one aggregate query** joining `Material Request Item` to `Material Request`: ```python Sum((IfNull(mri.stock_qty, 0) - IfNull(mri.ordered_qty, 0)) * IfNull(mri.rate, 0)).as_("amount") ``` filtered on `docstatus == 1`, `material_request_type == "Purchase"`, `status != "Stopped"`, fiscal-year date range, `mri.expense_account == key[2]`, `mri[key[0]] == key[1]`, and `mri.item_code` ∈ the current document's item codes. So: `requested_amount = Σᵢ (stock_qtyᵢ − ordered_qtyᵢ) × rateᵢ` over **all** matching line items from all submitted MRs. - The sibling `get_ordered_amount(key)` (lines 209–237) does the same for POs: `Sum(IfNull(poi.amount,0) − IfNull(poi.billed_amt,0))`. Results feed `handle_material_request_overlimit` / `handle_purchase_order_overlimit` / `handle_cumulative_overlimit*`, which compare against `budget_amount` and `get_accumulated_monthly_budget`. Note `current_requested_amount` stays 0 for MR/PO because validation runs *after* submit, so the document's own rows are already inside the aggregate (comment at lines 91–93). **2. Legacy controller — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py`** `BuyingController.validate_budget()` legacy branch (buying_controller.py:984–1000) calls `validate_expense_against_budget(args)` (budget.py:377) per item row → `compare_expense_with_budget()` (line 540) → `get_requested_amount(params)` (lines 689–714): ```python # rate inside the aggregate: Sum(qty * rate) is the correct requested amount and is PG-valid Coalesce(Sum((child.stock_qty - child.ordered_qty) * child.rate), 0).as_("amount") ``` with an extra per-row filter `child.stock_qty > child.ordered_qty`. Here, for a Material Request `amount = requested_amount + ordered_amount`; for a Purchase Order `amount = ordered_amount`; then `total_expense = actual_expense + amount` is compared to the budget, raising `BudgetError` on "Stop". ## Why `rate` must be *inside* `Sum()` 1. **Mathematical correctness across heterogeneous line items.** The matched row set spans multiple Material Requests and multiple lines for the same item/dimension/expense account, potentially at *different* rates (different suppliers, price-list revisions). If `rate` were outside the aggregate — `SUM(stock_qty − ordered_qty) * rate` — SQL would first collapse everything into one total pending quantity and then multiply by a single **arbitrary row's** rate. That's only correct when all matched rows share one rate. The quantity-weighted form `Σ(qtyᵢ − ordered_qtyᵢ)·rateᵢ` is the true pending commitment; factoring `rate` out over- or under-states it, so `compare_expense_with_budget` / `handle_individual_doctype_action` would compare the wrong figure against the budget and could wrongly **Stop** a legitimate purchase or **Warn/allow** an overrun. 2. **SQL validity / determinism.** In an aggregate query without `GROUP BY`, a bare column reference outside an aggregate is rejected by PostgreSQL ("column … must appear in the GROUP BY clause or be used in an aggregate function") and by MySQL/MariaDB with `ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY`; on old MariaDB it silently picks a value from an arbitrary row. That is exactly what the comment at `budget.py:700` records — `Sum(qty * rate)` is both the correct requested amount *and* the only PG-valid form. A related robustness detail: the new controller wraps each operand in `IfNull(…, 0)` so one NULL `rate`/`qty` row can't NULL out the entire `SUM`, while the legacy version uses `Coalesce(Sum(…), 0)` to map an empty aggregate result to 0.
