final answer
All three auxiliary-data endpoints live in `erpnext/stock/doctype/item/item.py` and are called from `erpnext/stock/doctype/item/item.js`. Each one begins with an explicit, manually-coded permission check at the top of the function — since these are `@frappe.whitelist()` methods, whitelisting alone grants any logged-in user access, so the guard is the function body itself, not the decorator. ## 1. Attribute autocomplete — `get_item_attribute` (item.py:1525–1535) Called from `item.js:1483` (the variant-attribute awesomplete input). ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_attribute(parent: str, attribute_value: str = ""): """Used for providing auto-completions in child table.""" if not frappe.has_permission("Item"): frappe.throw(_("No Permission")) return frappe.get_all( "Item Attribute Value", ... ) ``` **Guard:** `frappe.has_permission("Item")` — checks that the user has **read** permission on the **Item** doctype (the `ptype` defaults to `"read"`). If not, it throws. Note this check is essential because the follow-up query uses `frappe.get_all`, which ignores row-level permissions by default — the explicit `has_permission` call is the only barrier. ## 2. Item price preview — `get_item_prices` (item.py:1588–1623) Called from `item.js:861` to populate the Item Prices quick view. ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_prices(item_code: str): """Fetch valid item prices for the item prices tab.""" if not frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read"): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` **Guard:** `frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read")` — requires read permission on the **Item Price** doctype (not just Item), because the query reads Item Price documents directly via `frappe.qb`. It raises `frappe.PermissionError` (a 403-class exception) rather than a plain validation error. ## 3. Opening stock creation — `make_opening_stock_entry` (item.py:1626–1696) Called from `item.js:1001` inside the "Add Opening Stock" dialog. ```python @frappe.whitelist() def make_opening_stock_entry(item_code, company, qty, valuation_rate, warehouse=None): if not frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) item = frappe.get_doc("Item", item_code) ... stock_reco = create_opening_stock_reconciliation(...) stock_reco.insert() ... stock_reco.submit() ``` **Guard (two layers):** - **Explicit check:** `frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code)` passes the document name as the third argument, so it's a **document-level write check** on that specific Item — it enforces both the doctype's write `DocPerm` and any User Permissions/share restrictions scoped to that item. Failing it raises `frappe.PermissionError`. - **Implicit check:** the Stock Reconciliation it creates (`create_opening_stock_reconciliation`, item.py:1699) is built with `frappe.get_doc({...})` and persisted via `stock_reco.insert()` / `stock_reco.submit()`, which pass through Frappe core's standard create/submit permission checks on the **Stock Reconciliation** doctype. So a user with Item write rights still can't create the opening stock unless they may also create/submit Stock Reconciliations. ## Summary | Whitelisted method | Guard | Permission checked | Exception raised | |---|---|---|---| | `get_item_attribute` | `frappe.has_permission("Item")` | Item: read (doctype-level) | generic `frappe.throw(_("No Permission"))` (ValidationError) | | `get_item_prices` | `frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read")` | Item Price: read (doctype-level) | `frappe.PermissionError` | | `make_opening_stock_entry` | `frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code)` | Item: write, **per-document** | `frappe.PermissionError`, plus core create/submit checks on Stock Reconciliation | In every case the pattern is the same: the whitelisted function cannot rely on the decorator for authorization, so the first statement (before any data is touched) performs the relevant `frappe.has_permission` check, and only then runs the raw `frappe.get_all`/`frappe.qb` query or document creation that would otherwise bypass row-level permission filtering.

final answer
I now have the complete picture. Here's the full answer: ## The three whitelisted endpoints and their guards All three live in `erpnext/stock/doctype/item/item.py` and are exposed with plain `@frappe.whitelist()` (no `allow_guest`), so they at minimum require an authenticated session — but each goes further with an explicit `frappe.has_permission` check as its first statement. ### 1. Attribute autocomplete — `get_item_attribute` (item.py:1525–1535) Called from `item.js:1482` for the Attributes child-table autocomplete. ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_attribute(parent: str, attribute_value: str = ""): """Used for providing auto-completions in child table.""" if not frappe.has_permission("Item"): frappe.throw(_("No Permission")) ``` - `frappe.has_permission("Item")` defaults to `ptype="read"`, so any user with read access to the **Item** doctype passes. - Notably it checks **Item**, not `Item Attribute Value` — child-table DocTypes have no independent permission model, so the check is anchored on the parent doctype the user is already editing. Data access is also scoped to `parent` (the Item Attribute linked to the item). ### 2. Item price previews — `get_item_prices` (item.py:1588–1623) Called from `render_item_prices` in `item.js:860` to populate the prices tab. ```python if not frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read"): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` - Requires explicit `read` permission on the **Item Price** doctype (a different doctype than the one the form is rendering), and raises `frappe.PermissionError`, which the framework maps to HTTP 403. - Mirrored client-side in `item.js:847`: `render_item_prices` first checks `frappe.model.can_read("Item Price")` and hides the `prices_html` section entirely if false — but that's only cosmetic; the server throw is the authoritative guard. ### 3. Opening stock creation — `make_opening_stock_entry` (item.py:1626–1696) Called from `show_opening_stock_dialog` in `item.js:1000` when the "Set Opening Stock" dialog is saved. It has two layers of protection: ```python if not frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` - This is a **document-level** write check — the third positional argument of `frappe.has_permission` is the `doc`, so both role-based Item permissions and per-document sharing rules are enforced against the specific item being modified. - After the guard, it validates business preconditions (`is_stock_item`, not serial/batch-tracked, `item.stock_ledger_created()` is false, qty > 0, valuation rate ≥ 0, warehouse belongs to the company). - **Implicit second layer:** `create_opening_stock_reconciliation` (item.py:1699–1730) performs a plain `stock_reco.insert()` followed by `stock_reco.submit()` — no `ignore_permissions` flag — so the user must additionally hold **create** and **submit** permission on **Stock Reconciliation**, or the insert itself raises `PermissionError`. - Client-side mirror in `item.js:205–216`: the "Set Opening Stock" button is only rendered when `frappe.model.can_create("Stock Entry") && frappe.model.can_write("Stock Entry")` and `__onload.stock_exists` is falsy — again, UI gating only. ### Related endpoint (same pattern) The stock-level dashboard on the same form calls `erpnext/stock/dashboard/item_dashboard.py::get_data` (item.js:836), which uses the same idiom but degrades gracefully instead of throwing: `if not frappe.has_permission("Bin", "read"): return []` (item_dashboard.py:20–21). **In summary:** each endpoint re-validates server-side rather than trusting the client — autocomplete checks read on `Item`, price preview checks read on `Item Price` (cross-doctype), and opening-stock creation checks doc-level write on the specific `Item` plus, transitively, create/submit on `Stock Reconciliation` through a non-bypassed `insert()`/`submit()`. The JS-side `can_read`/`can_create`/`can_write` checks merely hide the UI affordances.

I have everything needed. All three whitelisted endpoints live in `erpnext/stock/doctype/item/item.py`, and each opens with an explicit `frappe.has_permission(...)` gate before touching the database — necessary because the queries underneath use permission-bypassing APIs (`frappe.get_all` / `frappe.qb`). ## 1. Attribute autocomplete — `get_item_attribute` (item.py:1525–1535) Called from `item.js:1483` while filling the Item Variant attribute child table. ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_attribute(parent: str, attribute_value: str = ""): """Used for providing auto-completions in child table.""" if not frappe.has_permission("Item"): frappe.throw(_("No Permission")) ``` - Guard: `frappe.has_permission("Item")` with no `ptype`, which defaults to **read** permission on the **Item** doctype. Only users who can read Items may fetch the list of `Item Attribute Value` child-table rows (which would otherwise leak variant attribute options). - Note the query itself is `frappe.get_all("Item Attribute Value", ...)`, which ignores permissions — so this early `frappe.throw(_("No Permission"))` is the *only* barrier. (Minor stylistic difference: it throws the generic ValidationError rather than `frappe.PermissionError`.) ## 2. Item price preview — `get_item_prices` (item.py:1588–1623) Called from `item.js:861` to populate the "Item Prices" tab. ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_prices(item_code: str): """Fetch valid item prices for the item prices tab.""" if not frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read"): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` - Guard: **read** permission on the **Item Price** doctype — deliberately *not* just `Item`, because being able to view an Item doesn't imply the right to see its price lists/rates (price lists can be restricted per role). - It throws `frappe.PermissionError`, so the client gets a proper 403-style permission error. The subsequent `frappe.qb` select over `Item Price` runs with no permission filtering, so this check is again the sole gate. ## 3. Opening stock creation — `make_opening_stock_entry` (item.py:1626–1696) Called from `item.js:1001` for the "Set Opening Stock (Qty / Valuation)" action on a stock Item. ```python @frappe.whitelist() def make_opening_stock_entry(item_code, company, qty, valuation_rate, warehouse=None): if not frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` - Guard: **write** permission on **Item**, and passed `item_code` as the third argument, so it's a **document-level** check (`frappe.has_permission(doctype, ptype, doc=name)`) — user-specific Item permissions apply, not just role-level doctype access. It also raises `frappe.PermissionError`. - This is a write path, so it has **layered** enforcement: 1. The explicit Item-write check above (validates the item is a stock item, not serial/batch, no existing stock ledger, valid qty/valuation, warehouse belongs to the company). 2. `create_opening_stock_reconciliation()` (item.py:1699) then does `stock_reco.insert()` and `stock_reco.submit()` on a **Stock Reconciliation** doc — the Frappe framework itself re-runs `create`/`write`/`submit` permission checks for that doctype during insert/submit, so a user lacking Stock Reconciliation rights is blocked there too even if they passed the Item check. ## Summary | Endpoint | Guard | Scope | |---|---|---| | `get_item_attribute` | `frappe.has_permission("Item")` | read on Item doctype | | `get_item_prices` | `frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read")` + `PermissionError` | read on Item Price doctype | | `make_opening_stock_entry` | `frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code)` + `PermissionError` | write on the *specific* Item document, plus framework checks on the Stock Reconciliation insert/submit | The common pattern: because these whitelisted methods query data directly with permission-bypassing APIs (`frappe.get_all`, `frappe.qb.from_`) or create subsidiary documents, each must open with its own `frappe.has_permission` check — read on Item, read on Item Price, and document-level write on the Item (with the Stock Reconciliation's own permissions providing the second line of defense for opening stock).

final answer
## Summary All three auxiliary-data endpoints live in `erpnext/stock/doctype/item/item.py` and are called from `erpnext/stock/doctype/item/item.js`. Each whitelisted function performs its own explicit server-side permission check up front (unlike some other whitelisted helpers in the same file, e.g. `get_item_details` / `get_uom_conv_factor` / `get_asset_naming_series`, which have none and rely on framework defaults). ### 1. Attribute autocomplete — `get_item_attribute(parent, attribute_value)` `item.py:1525–1535`, called from the Awesomplete autocomplete in the variant-attributes dialog (`item.js:1482–1487`). ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_attribute(parent: str, attribute_value: str = ""): if not frappe.has_permission("Item"): frappe.throw(_("No Permission")) ``` - Guard: `frappe.has_permission("Item")` with no `ptype` argument — this defaults to **`"read"`**, so it requires read permission on the **Item** doctype and raises a generic "No Permission" otherwise. - Note it checks **Item**, not the `Item Attribute Value` child doctype it actually queries; the query itself is scoped to `parent` (the attribute name), and anyone legitimately using the variant dialog must already be able to read the Item. ### 2. Item price preview — `get_item_prices(item_code)` `item.py:1588–1623`, called by `render_item_prices` for the prices tab (`item.js:860–862`). ```python @frappe.whitelist() def get_item_prices(item_code: str): if not frappe.has_permission("Item Price", "read"): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` - Guard: an explicit **`"read"`** check against the **`Item Price`** doctype (deliberately *not* `Item` — the sensitive data being exposed is prices), raising `frappe.PermissionError`. - The client mirrors this: `render_item_prices` (`item.js:844–851`) hides the `prices_html` section and skips the call entirely unless `frappe.model.can_read("Item Price")`. The client check is only UX; the server-side `frappe.has_permission` is the authoritative barrier. ### 3. Opening stock creation — `make_opening_stock_entry(item_code, company, qty, valuation_rate, warehouse=None)` `item.py:1626–1696`, invoked by the "Add Opening Stock" dialog's primary action (`item.js:1000–1008`). ```python @frappe.whitelist() def make_opening_stock_entry(...): if not frappe.has_permission("Item", "write", item_code): frappe.throw(_("Not permitted"), frappe.PermissionError) ``` - Guard: a **`"write"`** permission check on **the specific Item document** — the third argument (`doc=item_code`) means Frappe applies document-level permission checks (user permissions, company restrictions, etc.), not just doctype-level write. - This is the strongest of the three because the endpoint *writes*: after the guard it creates and submits a **Stock Reconciliation** (`create_opening_stock_reconciliation`, `item.py:1699–1730` calls `stock_reco.insert()` then `stock_reco.submit()`). Frappe's `Document.insert()`/`submit()` enforce `create`/`submit` permission on Stock Reconciliation themselves, so a user with Item write but no Stock Reconciliation rights is still blocked there. The function then layers business validation on top: item must be a stock item, must not be serial/batch tracked (those must go through the Stock Reconciliation form), no prior stock ledger entries (`item.stock_ledger_created()`), `qty > 0`, non-negative `valuation_rate`, and the chosen warehouse must belong to the given company. ### The shared pattern All three follow the same idiom: since `@frappe.whitelist()` makes a method callable by any authenticated session directly via `/api/method/...`, each endpoint begins with an explicit `frappe.has_permission(...)` check and `frappe.throw(...)` before touching data — with the permission target matched to what the call actually reads or mutates: | Endpoint | Guard | Scope | |---|---|---| | `get_item_attribute` | `has_permission("Item")` (read by default) | doctype-level read on Item | | `get_item_prices` | `has_permission("Item Price", "read")` | doctype-level read on Item Price | | `make_opening_stock_entry` | `has_permission("Item", "write", item_code)` | doc-level write on the Item, plus framework `create`/`submit` checks on Stock Reconciliation downstream |

final answer
I've now traced the full mechanism. Here's the complete picture. ## The short answer ERPNext keeps the promise in a **Stock Reservation Entry (SRE)** that names the exact Sales Order (and even the exact serial numbers/batches) the stock is promised to, rolls it up into two counters on the **Bin** (`reserved_qty` from open Sales Orders and `reserved_stock` from SREs), computes "free to promise" as `projected_qty` / `available_qty_to_reserve`, and enforces it in the **stock ledger** and in the **serial-and-batch picking** logic so an unrelated voucher simply cannot post against those units. ## 1. Where the promise is recorded **`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reservation_entry/stock_reservation_entry.py`** — the hard promise. When a Sales Order is submitted with `reserve_stock` checked (requires *Enable Stock Reservation* in Stock Settings), `SalesOrder.on_submit` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:470`) calls `SalesOrderStockReservation.create_stock_reservation_entries()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py`), which delegates to `create_stock_reservation_entries_for_so_items()` in the SRE module. Each SRE stores: - `voucher_type` / `voucher_no` / `voucher_detail_no` — e.g. the exact *Sales Order Item* row it's promised to, - `item_code`, `warehouse`, `reserved_qty`, `delivered_qty`, `transferred_qty`, `consumed_qty`, - for serial/batch items, child rows `sb_entries` (`Serial and Batch Entry`) pinning the **specific serial nos / batches** to that order (`auto_reserve_serial_and_batch()`, `validate_reservation_based_on_serial_and_batch()`), - status via `StockReservationEntry.update_status()` (Draft → Partially Reserved → Reserved → Partially Delivered → Delivered/Closed). Pick Lists, Work Orders, Production Plans and Subcontracting Orders get SREs via the `StockReservation` helper class (`make_stock_reservation_entries()`, `transfer_reservation_entries_to()`) in the same file. **`erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py`** — the aggregated counters: - `Bin.reserved_qty` — soft promise, recomputed from *all open Sales Orders* by `get_reserved_qty()` in `erpnext/stock/stock_balance.py` (sums `qty − delivered_qty` of submitted, non-"On Hold"/"Closed", not-delivered-by-supplier SO items, incl. Packed Items for bundles). Refreshed on SO submit/cancel by `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty()` → `update_bin_qty(..., {"reserved_qty": get_reserved_qty(...)})`. - `Bin.reserved_stock` — hard promise from SREs: `Bin.update_reserved_stock()` calls `get_sre_reserved_qty_for_item_and_warehouse()` in the SRE module. ## 2. How "still available to promise" is calculated - **`Bin.set_projected_qty()`** (bin.py) — the standard ATP: `projected_qty = actual_qty + ordered_qty + indented_qty + planned_qty − reserved_qty − reserved_qty_for_production − reserved_qty_for_sub_contract − reserved_qty_for_production_plan`. This is what stock balance reports/dashboards (`erpnext/stock/report/stock_balance`, `erpnext/stock/dashboard/item_dashboard.py`) show. - **`get_available_qty_to_reserve(item_code, warehouse)`** (SRE module) — SRE-level ATP: `get_stock_balance()` (erpnext/stock/utils.py) minus the outstanding Σ(`reserved_qty − delivered_qty − transferred_qty − consumed_qty`) of other SREs, executed **`FOR UPDATE`** (with explicit Bin-row/SRE row locking on both MariaDB and Postgres) so two concurrent reservations can't over-commit. - **`StockReservationEntry.validate_with_allowed_qty()`** caps one more reservation per order row at `min(available_qty, voucher_qty − delivered_qty − already reserved for this row)`. - For serial/batch items: `get_available_serial_nos_to_reserve()` subtracts serials already held by other SREs; batch-level is `get_batch_qty(...) / get_available_batches(...)` minus SRE holds. - On the order side, `get_unreserved_qty()` (sales_order/services/reservation.py) = `stock_qty − delivered_qty − already-reserved` per row. ## 3. How it stops an unrelated shipment from taking that stock 1. **Stock ledger hard stop** — `make_sl_entries()` in **`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`** loads `Bin.reserved_stock` into the SLE args (line 161). During valuation, `update_entries_after.validate_negative_stock()` (line 1352) computes `qty_after_transaction + actual_qty − reserved_stock` and flags anything negative; `raise_exceptions()` (line 1833) then raises `NegativeStockError` with the explicit message *"As X units are reserved for other sales orders, you are allowed to consume only Y units."* `validate_reserved_stock()` (line 2470) blocks independently when balance − reserved_stock < 0. So **even with "Allow Negative Stock" enabled**, an unrelated delivery note/stock entry cannot post the reserved units. 2. **Auto-picking skips reserved stock** — when an unrelated voucher auto-selects stock: `get_available_serial_nos()` (serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2422) drops serial numbers held by SREs of *other* vouchers (`get_reserved_serial_nos_for_sre`, `get_other_doc_reserved_serials`) but keeps the ones reserved for *its own* SO (`get_reserved_serial_nos_for_voucher`, using `get_reserved_voucher_details()` to map a Delivery Note row to its `against_sales_order`). For batches, `get_auto_batch_nos()` (line 2971) subtracts `get_reserved_batches_for_sre()` (line 2921) from available batch quantities. 3. **Manual picks are validated** — `SerialAndBatchBundle.validate_serial_nos_inventory()` (line 269, via `get_serial_no_reservation()`) throws *"Serial No … is reserved for Sales Order X via SRE"*; `SerialBatchBundleService.validate_reserved_batches()` (erpnext/stock/services/serial_batch_bundle_service.py:587, invoked from `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:217`) raises a *"Reserved Batch Conflict"* when an outward bundle would leave a batch below its outstanding SRE reservations (own vouchers excluded). 4. **Warehouse pinning** — `DeliveryNote.validate_against_stock_reservation_entries()` (erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:544) forces the DN to ship from a warehouse listed in `get_sre_reserved_warehouses_for_voucher()`. 5. **Redemption, not double-spend** — on DN submit, `SellingController.update_stock_reservation_entries()` (erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:930) consumes the SRE (bumps `delivered_qty`, marks serial/batch entries delivered via `update_serial_batch_delivered_qty()`), then `update_status()` + `update_reserved_stock_in_bin()` release the hold; the DN's `on_submit` deliberately runs `update_stock_ledger()` **after** SO `delivered_qty` is updated so `Bin.reserved_qty` reflects the delivered units. 6. **Guards against back doors** — `StockReconciliation.validate_reserved_stock()` (erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reconciliation/stock_reconciliation.py:829, called at lines 99/185) refuses to adjust/reconcile stock that has SRE holds, and `validate_reserved_entries()` stops cancelling an SRE already used in a work order. So a customer-promised unit is visible to everyone (`Bin.reserved_qty`/`reserved_stock` → reduced `projected_qty`), claimable only by its own voucher (SRE `voucher_no` + pinned serials/batches), and physically un-takeable by anyone else thanks to the reserved-stock-aware negative-stock check in `stock_ledger.py`.

final answer
I now have the complete picture. Here's how ERPNext handles "this stock is promised to customer X": ## The promise is recorded in the **Stock Reservation Entry (SRE)** **File: `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reservation_entry/stock_reservation_entry.py`** The SRE is a submittable doctype that binds a specific warehouse's stock to a specific voucher row: - `voucher_type` = `"Sales Order"`, `voucher_no` (the SO, which carries the customer), `voucher_detail_no` (the exact SO Item row), plus `item_code`, `warehouse`, `reserved_qty`, `delivered_qty`, `transferred_qty`, `consumed_qty`, `status`, and — for serial/batch items — `reservation_based_on = "Serial and Batch"` with child `Serial and Batch Entry` rows (`sb_entries`). Creation chain: - `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:470-471`) → `SalesOrder.create_stock_reservation_entries()` → `SalesOrderStockReservation.create_stock_reservation_entries()` in **`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py:76`** → module function `create_stock_reservation_entries_for_so_items()` (`stock_reservation_entry.py:1606`). It only runs for SO rows with `reserve_stock` checked, requires Stock Settings → `enable_stock_reservation`, skips non-stock/group warehouses, and computes `qty_to_be_reserved = min(unreserved_qty, available_qty_to_reserve)`. It's also called from Pick List (`PickList.create_stock_reservation_entries`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/pick_list/pick_list.py:498`) and Purchase Receipt. - On submit, `StockReservationEntry.on_submit()` (line 93) runs `update_reserved_qty_in_voucher()` (keeps the SO row's `stock_reserved_qty` in sync), `update_status()`, and `update_reserved_stock_in_bin()`. There is also a **soft** layer: `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty()` (`reservation.py:35-58`) calls `get_reserved_qty(item_code, warehouse)` in **`erpnext/stock/stock_balance.py:89-147`**, which sums outstanding qty (`stock_qty − delivered_qty`, minus `returned_qty` if *Don't Reserve SO Qty on Sales Return*) across **all open Sales Orders** for that item+warehouse (including Product Bundle/Packed Items), and writes it into `Bin.reserved_qty` via `update_bin_qty()` (stock_balance.py:274). This is the "reserved for sales orders" figure on the Bin, not customer-specific. ## How "still available to promise" is calculated - **Hard (SRE) ATP:** `get_available_qty_to_reserve(item_code, warehouse, batch_no, ignore_sre)` (`stock_reservation_entry.py:693-746`) = `get_stock_balance(...)` (from `erpnext/stock/utils.py:99`, i.e., last SLE's `qty_after_transaction`) **minus** `Sum(reserved_qty − delivered_qty − transferred_qty − consumed_qty)` over submitted SREs where `delivered_qty < reserved_qty`. The aggregate is taken under `FOR UPDATE` row locks so two concurrent reservations can't both claim the same stock. Per-batch it delegates to `get_batch_qty`. The result snapshot is stored on each SRE as `available_qty`. - **Per-voucher cap:** `StockReservationEntry.validate_with_allowed_qty()` (line 574) enforces `Allowed Qty = min(Available Qty To Reserve, Voucher Qty − Delivered Qty − Total Reserved Qty)` and throws *"Cannot reserve more than Allowed Qty…"* otherwise; `validate_reservation_based_on_serial_and_batch()` (line 344) does the same per serial/batch (*"…might be reserved in another Stock Reservation Entry"*). - **Reported ATP:** `Bin.set_projected_qty()` in **`erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py:66-76`**: `projected_qty = actual_qty + ordered_qty + indented_qty + planned_qty − reserved_qty − reserved_qty_for_production − reserved_qty_for_sub_contract − reserved_qty_for_production_plan`. SRE reservations additionally surface in the Stock Balance report via `StockBalanceReport.get_sre_reserved_qty_details`. ## How an unrelated shipment is stopped The enforcement happens when the stock ledger is posted, keyed off **`Bin.reserved_stock`** (distinct from `reserved_qty`): 1. `StockReservationEntry.update_reserved_stock_in_bin()` → `Bin.update_reserved_stock()` (`bin.py:217-226`) → `get_sre_reserved_qty_for_item_and_warehouse()` (`stock_reservation_entry.py:803`) keeps `Bin.reserved_stock` = Σ(reserved − delivered − transferred − consumed) of open SREs. 2. When an outbound SLE is processed, `StockLedgerEntry.get_reserved_stock()` (**`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:631-648`**) loads that outstanding reserved amount, and `repost_current_voucher` copies `Bin.reserved_stock` into the args (`stock_ledger.py:160-161, 190`). 3. `validate_negative_qty_in_future_sle()` (`stock_ledger.py:2355`) calls **`validate_reserved_stock(args)`** (`stock_ledger.py:2470-2484`) — if `stock_balance − reserved_stock < 0`, it throws with title **"Reserved Stock"**: *"N units of Item needed in Warehouse … to complete this transaction"*. The negative-stock error is likewise reworded at lines 1860-1868: *"As X units are reserved for other sales orders, you are allowed to consume only Y units."* So a Delivery Note / Stock Entry / POS shipment **not tied to the reserved SO** physically cannot post past the reserved quantity. 4. Serial/batch items get per-unit protection: `SerialBatchBundleService.validate_reserved_batches()` (**`erpnext/stock/services/serial_batch_bundle_service.py:587`**) collects the negative (outbound) batch rows of a Delivery Note/Sales Invoice/Stock Entry, excludes batches whose SRE `voucher_no` is among the doc's **own** references (`against_sales_order`, `sales_order`, `work_order`…), and throws if the batch's free qty can't cover other vouchers' outstanding reservations. Companions: `get_sre_reserved_serial_nos_details` / `get_sre_reserved_batch_nos_details` (`stock_reservation_entry.py:956/984`) feeding `validate_reserved_serial_nos` / `validate_reserved_batch_nos` (`stock_ledger.py:2487/2503`), and `get_available_serial_nos` + `get_reserved_serial_nos_for_sre` / `get_reserved_voucher_details` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/serial_and_batch_bundle/serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2642-2815` exclude reserved serials from auto-picking. 5. Only the **matching** customer shipment draws down the promise: `SellingController.update_stock_reservation_entries()` (**`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:938-1104`**) matches DN items by `against_sales_order` + `so_detail`, consumes SREs FIFO (`delivered_qty += min(reserved − delivered, qty_to_deliver)` or per serial/batch entry), then updates status and `Bin.reserved_stock`; on cancel it reverses. The "Reserve" flow on `make_delivery_note` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/mapper.py:235-245, 344-366`) prefills rows using `get_sre_reserved_qty_details_for_voucher()` / `get_sre_details_for_voucher()` (`stock_reservation_entry.py:859/1016`). 6. Side doors are also closed: `StockReconciliation.validate_reserved_stock()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reconciliation/stock_reconciliation.py:829-870`) blocks any Stock Reconciliation that would reduce stock carrying open SREs; cancelling the SO cancels its SREs (`SalesOrder.on_cancel → cancel_stock_reservation_entries`, sales_order.py:497). The guarantee is literally captured in the test `TestStockReservationEntry.test_reserved_stock_cannot_be_delivered_against_a_different_sales_order` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reservation_entry/test_stock_reservation_entry.py:362`). **In short:** the promise lives in `Stock Reservation Entry` rows (customer promise = SO row + warehouse + reserved serials/batches), "still available to promise" = stock balance minus outstanding SRE qty (`get_available_qty_to_reserve`) and, at report level, `Bin.projected_qty = actual + ordered + indented + planned − reserved…`, and unrelated shipments are stopped at SLE posting time by `validate_reserved_stock` (plus batch/serial guards), which refuses to let the balance drop below the quantity reserved for other vouchers.

final answer
## How ERPNext "promises" stock to a customer and fences it off ### 1. Where the promise is recorded — the Stock Reservation Entry (SRE) The promise is a **Stock Reservation Entry** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reservation_entry/stock_reservation_entry.py`). One SRE row records: `voucher_type/voucher_no/voucher_detail_no` (the owning **Sales Order** and its item row), `item_code`, `warehouse`, `reserved_qty`, plus how much has since left: `delivered_qty`, `transferred_qty`, `consumed_qty`, and a `status` (Reserved → Partially Delivered → Delivered/Closed). For serial/batch items (`reservation_based_on = "Serial and Batch"`) it also pins exact serial nos/batches via child `sb_entries`. The feature is gated by `Stock Settings → enable_stock_reservation`; `validate_stock_reservation_settings()` (L675) currently allows reservations **only against Sales Orders**. The creation path: - `SalesOrder.validate()` → `SalesOrderStockReservation.validate_reserved_stock()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` L229; class in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py` L18). `enable_auto_reserve_stock()` turns on "Reserve Stock" per order/item (Stock Settings `auto_reserve_stock`). - `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (L450) → `create_stock_reservation_entries()` (L471) → `SalesOrderStockReservation.create_stock_reservation_entries()` (reservation.py L76) → `create_stock_reservation_entries_for_so_items()` (stock_reservation_entry.py L1606), which computes what's still unreserved via `get_unreserved_qty()` (reservation.py L147: `stock_qty − delivered_qty×conversion_factor − already reserved`) and creates/submits SREs through `StockReservation.make_stock_reservation_entries()` (L1164). Product-bundle components go through `_reserve_packed_items()`. - On submit, `StockReservationEntry.update_reserved_stock_in_bin()` (L523) → `Bin.update_reserved_stock()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py` L217) → `get_sre_reserved_qty_for_item_and_warehouse()` (L803), which stores the live reserved total into **`Bin.reserved_stock`**. ### 2. How "still available to promise" is calculated - **`get_available_qty_to_reserve()`** (stock_reservation_entry.py L693; same logic as the method `StockReservation.get_available_qty_to_reserve()` L1270): `get_stock_balance(item_code, warehouse)` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py` L99) **minus** `Sum(reserved_qty − delivered_qty − transferred_qty − consumed_qty)` over submitted SREs where `delivered_qty < reserved_qty`. Note the `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` locking of the Bin row and SRE rows (L718–739) — two concurrent reservations can't both claim the same free stock. - Serial/batch equivalent: `get_available_serial_nos_to_reserve()` (L749); remaining reserved details per voucher: `get_sre_reserved_qty_details_for_voucher()` (L859), surfaced on the SO by `SalesOrderStockReservation.has_unreserved_stock()`. - The old-style projection (before SREs / shown in item dashboards) is still computed by `get_reserved_qty()` in `erpnext/stock/stock_balance.py` (L89) — the undelivered qty of open Sales Order Items (incl. Packed Items) — written to `Bin.reserved_qty` by `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty()` → `update_bin_qty()`. ### 3. How an unrelated shipment is stopped from taking the stock When **any** outgoing stock transaction posts SLEs, `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`: - loads `args.reserved_stock` from the Bin (L160–161) and, during ledger rebuild, `StockLedgerQuantityTree`-style state sets `self.reserved_stock = self.get_reserved_stock()` (L622, query at L631–648 summing active SREs at posting time); - **`validate_negative_stock()`** (L1352) computes `diff = qty_after_transaction + actual_qty − reserved_stock`. If the shipment would push the *un-reserved* balance below zero, `raise_exceptions()` (L1833) throws `NegativeStockError`, appending the explicit message: *"As X units are reserved for other sales orders, you are allowed to consume only Y units"* (L1860–1868); - `validate_negative_qty_in_future_sle()` (L2355) additionally calls **`validate_reserved_stock()`** (L2470), which throws the dedicated **"Reserved Stock"** error when `get_stock_balance() − Bin.reserved_stock < 0`. (Serial-no and batch-level analogues: `validate_reserved_serial_nos()` L2487 and `validate_reserved_batch_nos()` L2503, backed by `get_sre_reserved_serial_nos_details()`/`get_sre_reserved_batch_nos_details()`.) The reserved order's **own** delivery is not blocked because `DeliveryNote.on_submit()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py` L507) calls `update_stock_reservation_entries()` — implemented in `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py` L930 — **before** `update_stock_ledger()` (L511). That method walks the SREs of the referenced SO rows and increments `sre_doc.delivered_qty` up to `reserved_qty − delivered_qty` (L1023–1029), updates status and refreshes `Bin.reserved_stock`, thereby releasing this order's own floor. On cancel it reverses the delivered qty (L1039–1104). `Sales Invoice` with *Update Stock* does the same (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py` L452/L542). So: an unrelated Delivery Note for the same item/warehouse doesn't touch any SRE; the Bin still shows the other customer's reserved qty, and the ledger validation refuses the outgoing qty that would eat into it — while delivery against the reserving order passes because its own SRE is consumed first. **Supporting surfaces:** the `Reserved Stock` report (`erpnext/stock/report/reserved_stock/reserved_stock.py`), Item Dashboard reserved-stock details (`erpnext/stock/dashboard/item_dashboard.py` L84), and `bin_details` in `erpnext/stock/get_item_details.py` (L1547) showing `reserved_qty`. The same SRE machinery is reused for supply-side reservations via `PurchaseReceiptStockReservation` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/reservation.py`) and Work Orders (`erpnext/manufacturing/doctype/work_order/services/reservation.py`).

final answer
All the pieces are confirmed. Here's how ERPNext tracks "promised to a customer" stock end‑to‑end. ## 1. Where the promise is recorded There are two layers, both keyed on the **Sales Order**: **a) Implicit promise — `Bin.reserved_qty` (every open SO reserves stock automatically)** When a Sales Order is submitted, `SalesOrder.on_submit` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450`) calls `SalesOrder.update_reserved_qty` (`sales_order.py:544`), which delegates to `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py:35`. That collects distinct (item, warehouse) pairs from `items` (or `packed_items` for product bundles) and calls: - `update_bin_qty(item_code, warehouse, {"reserved_qty": get_reserved_qty(item_code, warehouse)})` — `erpnext/stock/stock_balance.py:274` and `get_reserved_qty` at `stock_balance.py:89`. `get_reserved_qty` is the actual "promise ledger": it sums `qty − delivered_qty` (minus `returned_qty` if Selling Settings `dont_reserve_sales_order_qty_on_sales_return` is set) over **submitted Sales Order Items** whose SO status is not `On Hold`/`Closed`, prorated by `stock_qty/qty`, skipping drop‑ship (`delivered_by_supplier`) rows — plus a parallel aggregate over `Packed Item` for bundles. The result lands in the **Bin** doctype (`erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py`), one Bin row per (item_code, warehouse). The same `get_reserved_qty` is used on reposts (`repost_stock`, `stock_balance.py:40`) and manual recalculation (`Bin.recalculate_qty`, `bin.py:40`). **b) Explicit promise — the `Stock Reservation Entry` doctype** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_reservation_entry/stock_reservation_entry.py`), used when Stock Settings `enable_stock_reservation` is on and the SO item has `reserve_stock` (or `auto_reserve_stock`). `SalesOrderStockReservation.create_stock_reservation_entries` (`reservation.py:76`) creates SREs that can pin down a specific warehouse, batch, or serial number. On SRE submit, `update_reserved_qty_in_voucher` writes `Sales Order Item.stock_reserved_qty`, and `update_reserved_stock_in_bin` (`SRE:523`) → `Bin.update_reserved_stock` (`bin.py:217`) → `get_sre_reserved_qty_for_item_and_warehouse` refreshes `Bin.reserved_stock`. On delivery, `DeliveryNote.on_submit`/`on_cancel` → `update_stock_reservation_entries` bumps SRE `delivered_qty` (SREs move to `Partially Delivered`/`Delivered` via `update_status`, SRE:530). ## 2. How "still available to promise" is computed - **`Bin.set_projected_qty`** (`bin.py:66`): `projected_qty = actual_qty + ordered_qty + indented_qty + planned_qty − reserved_qty − reserved_qty_for_production − reserved_qty_for_sub_contract − reserved_qty_for_production_plan`. So the open‑SO promise is subtracted from on‑hand plus incoming supply. The incremental form is in `update_qty` (`bin.py:251`), called from `update_bin_qty`; `get_projected_qty` (`erpnext/stock/get_item_details.py:1535`) exposes it to the UI. - **Reservable quantity for an SRE**: `get_available_qty_to_reserve` (`stock_reservation_entry.py:693` and method at `1270`) = `get_stock_balance` (actual qty from the Stock Ledger, `erpnext/stock/utils.py:99`) − Σ SRE `reserved_qty − delivered_qty − transferred_qty − consumed_qty`. `validate_with_allowed_qty` (SRE:574) caps a new reservation at `min(available, voucher_qty − already_delivered − already_reserved)` and throws *"Item X is already reserved/delivered against Sales Order Y"* if you over‑reserve. - **Batch/serial granularity**: `get_auto_batch_nos` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/serial_and_batch_bundle/serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2971`) subtracts `get_reserved_batches_for_sre` (line 2921), `get_reserved_batches_for_pos` (2844) and pick‑list batches via `update_available_batches` (3132) from raw batch balances; `get_batch_qty(..., ignore_reserved_stock=...)` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/batch/batch.py:235`) does the same for reporting. Pick List availability comes from `get_available_item_locations*` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/pick_list/pick_list.py:1041+`). ## 3. How an unrelated shipment is kept off the reserved stock - **Batch/serial items — hard block.** When a Delivery Note/POS invoice auto‑picks stock, `SerialBatchCreation.set_auto_serial_batch_entries_for_outward` (`erpnext/stock/serial_batch_bundle.py:1245`) pulls from `get_available_batches` / `get_serial_nos_for_outward`, which route through `get_auto_batch_nos` and the serial filter at `serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2445‑2468`: quantities/serial numbers held by an SRE for another voucher are removed from the candidate pool (`get_reserved_serial_nos_for_sre`, `get_other_doc_reserved_serials`), and `get_reserved_serial_nos_for_voucher` (2753) only surfaces serials reserved for *your* voucher. If someone forces the wrong serial, `validate_serial_no_warehouse` (line ~262‑326) throws `SerialNoWarehouseError`: *"Serial No … is reserved for {voucher} {no} via Stock Reservation Entry … Please use an unreserved serial number."* - **Delivery Note warehouse — validated.** `DeliveryNote.validate` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:276`) calls `validate_against_stock_reservation_entries` (line 544/296): if the referenced SO item has SREs, `get_sre_reserved_warehouses_for_voucher` (SRE:881) returns the reserved warehouses and the DN either inherits one or **throws "Stock is reserved for item X in warehouse Y"** (`Stock Reservation Warehouse Mismatch`) if you pick another warehouse. - **Pick List — refuses to double‑promise.** A Pick List against an SO with existing reservations is blocked: *"Cannot create a pick list for Sales Order … because it has reserved stock"* (`pick_list.py:245‑260`); picking works off `stock_reserved_qty` fields that SREs maintain via `update_reserved_qty_in_pick_list` (SRE:497). - **The physical backstop — negative stock check.** Even for plain (non‑batch/serial) items, `Stock Ledger Entry.validate_negative_stock` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:1352`, invoked at line 1025) throws `NegativeStockError`/`Insufficient Stock` when an issue would drive actual qty below zero (unless "Allow Negative Stock"), so once only the promised goods remain in the bin, no unrelated shipment can post. - **Release on delivery.** When the SO's own shipment goes through, `SellingController.update_reserved_qty` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:492`, called from `update_stock_ledger` at line 676) re-runs the SO's reservation update after `delivered_qty` changes — `DeliveryNote.on_submit` even comments that `update_stock_ledger` must run *after* the status update "because updating reserved qty in bin depends upon updated delivered qty in SO" (`delivery_note.py:509‑511`) — shrinking `Bin.reserved_qty` so the stock stops counting as promised. **In short:** the promise lives in open `Sales Order Item` rows (rolled up into `Bin.reserved_qty` by `get_reserved_qty` in `erpnext/stock/stock_balance.py`) and, for explicit reservations, in `Stock Reservation Entry` (rolled up into `Bin.reserved_stock`); "available to promise" is `Bin.projected_qty` (`Bin.set_projected_qty`) or actual − SRE‑reserved (`get_available_qty_to_reserve`); and unrelated shipments are stopped by excluding reserved batches/serials from auto‑picking in `get_auto_batch_nos`, the SRE warehouse check in `DeliveryNote.validate_against_stock_reservation_entries`, the Pick List reservation guard, and finally the negative‑stock validation in `stock_ledger.py`.

final answer
## Short answer The whole "back‑solving" lives in `calculate_taxes_and_totals` — specifically **`determine_exclusive_rate()`** in `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py` (line 303), with its helper **`get_current_tax_fraction()`** (line 348) and **`_get_tax_rate()`** (line 384). It runs inside `_calculate()` (line 78–89) right after `calculate_item_values()`, and is mirrored client‑side in `erpnext/public/js/controllers/taxes_and_totals.js` (`determine_exclusive_rate`, line 254) so the form shows the same net rate while editing. ## How it works ### 1. Trigger and setup - The back‑calculation only runs if **any** tax row has `included_in_print_rate = 1` ("Include in Print Rate"), checked at line 304 (`if not any(cint(tax.included_in_print_rate) ...): return`). The entered `item.rate` / `item.amount` (`rate × qty` from `calculate_item_values`) is then treated as the **tax‑inclusive gross** for the line. - The effective rate per tax row comes from `_get_tax_rate()`: it prefers the per‑item **Item Tax Template** map (`item.item_tax_rate` JSON, loaded by `update_item_tax_map()` → `_load_item_tax_rate()`) keyed by account head, falling back to `tax.rate`. A row whose rate resolves to `NOT_APPLICABLE_TAX` contributes nothing. ### 2. The math (per item row, taxes iterated in order) For each item, every tax row produces a **fraction of the net (pre‑tax) amount**: ``` cumulated_tax_fraction = Σ tax_fraction_for_current_item item._unrounded_net_amount = (item.amount − total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty) / (1 + cumulated_tax_fraction) ``` (line 334–336). This works because each percentage tax equals `fᵢ × net`, so `gross = net × (1 + Σ fᵢ)`; inverting gives `net = gross / (1 + Σ fᵢ)`. Results land in `item.net_amount` / `item.net_rate` (and base currency via `_set_in_company_currency`), with the unrounded value cached in `item._unrounded_net_amount`. ### 3. Multiple inclusive taxes All inclusive rows contribute their fraction to `cumulated_tax_fraction` in a single pass (lines 312–327), and the division is done **once** at the end — there is no iterative "peel one tax at a time" loop. ### 4. Compounding tax rows Handled through two per‑row accumulators: - **"On Net Total"**: `f = rate/100`. - **"On Previous Row Amount"**: `f = (rate/100) × taxes[row_id−1].tax_fraction_for_current_item` — compounds on one prior row only. - **"On Previous Row Total"**: `f = (rate/100) × taxes[row_id−1].grand_total_fraction_for_current_item`, where `grand_total_fraction_for_current_item` is the running multiplier built along the way (`1 + f₀` for row 0; previous row's value + this row's fraction afterwards, lines 318–324). This correctly captures "net + all earlier taxes". Validation is in **`validate_inclusive_tax()`** (`erpnext/accounts/services/taxes.py`, line 298, called from `initialize_taxes()` at taxes_and_totals.py:259): an inclusive "Actual" row is rejected; an inclusive "On Previous Row Amount"/"On Previous Row Total" is rejected unless the referenced row(s) are also inclusive; "Valuation" category rows cannot be inclusive. ### 5. Per‑quantity taxes ("On Item Quantity") These are flat amounts per unit, not percentages, so they can't be a fraction of net. Instead `inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty = flt(tax_rate)` (line 376) is accumulated into `total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty` (× `item.qty`, line 327) and **subtracted from the gross line amount first** (`amount = item.amount − total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty`, line 334) before dividing by `1 + Σ fᵢ`. In the forward pass (`calculate_taxes` → `get_current_tax_and_net_amount`, line 626) such a row contributes `tax_rate × item.qty` and deliberately leaves `current_net_amount` at 0 so it doesn't pollute item‑wise taxable totals. ### 6. Deduction‑type taxes (purchase docs, `add_deduct_tax = "Deduct"`) In `get_current_tax_fraction` (lines 378–380) both the fraction and the per‑qty amount are **negated**, so a deducted inclusive tax shrinks the `(1 + Σ fᵢ)` divisor — i.e., it's backed out with the opposite sign. Downstream, `get_tax_amount_if_for_valuation_or_deduction()` (line 568) multiplies by −1 for Deduct rows on Purchase Order/Invoice/Receipt/Supplier Quotation and zeroes "Valuation"-category rows; `set_item_wise_tax()` (line 635) applies the same −1 multiplier for item‑wise breakup. ## Downstream reconciliation - In `get_current_tax_and_net_amount` (lines 609–615), inclusive "On Net Total" rows recompute their tax from `item._unrounded_net_amount` instead of the rounded `net_amount`, so the recomputed taxes sum back exactly to the inclusive gross with no rounding drift. - **`adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax()`** (line 700): since inclusive taxes are already inside `doc.total`, the last tax row's running `total` must equal `doc.total + non‑inclusive taxes`. Any residual within half a unit of `tax_amount` precision is kept as `grand_total_diff` (added back in `calculate_totals()`, line 731–735, and excluded from `total_taxes_and_charges`), so the customer still pays exactly the printed inclusive rates plus any genuinely extra taxes. - When a document‑level discount is applied, `determine_exclusive_rate` is skipped (`not self.discount_amount_applied` guard, line 330); `apply_discount_amount()` (line 857) distributes the discount proportionally over the already‑backed‑out `net_amount`s and re‑runs `_calculate()`. For "Apply Discount On: Grand Total", `get_total_for_discount_amount()` (line 914) computes the base as grand total minus Actual/qty taxes, and `grand_total_for_distributing_discount` includes the inclusive rounding diff (lines 726–729). Reference tests: `test_sales_invoice_with_discount_and_inclusive_tax`, `test_inclusive_tax_with_decimal_value_on_previous_row_amount(_non_inclusive)` and the zero‑decimal‑currency tests in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/test_sales_invoice.py` (lines 334–610).

I have the complete picture. Here's how ERPNext reverse-engineers pre-tax amounts from tax-inclusive prices. ## Where it happens The back-calculation lives in **`erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py`**, in two methods of the `calculate_taxes_and_totals` class: - **`determine_exclusive_rate()`** (lines 303–343) — the core reverse calculation, run per item row - **`get_current_tax_fraction(tax, item_tax_map)`** (lines 348–382) — computes each tax row's contribution as a *fraction* of the inclusive price It's invoked from the pipeline in `_calculate()` (lines 78–89), in this order: 1. `calculate_item_values()` — line 224: `item.amount = item.rate * item.qty`, where `rate` is the **tax-inclusive** rate, so `amount` is the gross (tax-laden) line total 2. `update_item_tax_map()` — line 142: loads the item's Item Tax Template into `item.item_tax_rate` (JSON of `account_head → rate`) 3. `initialize_taxes()` — line 254: zeroes per-row scratch fields and calls `validate_inclusive_tax()` (`erpnext/accounts/services/taxes.py:298`) to reject impossible configurations 4. **`determine_exclusive_rate()`** — overwrites `item.net_amount` / `item.net_rate` with the pre-tax values 5. `calculate_net_total()` → `calculate_taxes()` → `adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax()` (line 700) → `calculate_totals()` An identical mirror runs client-side for live form updates: **`erpnext/public/js/controllers/taxes_and_totals.js`** — `determine_exclusive_rate()` (254–298) and `get_current_tax_fraction()` (300–333), called from `_calculate_taxes_and_totals()` (line 107). Payment Entry has its own analog keyed on `included_in_paid_amount` instead of `included_in_print_rate`: `PaymentEntry.determine_exclusive_rate()` (`payment_entry.py:1486–1503`, computes `paid_amount_after_tax = base_paid_amount / (1 + cumulated_tax_fraction)`), mirrored in `payment_entry.js:1570`. ## The math `determine_exclusive_rate()` runs only if any tax row has **`included_in_print_rate`** checked (line 304). For each item it: 1. Walks the tax rows in order, asking `get_current_tax_fraction()` for each row's `tax_fraction_for_current_item` (fraction of the *net* amount the tax represents) and, for per-quantity taxes, an absolute `inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty`. 2. Builds a running **`grand_total_fraction_for_current_item`** per row: `row[i] = row[i-1] + tax_fraction[i]`, starting from `1 + fraction[0]` — i.e. the cumulative multiplier that turns net amount into grand total as of that row. 3. Sums everything into `cumulated_tax_fraction` and, for per-qty taxes, `total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty` (× `item.qty`). 4. Computes (lines 334–338): ``` amount = item.amount - total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty item._unrounded_net_amount = amount / (1 + cumulated_tax_fraction) item.net_amount = rounded(_unrounded_net_amount) item.net_rate = net_amount / qty ``` The unrounded value is deliberately kept on the item — `get_current_tax_and_net_amount()` (lines 610–615) later computes the inclusive tax row's own `tax_amount` from `item._unrounded_net_amount` instead of the rounded one, so the tax breakup and the back-derived net amount stay consistent and don't accumulate rounding drift. ## How each tax shape is handled in `get_current_tax_fraction()` - **Simple percentage ("On Net Total")**: `fraction = rate / 100`. Example: 110 incl. with 10% → `110 / 1.1 = 100`. - **Compounding tax rows**: - *"On Previous Row Amount"*: `fraction = (rate/100) × previous_row.tax_fraction_for_current_item` — tax computed on the previous row's tax alone. - *"On Previous Row Total"*: `fraction = (rate/100) × previous_row.grand_total_fraction_for_current_item` — tax on net + all prior taxes. Because the grand-total fraction chains cumulatively, a single division by `(1 + cumulated_tax_fraction)` at step 4 above exactly undoes the whole compounded chain in one shot (e.g. 10% + 5%-on-total → fractions 0.1 and 0.055 → net = amount / 1.155). - **Per-quantity taxes ("On Item Quantity")**: the rate is an absolute amount per unit, not a fraction, so it can't be divided out. Instead `inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty = flt(tax_rate)`; in `determine_exclusive_rate()` this is **subtracted** from the line amount first (`amount - per_qty × qty`), and only the remainder is divided by `(1 + cumulated_tax_fraction)` for the percentage taxes. The corresponding tax row amount is later just `tax_rate × item.qty` (`get_current_tax_and_net_amount`, line 626). - **Deduction-type taxes** (`add_deduct_tax == "Deduct"`, purchase-side charge rows): both the fraction and the per-qty amount are **negated** (lines 378–380). Subtracting a negative fraction means a Deduct inclusive row *increases* the derived pre-tax amount, mirroring how it reduces the payable total. In `calculate_taxes()`, `get_tax_amount_if_for_valuation_or_deduction()` (line 568) also flips the sign for Deduct rows (and zeroes out `category == "Valuation"` rows) when accumulating into document totals. ## Guards and edge cases - **`validate_inclusive_tax()`** (`erpnext/accounts/services/taxes.py:298`, called from `initialize_taxes()` line 259) enforces consistency: an *Actual* charge can never be inclusive (there's no rate to back out); an *"On Previous Row Amount"* tax can only be inclusive if the row it references is also inclusive; an *"On Previous Row Total"* tax requires **all rows above it** to be inclusive; and Valuation-category charges can't be inclusive. - **Item-specific rates**: `_get_tax_rate()` (lines 384–391) overrides the tax row's rate with the rate from the item's Item Tax Template map. If the template marks the account as `NOT_APPLICABLE_TAX` (`"N/A"`, defined in `erpnext/stock/get_item_details.py:41`), the fraction is 0 — that tax is treated as not embedded in the price for that item, so it neither reduces the net amount nor gets divided out. - **Discounts**: when `discount_amount_applied` is set (distributing a document-level discount on Grand Total), the back-calculation is skipped so it doesn't fight the discount pass; `discount_percentage` is also re-zeroed on the item (lines 339–341) since rate/discount fields no longer relate to the net rate. - **Grand total reconciliation**: since inclusive tax is already inside `doc.total` but the cumulative tax chain also adds it on top of `net_total`, `adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax()` (lines 700–729) computes `grand_total_diff = total + non_inclusive_taxes − last_tax.total`. The two expressions should agree exactly; any tiny residual (within the tax-amount precision) is kept as a rounding adjustment applied to `grand_total`, and `total_taxes_and_charges` is then reported as `grand_total − net_total − grand_total_diff`, which correctly includes both the inclusive and exclusive taxes.

I have the complete picture. Here's the full explanation. ## Where it happens The back-calculation lives in **`calculate_taxes_and_totals.determine_exclusive_rate()`** at `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py:303`, with its helper **`get_current_tax_fraction()`** at line 348. It runs inside the pipeline in `_calculate()` (line 78): ``` calculate_item_values() → initialize_taxes() → determine_exclusive_rate() → calculate_net_total() → calculate_taxes() → adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax() → calculate_totals() ``` Two parallel implementations exist and are kept line-for-line in sync: - **Client side**: `erpnext/public/js/controllers/taxes_and_totals.js:254` (`determine_exclusive_rate`, `get_current_tax_fraction` at :300) — so the form shows correct net rates live as the user types. - **Payment Entry**: `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_entry/payment_entry.py:1486` — a simpler variant keyed on `included_in_paid_amount` instead of `included_in_print_rate`, back-solving the whole `base_paid_amount` in one shot (no per-item loop, no per-qty taxes). **The input** is the gross line from `calculate_item_values()` (line 224): `item.amount = rate × qty`, where `rate` is the tax-inclusive price. At that point `net_rate`/`net_amount` still equal the gross values; `determine_exclusive_rate` is what rewrites them. The method exits immediately (line 304) unless any tax row has `included_in_print_rate` checked. ## The back-solve itself (lines 307–343) For each item, it walks the tax table **in order** and builds two accumulators via `get_current_tax_fraction()`: 1. **`cumulated_tax_fraction`** — sum of multiplicative fractions (rate/100 terms) 2. **`total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty × qty`** — sum of flat per-unit inclusive amounts Plus per-row state used for compounding: - `tax.tax_fraction_for_current_item` — this row's own fraction - `tax.grand_total_fraction_for_current_item` — running total: row 0 → `1 + f₀`; row *i* → previous row's value + `fᵢ`. This encodes "net + all taxes so far". Then the single formula (lines 334–338): ```python amount = flt(item.amount) - total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty # strip flat per-qty taxes item._unrounded_net_amount = amount / (1 + cumulated_tax_fraction) # divide out % taxes item.net_amount = flt(item._unrounded_net_amount, item.precision("net_amount")) item.net_rate = flt(item.net_amount / item.qty, ...) ``` (`base_net_rate`/`base_net_amount` follow via `_set_in_company_currency`, line 343.) ## How each case is handled **Multiple inclusive taxes** — every inclusive row contributes its fraction to *one* shared divisor `1 + Σfᵢ`, so any number of inclusive taxes is inverted in a single division. This works because each row's tax is defined against the net in the forward pass; e.g., 10% + 5% gives gross = net × (1 + 0.10 + 0.05), so net = gross ÷ 1.15. Each tax's individual amount is recovered later in the forward pass `calculate_taxes()` → `get_current_tax_and_net_amount()` (line 591), where "On Net Total" rows compute `rate × item.net_amount` — deliberately using the **unrounded** `_unrounded_net_amount` when the tax is inclusive (lines 609–617) to avoid double rounding. Exclusive (non-inclusive) rows contribute 0 fraction here; they're just added on top afterwards. **Compounding rows** ("On Previous Row Amount" / "On Previous Row Total") — handled inside `get_current_tax_fraction()` (lines 365–373): - *On Previous Row Amount*: `fraction = (rate/100) × previous_row.tax_fraction_for_current_item` → tax-on-tax as a % of the previous tax amount alone. - *On Previous Row Total*: `fraction = (rate/100) × previous_row.grand_total_fraction_for_current_item` → a % of net + all prior taxes. Because `grand_total_fraction` already folds prior compounding in, every row's fraction stays denominated in "per unit of net", so the simple `1 + Σf` divisor remains exact even for chained/compounded taxes. A guard makes this well-defined: **`validate_inclusive_tax()`** in `erpnext/accounts/services/taxes.py:298` (called from `initialize_taxes()`, line 259) throws unless the referenced row ("On Previous Row Amount") or *all* rows 1…row_id−1 ("On Previous Row Total") are themselves inclusive — *"To include tax in row {0} in Item rate, taxes in rows {1} must also be included"*. It also forbids `Actual`-type and `Valuation`-category charges from being inclusive. Item-specific rates come from `_get_tax_rate()` (line 384), which overrides the row's default rate with the `item.item_tax_rate` JSON map (account head → rate), and a `NOT_APPLICABLE_TAX` sentinel zeroes the row's contribution for that item. **Per-quantity taxes** ("On Item Quantity") — these are absolute currency-per-unit amounts, not percentages, so they can't be divided out. `get_current_tax_fraction()` returns them as `inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty` (line 376) instead of a fraction; `determine_exclusive_rate` multiplies by `item.qty` and **subtracts** them from the gross amount *before* the division (lines 327, 334). In the forward pass they're computed as `rate × item.qty` (line 626) with no taxable base. **Deduction-type taxes** (`add_deduct_tax == "Deduct"`, purchase-side rows) — lines 378–380 **negate both** the fraction and the per-qty amount, so a deductive inclusive tax simply enters the back-solve as a negative tax (shrinking the divisor / the flat subtraction). In the forward pass the sign is applied by `get_tax_amount_if_for_valuation_or_deduction()` (line 568): the amount is zeroed for `category == "Valuation"` and multiplied by −1 only on purchase doctypes (Purchase Order/Invoice/Receipt, Supplier Quotation), and `set_item_wise_tax()` (line 635) uses the same sign for the item-wise breakup. ## Two finishing touches - **Discounts**: `determine_exclusive_rate` is skipped when `discount_amount_applied` is set (line 330) — `apply_discount_amount()` (lines 868/909) prorates the already-computed net amounts instead of re-deriving them; inclusive "On Net Total" rows likewise fall back to the rounded `net_amount` for tax computation during the discount pass. - **Rounding residue**: because each item's net is rounded independently, the recomputed taxes may not sum exactly back to the gross total. `adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax()` (line 700) computes `diff = doc.total + non_inclusive_tax_amount − taxes[-1].total`; if it's within one unit of tax precision it's kept as `grand_total_diff`, and `calculate_totals()` (lines 731–745) sets `grand_total = taxes[-1].total + grand_total_diff` — absorbing the residual into the grand total (like a rounding adjustment) rather than distorting the tax rows. The old override hook `manipulate_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax` is deprecated and now just delegates to this method (line 696). **In short**: ERPNext treats every inclusive percentage tax as a fraction-of-net (with compounding pre-absorbed into `grand_total_fraction_for_current_item`), strips flat per-quantity inclusive taxes additively, treats Deduct rows as negative taxes, and then recovers the pre-tax line amount with one exact step: `net = (gross − flat_inclusive_taxes) ÷ (1 + Σ fractions)` — done identically in Python for the saved document, in JS for the live form, and (in simplified form) in Payment Entry.

## Where the backward calculation happens The tax-inclusive ("included in print rate") back-out lives in the tax engine used by every selling/buying doctype: - **Server:** `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py` — `calculate_taxes_and_totals.determine_exclusive_rate()` (line 303) plus its helper `get_current_tax_fraction()` (line 348). It's a step in the fixed pipeline in `_calculate()` (line 78): `calculate_item_values → update_item_tax_map → initialize_taxes → determine_exclusive_rate → calculate_net_total → calculate_taxes → adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax → calculate_totals`. - **Client mirror** (so the form recalculates live while editing): `erpnext/public/js/controllers/taxes_and_totals.js` — `determine_exclusive_rate()` (line 254) and `get_current_tax_fraction()` (line 300), identical logic. - **The same pattern is reused** for advance payments in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_entry/payment_entry.py` (`apply_taxes` line 948 → `determine_exclusive_rate` line 1486), keyed on `included_in_paid_amount` instead of `included_in_print_rate`. - Guard-rail validation: `validate_inclusive_tax()` in `erpnext/accounts/services/taxes.py` (line 298), called from `initialize_taxes()` (taxes_and_totals.py line 259). ## The core inversion The trigger is the `included_in_print_rate` checkbox on a Taxes and Charges row. `determine_exclusive_rate()` returns immediately if no row has it (line 304). Otherwise, for **each item row** (lines 307–343): 1. Load the item's per-item tax map (`item.item_tax_rate` JSON from its Item Tax Template) via `_load_item_tax_rate`. 2. Walk the tax rows in idx order, asking `get_current_tax_fraction(tax, item_tax_map)` for a pair: `(tax_fraction_for_current_item, inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty)`. 3. Accumulate two running sums: `cumulated_tax_fraction` (all percentage contributions) and `total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty` (per-quantity contributions × `item.qty`). 4. Do the actual back-out (lines 334–338): ```python amount = flt(item.amount) - total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty item._unrounded_net_amount = amount / (1 + cumulated_tax_fraction) item.net_amount = flt(item._unrounded_net_amount, item.precision("net_amount")) item.net_rate = flt(item.net_amount / item.qty, item.precision("net_rate")) ``` The algebra: since `net × (1 + Σfractions) = gross − flat per-unit taxes`, dividing by `1 + Σfractions` recovers the pre-tax amount. `item.rate`/`item.amount` keep the tax-inclusive figures the customer sees; `net_rate`/`net_amount`/`net_total` become the pre-tax values (converted to company currency via `_set_in_company_currency`). Note the ordering: the **absolute per-quantity taxes are stripped out first**, then the **percentage division** is applied — mixing the two in one step would be wrong since per-unit amounts don't scale with the divisor. ## Multiple inclusive taxes Every row flagged `included_in_print_rate` contributes its fraction to the *single* `cumulated_tax_fraction`, so one division `amount / (1 + Σf)` handles any number of inclusive taxes simultaneously — e.g., 10% VAT + 5% cess both inclusive gives divisor 1.15. Rows whose rate is `NOT_APPLICABLE_TAX` for that item's tax map contribute nothing (line 359–360). A second running sum, `grand_total_fraction_for_current_item` (first row: `1 + f`; later rows: previous row's value + current `f`, lines 318–324), tracks "net + all taxes up to this row" and exists purely to support compounding. ## Compounding tax rows ("On Previous Row Amount" / "On Previous Row Total") Because rows are processed in order, each row can read the previous row's freshly computed fractions (lines 365–373): - `On Previous Row Amount`: `fraction = (rate/100) × previous_row.tax_fraction_for_current_item` — tax on that tax alone. - `On Previous Row Total`: `fraction = (rate/100) × previous_row.grand_total_fraction_for_current_item` — tax on net total plus all prior taxes. So 10% VAT inclusive followed by 2% "On Previous Row Total" yields fractions 0.10 and 0.022, divisor 1.122 — exactly mirroring how the taxes compound forward. `validate_inclusive_tax()` (services/taxes.py:298) keeps this well-defined: an inclusive tax can't be `Actual`; an inclusive `On Previous Row Amount` must reference a row that is itself inclusive; inclusive `On Previous Row Total` requires *all* preceding rows to be inclusive; and `category == "Valuation"` taxes can never be inclusive (valuation-only charges never enter the printed price). Without these rules the divisor wouldn't represent the true gross→net ratio. ## Per-quantity taxes ("On Item Quantity") A percentage back-out is meaningless for flat per-unit charges, so `get_current_tax_fraction` returns fraction = 0 and `inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty = flt(tax_rate)` (line 375–376). These accumulate into `total_inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty` (line 327) and are subtracted from the line amount before the percentage division. Example: qty 2, gross 110, inclusive per-unit cess 5 → `amount = 110 − 10 = 100`, then divided by `1 + cumulated_fraction`. Later, in `calculate_taxes` → `get_current_tax_and_net_amount` (line 624–626), the tax amount itself is recomputed as `tax_rate × item.qty`, and no taxable amount is recorded for this charge type (`set_item_wise_tax`, line 659–660). ## Deduction-type taxes (`add_deduct_tax = "Deduct"`) Lines 378–380 negate both returned values: ```python if tax.add_deduct_tax == "Deduct": current_tax_fraction *= -1.0 inclusive_tax_amount_per_qty *= -1.0 ``` A deductible inclusive tax therefore *shrinks* the divisor (e.g., −5% → divide by 0.95), treating it as a negative tax already baked into the rate. The sign carries through the rest of the engine: `set_item_wise_tax` multiplies by −1 (line 635) and `get_tax_amount_if_for_valuation_or_deduction` flips the sign for purchase doctypes (line 579). ## Consistency details worth knowing - The unrounded net is stashed in `item._unrounded_net_amount`; `calculate_taxes` reuses it for inclusive "On Net Total" rows (`current_tax_amount = (rate/100) × item._unrounded_net_amount`, lines 609–615) so the recomputed tax exactly matches what was backed out — no double-rounding drift. - When a document-level discount applies, `apply_discount_amount` (line 857) distributes the discount proportionally over each item's `net_amount`, sets `self.discount_amount_applied = True` (line 909) and re-runs `_calculate()`. On that second pass `calculate_item_values` (line 225) and `determine_exclusive_rate` (line 330) both skip their work so the discounted nets aren't overwritten. - Finally, `adjust_grand_total_for_inclusive_tax` (line 700) computes `diff = doc.total + non_inclusive_tax_amount − last_tax.total`: with inclusive taxes the grand total must equal the sum of the (inclusive) item amounts plus only the *non*-inclusive taxes, so any residue within half the smallest precision is absorbed into `grand_total_diff` instead of surfacing as a rounding adjustment.

final answer
## The holding spot: "Stock Received But Not Billed" (SRBNB) ERPNext parks the value of received-but-unbilled goods in a **liability account named "Stock Received But Not Billed"** (a Company default, field `stock_received_but_not_billed` on the Company doctype; created under *Current Liabilities → Stock Liabilities* in the chart of accounts, `erpnext/accounts/doctype/account/chart_of_accounts/verified/standard_chart_of_accounts.py:164-173`, seeded in `erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py:697-704`). For fixed assets the parallel account is "Asset Received But Not Billed". This is the classic GR/IR accrual: the balance-sheet credit stands in for the supplier's invoice. ## Receipt side — parking the value (Purchase Receipt) `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:478`) delegates to **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()`** in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`, which calls `_make_item_gl_entries()`. Per stock item (perpetual inventory on): 1. The holding account is resolved at `gl_composer.py:297-301`: `stock_asset_rbnb = doc.get_company_default("asset_received_but_not_billed")` if the item is a fixed asset, else `doc.get_company_default("stock_received_but_not_billed")`. 2. `stock_value_diff` is pulled from the Stock Ledger via `get_stock_value_difference()` (`purchase_receipt.py:544`). 3. **`make_item_asset_inward_gl_entry()`** (`gl_composer.py:57`) **debits** the warehouse's inventory account (or the item's expense account, for assets) with `stock_value_diff`. 4. **`make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry()`** (`gl_composer.py:74`) posts the other half: it calls `self.add_gl_entry(...)` with a deliberately **negative debit of `item.base_net_amount`** (i.e., a credit) against the SRBNB account, "against" the stock account. So the parked entry is: **Dr Stock/Inventory account → Cr Stock Received But Not Billed** It also handles internal transfers (uses the from-warehouse's valuation diff), rejected-quantity valuation, and an exchange-rate discrepancy adjustment (extra debit to SRBNB / credit to `exchange_gain_loss_account`). 5. `_make_tax_gl_entries()` (`gl_composer.py:394`) credits valuation-tax accounts for the `item_tax_amount` capitalized into stock (the "negative expense" booked at receipt). `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry()` (`gl_composer.py:233`) absorbs any gap between document value and booked stock value (Purchase Price Variance for Standard Cost items via `get_divisional_loss_account`). Everything is then merged through `process_gl_map()` (`erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`). ## Billing side — moving the value out (Purchase Invoice, *Update Stock* unchecked) 1. **Linking:** `make_purchase_invoice()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/mapper.py:58` maps each `Purchase Receipt Item` to `Purchase Invoice Item` with `name → pr_detail` and `parent → purchase_receipt` (`mapper.py:142-154`) — this linkage is what lets the invoice find the parked credit. 2. **Forcing the debit account:** `PurchaseInvoice.validate()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/purchase_invoice.py:288-291`) runs **`ExpenseAccountService.set_expense_account(for_validate=True)`** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/expense_account.py:20`). For stock items under perpetual inventory it forcibly sets `item.expense_account = stock_not_billed_account` — either because the linked PR already credited SRBNB (verified by querying `GL Entry` for `voucher_type="Purchase Receipt"`, lines 57-82), or because no PR exists yet (invoice-before-receipt case, lines 83-102). Fixed-asset items similarly get "Asset Received But Not Billed" if it was credited in the PR. 3. **Posting:** `PurchaseInvoice.make_gl_entries()` (`purchase_invoice.py:671`) → `get_gl_entries()` (`purchase_invoice.py:703`) → **`PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer.compose()`** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/gl_composer.py:18`), which first resolves `doc.stock_received_but_not_billed = doc.get_company_default(...)` (line 26), then: - **`make_supplier_gl_entry()`** (line 80) credits `doc.credit_to` (Creditors) for the grand total. - **`make_item_gl_entries()`** (line 129), in the `update_stock == 0` branch (lines 319-350), **debits `item.expense_account` — which is SRBNB — against the supplier**. The code comment is explicit: *"When Update Stock is disabled, this invoice has no stock impact: the linked Purchase Receipt already booked the stock (at standard)... Here we only clear 'Stock Received But Not Billed' at the full billed amount against the supplier."* That debit is what moves the value out of the holding spot. - If the PR never credited the valuation taxes, SRBNB is additionally debited for `item.item_tax_amount` (lines 395-439, `doc.negative_expense_to_be_booked`), and `make_tax_gl_entries()` (line 605, block at 650-680) credits the tax accounts — the mirror of step 5 on the receipt side. - Exchange-rate drift between receipt and bill is booked as an extra debit to SRBNB against `exchange_gain_loss_account` (lines 352-393). ## Net result ``` Receipt: Dr Stock/Inventory Cr SRBNB (value parked as a liability) Invoice: Dr SRBNB Cr Creditors (parking spot cleared) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Net: Dr Stock/Inventory Cr Creditors ``` SRBNB nets to zero once fully billed; partial billing (`get_pending_qty` in the mapper, billed-qty tracking via `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status`) leaves the unbilled remainder parked. If the bill arrives *first* (no PR yet), the same pair posts in reverse order — PI debits SRBNB/Cr Creditors, and the later PR credits SRBNB to clear it. Two side variants: `update_stock=1` on the PI skips parking entirely (PI debits the warehouse account directly, `gl_composer.py:137-269` via `make_stock_adjustment_entry`), and non-stock items with provisional accounting park value in the "Provisional Account" instead (`add_provisional_gl_entry`, reversed proportionally by `make_provisional_gl_entry` in the PI composer).

It also handles internal transfers, rejected-qty valuation, and the bill-first case (when the item already references a `purchase_invoice`, it books exchange-rate discrepancies into SRBNB + `exchange_gain_loss_account`, lines 126–162). Companion entries: landed-cost credits, `make_amount_difference_entry` (line 202, PR-vs-PI rate differences), subcontracting cost, and `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` (line 233).
