final answer
## Short answer **No — not for the purposes that represent issuing/moving stock out.** ERPNext does have a `BatchExpiredError` validation for Stock Entry, but it is deliberately **bypassed for "Material Issue" and "Material Transfer"**. Expired batches are only blocked from picker UI (soft filtering) for those purposes; nothing server-side throws at save/submit. ## The three throw sites and why none of them fire for Issue/Transfer **1. `SerialBatchBundleService.validate_serialized_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/services/serial_batch_bundle_service.py:106-147`, invoked from `StockEntry.validate()` (`stock_entry.py:318`). This throws `BatchExpiredError` ("Row #{0}: The batch {1} has already expired.") when `getdate(expiry_date) < getdate(posting_date)` for rows with `qty > 0` — but it explicitly exempts the exact purposes you asked about: ```python is_material_issue = False if self.doc.doctype == "Stock Entry" and self.doc.purpose in ["Material Issue", "Material Transfer"]: is_material_issue = True ... if is_material_issue: continue # skips the expiry_date check entirely ``` **2. `StockEntry.validate_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py:1479-1487` (called in `validate()` at line 310). It delegates to `StockEntryDetail.validate_batch()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry_detail/stock_entry_detail.py:88-99`), which throws `"Batch {0} of Item {1} has expired."` when `posting_date > expiry_date` — but only for purposes `["Material Transfer for Manufacture", "Manufacture", "Repack", "Send to Subcontractor"]`. Again, Material Issue / Material Transfer are excluded. **3. `StockLedgerEntry.validate_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_ledger_entry/stock_ledger_entry.py:287-299`. The ledger-level backstop also throws "Batch … has expired", but it opens with `if self.batch_no and self.voucher_type != "Stock Entry":` — so it never applies to Stock Entries, expired or not. ## What *does* exist - **Hard throw for inward purposes**: `validate_serialized_batch` fires for e.g. Material Receipt. Confirmed by `test_batch_expiry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/test_stock_entry.py:1958-1982`): a Material Receipt with a batch whose `expiry_date` is yesterday raises `BatchExpiredError` on `save`. But "Material Receipt" isn't in the `is_material_issue` skip list — Issue/Transfer are. - **UI/selection-level filtering only (soft)**: the Batch link search `get_batch_numbers` (`erpnext/controllers/queries.py:931-947`, filters `expiry_date.isnull() | expiry_date >= today()`), the batch pickers `get_batches_from_stock_ledger_entries` / `get_batches_from_serial_and_batch_bundle` (`queries.py:555/616`, skip expired unless `include_expired_batches`), and auto batch selection `get_auto_batch_nos` → `get_non_expired_batches` (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2570-2584`, `or_filters expiry_date >= today() or not set`). These hide expired batches from the picker, but are not submit-time enforcement — a stale/hand-entered batch passes. - **Informational helpers, not validators**: `get_expired_batches()` / `get_expired_batch_items()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/serial_batch.py:339-373` (used to surface expired stock, e.g. for warnings). Pick List separately has `validate_expired_batches` (`pick_list.py:286`), but that's a `msgprint` warning on Pick List, not Stock Entry, and not a throw. **Conclusion**: The design is intentional — ERPNext lets you *issue or transfer* an expired batch (so you can move/destroy expired stock), while blocking expired batches from coming *into* stock (Receipt, Manufacture FG, Repack, etc.). The only guard for Issue/Transfer is that the batch selector won't normally show expired batches; there is no server-side `frappe.throw` on expiry for those purposes.

final answer
## Short answer **No — not for Material Issue / Material Transfer.** ERPNext *does* have submit-time batch-expiry validations that raise on an expired `expiry_date`, but both of them deliberately **skip** the exact purposes you're asking about ("Material Issue" and "Material Transfer" Stock Entries), and the stock-ledger-level check excludes Stock Entry altogether. It's an intentional design: moving/issuing expired stock is allowed (e.g., to scrap or quarantine it); only *putting stock into* an expired batch is blocked. ## The validations that exist (and their exemptions) 1. **`SerialBatchBundleService.validate_serialized_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/services/serial_batch_bundle_service.py:106-147` Called from `StockEntry.validate()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py:318`) and from the generic `StockController.validate()` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:57`). It reads `Batch.expiry_date` and throws `BatchExpiredError` ("Row #{0}: The batch {1} has already expired.", exception defined in `erpnext/exceptions.py:46`) when `getdate(expiry_date) < getdate(posting_date)`. **But** it first sets: ```python is_material_issue = False if self.doc.doctype == "Stock Entry" and self.doc.purpose in ["Material Issue", "Material Transfer"]: is_material_issue = True ... if is_material_issue: continue # skips the expiry throw entirely ``` (`serial_batch_bundle_service.py:110-112, 130-131`). It also only fires for rows with `qty > 0` (inward) carrying a plain `row.batch_no` — i.e. old-style `use_serial_batch_fields` rows; it never inspects the linked Serial and Batch Bundle. 2. **`StockEntryDetail.validate_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry_detail/stock_entry_detail.py:88-99` (via `StockEntry.validate_batch()` at `stock_entry.py:1479-1487`, called at `stock_entry.py:310`) Throws generic `frappe.throw("Batch {0} of Item {1} has expired.")` when `posting_date > expiry_date` (and blocks disabled batches) — but only for purposes `"Material Transfer for Manufacture"`, `"Manufacture"`, `"Repack"`, `"Send to Subcontractor"`. Again, not Issue/Transfer. 3. **`StockLedgerEntry.validate_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_ledger_entry/stock_ledger_entry.py:287-299` Same expiry throw at ledger-posting time, but guarded by `if self.batch_no and self.voucher_type != "Stock Entry":` — Stock Entries are carved out wholesale (precisely because the doc-level checks above are supposed to own this, and those skip issue/transfer). 4. **`SerialAndBatchBundle.validate()`** (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:109-145`) has **no** expiry throw at all — a manually built bundle referencing an expired batch validates fine as long as batch qty is available. ## This exemption is intentional and mirrored in the UI - `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.js:129-131`: the `batch_no` link query passes `filters["include_expired_batches"] = 1` exactly for `["Material Receipt", "Material Transfer", "Material Issue"]`. - `erpnext/controllers/queries.py::get_batch_no` (line 502) → `get_batches_from_stock_ledger_entries` / `get_batches_from_serial_and_batch_bundle` (lines 555-679) then **skip** the `expiry_date >= posting_date/today` filter when `include_expired_batches` is set (lines 588-589, 652-655) — so the autocomplete deliberately offers expired batches for issue/transfer. ## What *is* protected - **Inward into an expired batch is blocked**: the regression test `test_batch_expiry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/test_stock_entry.py:1958-1982`) creates a batch with `expiry_date = add_days(today(), -1)`, a **Material Receipt** entry with `use_serial_batch_fields=1`, and asserts `BatchExpiredError` on `se.save()` — the same check that Issue/Transfer `continue`s past. - **Auto-picking avoids expired stock** (soft guard, not a hard throw): `get_non_expired_batches()` (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2570-2584`, used at line 2492) and the `expiry_date >= today()` filter in `get_available_batches()` (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:3173`, skipped only for `for_stock_levels`). So FIFO/"Expiry"-based auto selection (`based_on == "Expiry"` ordering at line 3206) won't pick expired batches, but a manual pick isn't rejected. - A whitelisted helper `get_expired_batch_items()` / `get_expired_batches()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/serial_batch.py:338-373` lists expired batches that still hold stock (used by `stock_entry.js:520`) — surfacing expired stock for clean-up rather than blocking it. - Related but different: `is_batch_expired()` (`erpnext/controllers/sales_and_purchase_return.py:1342`, used at `selling_controller.py:573`) blocks expired-batch returns on selling vouchers — not Stock Entry. **Bottom line:** if a user hand-picks an expired batch on a Material Issue or Material Transfer Stock Entry (with sufficient batch stock), nothing throws at save or submit — the `BatchExpiredError` check in `validate_serialized_batch` explicitly skips those two purposes, and the SLE-level expiry check skips all Stock Entries. The only hard expiry gate is on inward purposes (Material Receipt, Manufacture, Repack, etc.), and only for positive-qty rows using the old `batch_no` field.

## Short answer **No.** Submitting a Sales Order in core ERPNext does **not** automatically email the customer a confirmation. There is no email-sending code anywhere in the Sales Order submit path — automatic emails only happen if you (or an app) configure the framework's generic **Notification** doctype, or use an adjacent flow like Payment Request / Delivery Trip. ## Evidence: the submit flow contains no email logic 1. **`SalesOrder.on_submit()` — `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450-471`** is the submit hook. All it does is: - `check_credit_limit()`, `update_reserved_qty()`, delivery-schedule cleanup (`DeliveryScheduleService`), `Authorization Control` approval check, `update_project()`, `update_prevdoc_status("submit")`, `update_blanket_order()`, inter-company doc linking (`update_linked_doc`), coupon-code counting, and optional stock reservation entries. - A grep of the whole `sales_order` module shows **no `frappe.sendmail` / `send_email` / notification call at all** (the only `notify` hits are the `notify=` kwarg for stock-reservation entries). 2. **Inherited controllers are also email-free**: `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py` and `AccountsController.on_submit` in `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py` contain no `sendmail`/`notify` logic. 3. **ERPNext's hooks don't trigger emails on submit**: `doc_events` in `erpnext/hooks.py` (line 367+) registers only `validate` hooks for all doctypes (SLA application, transaction-deletion check, accounting period check) — nothing email-related for Sales Order. ## Where an automatic email *would* be triggered - **Frappe framework "Notification" doctype** (in the `frappe` app, not this repo): `frappe/email/doctype/notification/notification.py` → `trigger_notifications(doc, method)`, wired in frappe core's `hooks.py` under `doc_events["*"]` for `on_update`/`on_submit`/`on_cancel`/`on_change`. If someone creates a Notification with *Document Type = Sales Order, Event = Submit, Channel = Email*, that is the "automatic confirmation email" mechanism. **ERPNext does not install one by default** — the setup wizard (`erpnext/setup/setup_wizard/operations/install_fixtures.py:337-345`) only creates an Email Template named "Dispatch Notification", and that is used for *Delivery Trip*, not Sales Orders. - **Nearby email senders you may be thinking of** (none fire on SO submit): - `PaymentRequest.send_email()` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py:587-611`, enqueues `frappe.sendmail` with the payment link and an attached print of the Sales Order. Only runs when a Payment Request exists — created manually via the UI button (`make_payment_request()` in `erpnext/public/js/controllers/transaction.js:485`), by POS (`pos_invoice.py:841`), or by the webshop order page (`erpnext/templates/pages/order.html:41`), **not** by `SalesOrder.on_submit`. - Delivery Trip submit → `notify_customers()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_trip/delivery_trip.py:400-438`, which emails customers the "Dispatch Notification" template from Delivery Settings (`dispatch_template`, set up in `erpnext/setup/setup_wizard/operations/defaults_setup.py:58` and the v11 patch `erpnext/patches/v11_0/add_default_dispatch_notification_template.py`). - **Manual**: the Email button on the Sales Order form (`erpnext/public/js/controllers/transaction.js`) is user-initiated only. ## Bottom line If you need a confirmation email on SO submission, either (a) create a **Notification** doctype record (Document Type: Sales Order, Event: Submit, Channel: Email, recipients via the Contact's email), or (b) add a custom hook via `doc_events`/`on_submit` customization that calls `frappe.sendmail` — ERPNext core deliberately leaves this out.

final answer
## Answer: No — ERPNext does **not** automatically email the customer when a Sales Order is submitted I traced the entire submit path and there is no customer-facing email anywhere in it. Here's the evidence: ### 1. The submit hook itself contains no email logic `SalesOrder.on_submit()` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` (lines 450–471) does only internal bookkeeping: - `super().update_prevdoc_status()` — updates the linked Quotation - `check_credit_limit()` - `update_reserved_qty()` + `create_stock_reservation_entries()` - `DeliveryScheduleService(...).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items()` - Authorization Control check, `update_project()`, `update_blanket_order()`, `update_linked_doc()` (inter-company), coupon-code counting There is no `frappe.sendmail` or notification call in it, nor anywhere else in the `selling` module's Python code. ### 2. No `doc_events` hook emails the customer In `erpnext/hooks.py` (lines 367–439), the `doc_events` map has **no entry for "Sales Order" at all** — the only sales-side hook is the regional Italian `sales_invoice_on_submit`. So no app-level hook fires an email on SO submit either. ### 3. ERPNext ships no Sales Order Notification fixture ERPNext bundles only two standard Notification documents: `erpnext/accounts/notification/notification_for_new_fiscal_year/` and `erpnext/manufacturing/notification/material_request_receipt_notification/` — neither is a customer confirmation for Sales Orders. ### Where such an email *would* come from, if configured The submit-time email mechanism lives in the **Frappe framework** (not ERPNext): the **Notification doctype** (`frappe/automation/doctype/notification`). A Notification with **Event = "Submit"** and **Channel = "Email"** is evaluated by Frappe core on every submit of the matching doctype. ERPNext simply doesn't pre-create one for Sales Order — to get a "confirmation" email you'd configure it yourself (recipient e.g. `doc.contact_email`, optionally using an Email Template / print format). Related but distinct behaviors that are sometimes confused with this: - **The "Email" button** on the Sales Order form (`sales_order.js`) — purely manual, opens a compose dialog with the SO print format. - **Webshop order confirmations** — orders placed through the shopping cart get a confirmation email, but that logic lives in the separate **Webshop app**; `erpnext/shopping_cart/` in this repo is an empty stub (`__init__.py` only). - **Payment Request** — `PaymentRequest.on_submit` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py:269`) only updates advance-payment status; its payment-link email is not triggered by SO submission. **Bottom line:** submission of a Sales Order triggers `SalesOrder.on_submit()` with only status/stock/credit-limit/inter-company updates — no automatic customer email exists in the default flow. Automatic emailing on submit requires a user-configured Notification (or a workflow/custom script) in Frappe, or the external Webshop app for web-placed orders.

Here's the complete answer: ## Answer: No — submitting a Sales Order does **not** automatically email the customer There is no hardcoded customer-confirmation email anywhere in the Sales Order submit flow. Here's what I verified: ### 1. What `SalesOrder.on_submit()` actually does `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:L450-471` — the submit hook performs only bookkeeping: - `super().update_prevdoc_status()` (updates linked Quotations) - `check_credit_limit()` - `update_reserved_qty()` - `DeliveryScheduleService(self).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items()` - `Authorization Control.validate_approving_authority()` - `update_project()`, `update_prevdoc_status("submit")`, `update_blanket_order()` - `update_linked_doc()` (inter-company order), `update_coupon_code_count()`, `create_stock_reservation_entries()` **No `frappe.sendmail`, `send_email`, or `frappe.email` call exists** — a grep across `erpnext/controllers/` (SellingController → StatusUpdater/TransactionBase/AccountsController, the rest of the MRO) found zero email-sending calls. ### 2. No hook-based email either `erpnext/hooks.py:367+` — the `doc_events` map has **no entry for "Sales Order" at all** (only a wildcard `validate` for SLA/deletion checks, Stock Entry, User, Communication, Event, Sales Invoice regional hooks, etc.). Nothing in ERPNext intercepts SO submission to send mail. ### 3. Things that look email-related but aren't - `erpnext/startup/notifications.py` → `get_notification_config()` is only the desk "badge counter" config (which documents show as pending), not emails. - `test_sales_order.py:3187` sets `"send_email_alert": 0` — that's a **Workflow** doctype field that emails workflow *approvers* on state transitions, not the customer. ### 4. How automatic confirmation emails *do* happen (the real mechanism) The automatic email-on-submit capability lives in the **framework**, not ERPNext: - Frappe's **Notification** doctype (`frappe/email/doctype/notification/notification.py`) is globally hooked to document events (`*` doc_events: `on_submit`, `on_update_after_submit`, etc.). If a site admin creates a Notification with Document Type = **Sales Order**, Event = **Submit**, recipients = customer contact, and a message template, the customer gets an email at submit time. - ERPNext ships **no default/out-of-the-box Notification for Sales Order** — no code in the repo creates one (`doctype="Notification"` never appears), and the frappe app isn't even vendored in this repo. - Otherwise, emailing an order confirmation is **manual**: the "Email" button on a submitted Sales Order (sends the chosen Print Format via a Communication), or the portal's "Order Confirmation" template used on the website order page. **Bottom line:** the submit path (`SalesOrder.on_submit()` → base controller hooks) contains no email logic; customer confirmations are opt-in via a configured Frappe Notification, or sent manually from the document.

final answer
I have everything needed for a definitive answer. ## Answer: No — ERPNext does **not** automatically email the customer when a Sales Order is submitted There is no customer confirmation email in the Sales Order submit flow. Emailing the customer is either a manual action or something you configure yourself via Frappe's Notification framework. ### 1. Proof from the submit flow The Sales Order's own submit hook contains no email logic. `SalesOrder.on_submit` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450-455` does only this: ```python def on_submit(self): super().update_prevdoc_status() # marks linked Quotation as "Converted" self.check_credit_limit() self.update_reserved_qty() DeliveryScheduleService(self).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items() ``` The full inheritance chain (`SalesOrder → SellingController → StockController → AccountsController → TransactionBase → StatusUpdater`) adds status/stock/billing updates on submit — none of them call `frappe.sendmail` or touch an email template. A search of the entire `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/` package finds zero occurrences of `sendmail`, `send_email`, or `email_template` in production code. ### 2. No hook fires an email either - `erpnext/hooks.py:367` (`doc_events`) registers no `on_submit` handler for "Sales Order" at all — the only sales-document `on_submit` hook is a regional Italy tax handler on **Sales Invoice** (`erpnext.regional.italy.utils.sales_invoice_on_submit`). - `erpnext/hooks.py:73` registers `notification_config = "erpnext.startup.notifications.get_notification_config"` (`erpnext/startup/notifications.py:8`), but that config only feeds the **internal** desk notification badges (e.g., "Sales Order where status not in Completed/Closed" shown to logged-in users) — it never emails customers. ### 3. What ERPNext ships vs. how emails actually get sent ERPNext ships only two default Notification records in the whole codebase — `erpnext/manufacturing/notification/material_request_receipt_notification/` and `erpnext/accounts/notification/notification_for_new_fiscal_year/` — **neither is for Sales Order**. So if you want an automatic customer email on submit, you must create it yourself via Frappe framework features (in the `frappe` app, separate from this repo): - **Notification doctype** (`frappe/email/doctype/notification`): set Document Type = *Sales Order*, Event = *Submit*, Channel = *Email*, with a recipient condition on the customer's contact email. This hooks into the generic `on_submit` document event and calls `frappe.sendmail` — it's configuration, not ERPNext code. - Note: the `send_email_alert` field you'll see in `test_sales_order.py:3187` belongs to the **Workflow** doctype — it emails internal workflow users on state transitions, not the customer. ### Summary | Mechanism | Sends email on SO submit? | |---|---| | `SalesOrder.on_submit` (`sales_order.py:450`) | ❌ No email logic | | `doc_events` hooks (`erpnext/hooks.py:367`) | ❌ No SO submit handler | | `notification_config` (`erpnext/startup/notifications.py`) | ❌ Internal desk alerts only | | Default Notification records shipped by ERPNext | ❌ None for Sales Order | | Frappe **Notification** doctype (Event = Submit, user-configured) | ✅ Only if you configure it | | Manual "Email" button on the Sales Order form | ✅ But it's user-initiated |

final answer
## Short answer No. Purchase Order has **no supplier‑side counterpart to the customer credit limit**. There is no `credit_limit` field on the Supplier doctype and no `credit_limit` logic anywhere under `erpnext/buying/` — ERPNext simply doesn't model "how much this supplier is owed/exposed" as an automatic ceiling. What *does* gate Purchase Order submission are three different mechanisms, none of which is a per-party monetary exposure limit: ## 1. Supplier Scorecard block/warn (the only supplier-specific gate) `PurchaseOrder.validate_supplier()` in `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py` (lines 272–292, called from `validate()` at line 200): - If `Supplier.prevent_pos` is set → `frappe.throw("Purchase Orders are not allowed for {supplier} due to a scorecard standing of ...")`. - If `Supplier.warn_pos` is set → `frappe.msgprint(... "should be issued with caution", indicator="orange")`. Those flags aren't monetary limits; they're propagated from the **Supplier Scorecard** doctype (`erpnext/buying/doctype/supplier_scorecard/supplier_scorecard.py` — `prevent_pos`/`warn_pos` are set on the Supplier from a scoring "Standing", e.g. a Red standing defaults to `prevent_pos: 1`). It's a binary performance/standing gate: supplier behaves badly → POs blocked. No amount is compared. ## 2. Budget check (the real monetary gate — but not per-supplier) `PurchaseOrder.on_submit()` (line 386) calls `self.validate_budget()` → defined in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978`: - Modern path: `BudgetValidation` in `erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py` (`validate()` → `build_validation_map` → `validate_for_overbooking` → `handle_actions` → `handle_purchase_order_overlimit` / `handle_actual_expense_overlimit` / `handle_cumulative_overlimit` → `execute_action`, which `frappe.throw(msg, BudgetError, title="Budget Exceeded")` on "Stop" or `msgprint` on "Warn"). - Legacy path (`Accounts Settings.use_legacy_budget_controller`): `validate_expense_against_budget` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py:377` (Stop → `frappe.throw(..., BudgetError)` at line 582). The **Budget** doctype carries `applicable_on_purchase_order` plus PO-specific actions `action_if_annual_budget_exceeded_on_po` / `action_if_accumulated_monthly_budget_exceeded_on_po`. The check aggregates: ordered amounts of already-submitted POs (`get_ordered_amount`), pending Material Request amounts, and actual GL expense for the fiscal year, against a budget keyed by **Company + Fiscal Year + Expense Account + Cost Center/Project**. A user holding the Company's `exception_budget_approver_role` gets a Stop downgraded to a Warn. Note it runs inside `on_submit` — a throw there rolls the whole submission transaction back, so it effectively blocks submission (the code even notes the just-submitted doc is already visible to the query). ## 3. Authorization Rule / Authorization Control (who may spend, not which supplier) Right after the budget check, `PurchaseOrder.on_submit()` (line 388) calls `frappe.get_cached_doc("Authorization Control").validate_approving_authority(self.doctype, self.company, self.base_grand_total)` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154`). It matches `Authorization Rule` records (`based_on: Grand Total`, `value`, `system_user`/`system_role`) and throws "Not authorized since Grand Total exceeds limits … Can be approved by {roles/users}" if the submitting user has no rule covering the amount. ## How this differs in nature from a credit limit | | Sales Order credit limit | Purchase Order gates | |---|---|---| | Where | `SalesOrder.on_submit()` → `check_credit_limit()` (`sales_order.py:452, 514`) → `check_credit_limit(customer, company)` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514`, using `get_customer_outstanding` (line 706) and `get_credit_limit` (line 802) against the **Customer Credit Limit** child table (with `bypass_credit_limit_check` flag and an `Accounts Settings.credit_controller` role override) | Scorecard (`validate`), Budget + Authorization Control (`on_submit`) | | What it compares | That **party's** cumulative uncollected receivables vs a limit stored **on the party** | Budget: total **committed/actual spend** in an account × cost center/project envelope, regardless of supplier. Scorecard: supplier's **performance grade**. Authorization Rule: **submitting user's** authority vs grand total | | Nature | Dynamic financial-exposure ceiling on one counterparty, computed from its ledger balance | (a) internal fiscal-year spending envelope with Warn/Stop/Ignore actions, (b) qualitative binary block, (c) person/role approval threshold | So: the PO equivalent of "don't let this party's exposure exceed X" does not exist for suppliers; the closest monetary gate is the **budget check**, which limits *what the company spends on an expense account/cost center per fiscal year* — an internal appropriation control — while supplier-side blocking is purely discretionary via the Scorecard, and value-based blocking is tied to the *user*, not the supplier.

I now have the complete picture. Here's the answer. ## Short answer **No.** Purchase Order has no per-supplier spend/credit-limit check — the `Supplier` doctype (`erpnext/buying/doctype/supplier/supplier.json`) contains no credit- or limit-type field at all, and nowhere on the purchase side is a supplier's outstanding amount compared against a cap, the way `check_credit_limit(customer, company)` does for customers (`erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514-571`, comparing `get_customer_outstanding` against the `Customer Credit Limit` child table). What actually gates PO submission is a **budget control** plus an **approval-authority control**, both of which are structurally different from a credit limit. ## What does gate Purchase Order submission `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:372-396`) runs two spending-related checks: **1. Budget validation — `self.validate_budget()` (line 386)** Inherited from `BuyingController.validate_budget` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978-1000`). Controlled by the Accounts Settings switch `use_legacy_budget_controller`: - **New controller** — `BudgetValidation.validate()` in `erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py`: - Fetches submitted `Budget` records for the company/fiscal year/date range (`get_budget_records`, lines 163-207), including the PO-specific toggles `applicable_on_purchase_order`, `action_if_annual_budget_exceeded_on_po`, `action_if_accumulated_monthly_budget_exceeded_on_po`. - Aggregates spend per key *(dimension, dimension value, expense account)*: `get_ordered_amount` (unbilled remainder of submitted POs: `amount − billed_amt`, excluding Closed POs, lines 209-237), `get_requested_amount` (unconverted Material Requests), and `get_actual_expense` (GL debit−credit, lines 273-290), plus the current document's amount. - `handle_purchase_order_overlimit` → `handle_individual_doctype_action` (lines 311-357) compares annual and accumulated-monthly budget; `execute_action` (lines 298-309) turns the configured action into **`Stop` → `frappe.throw(..., BudgetError, "Budget Exceeded")`** (blocks submission) or **`Warn`** (msgprint only). A user holding the budget's `exception_approver_role` always gets Stop downgraded to Warn. - **Legacy controller** — per-item `validate_expense_against_budget(args)` from `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py` (same Stop/Warn semantics in `compare_expense_with_budget` / `validate_budget_records`, lines 500-537). (Material Request has the identical hook at `erpnext/stock/doctype/material_request/material_request.py:240`.) **2. Authorization Control — line 388:** `AuthorizationControl.validate_approving_authority(self.doctype, self.company, self.base_grand_total)` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154-237`). This checks the **submitting user**, matching per-user, per-role, and global `Authorization Rule` records based on Grand Total (or discount %) via `bifurcate_based_on_type` — i.e., "does this person have authority to commit this amount?" Additionally, at draft stage `PurchaseOrder.validate_supplier` (`purchase_order.py:272-294`) throws if the supplier has `prevent_pos` set and their **Supplier Scorecard** standing requires it — a supplier gate, but a quality/standing gate, not a spend limit. Notably, PO is *not* listed in the pre-submit preview framework `PRE_SUBMIT_DOCTYPE_CONFIG` (`erpnext/accounts/utils.py:2752-2771`), which only configures Sales Order, Sales Invoice, Delivery Note, Purchase Receipt, Purchase Invoice — so unlike Sales Order, PO gets no `preview_mode` pre-submit warning; its spend gates fire only inside `on_submit`. ## How it differs in nature from a credit limit - **Party vs. accounting dimension.** The credit limit is *bilateral and per-counterparty*: a cap stored on the customer (`Customer Credit Limit` rows per company) compared against that party's own receivable outstanding. The budget check never looks at the supplier at all — two POs to two different suppliers hitting the same expense account/cost center draw from the *same* budget; it is an **org-internal aggregate control** keyed by expense account (optionally project, cost center, accounting dimensions). - **What is measured.** Credit limit compares *outstanding receivables* (what the customer owes you) plus the new order. The budget check measures *committed + actual expenditure*: unbilled PO amounts, open MR amounts, and GL actuals versus an annual and accumulated-monthly allocation — it caps the company's own outflow, not a counterparty's debt. - **Configuration surface.** Credit limit is a field on the party master with a single global override role (`credit_controller` in Accounts Settings, checked inside `check_credit_limit`). Budgets are separate `Budget` documents per fiscal year with per-doctype, per-period Stop/Warn/Ignore actions and a per-budget `exception_approver_role`. - **Enforcement point.** Sales Order enforces credit both as a hard check in `SalesOrder.check_credit_limit`/`on_submit` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:514-524`) and as a pre-submit warning (`_check_credit_limit_warn`, `erpnext/accounts/utils.py:2805-2853`). PO's budget check runs only inside `on_submit` — no pre-submit equivalent exists for it. So: the purchasing analog of "don't extend too much credit to one customer" does not exist per supplier; the deliberate counterpart in ERPNext is "don't exceed the budget allocated to this expense account" (`BudgetValidation` → Stop on `on_submit`), supplemented by role/user-based `Authorization Control` approval limits.

final answer
## Answer **No — Purchase Order has no supplier-level spend/credit limit.** There is no `credit_limit` field on Supplier, no supplier-scoped amount check anywhere in `PurchaseOrder.validate()` or `on_submit()`. But submission *is* automatically gated — by the **Budget check**, which is a fundamentally different control. ### The Sales Order reference point - `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450`) calls `self.check_credit_limit()` (defined at line 514, also called from `on_update_after_submit` at line 550). - That skips the check if the `Customer Credit Limit` child row has `bypass_credit_limit_check` set, then calls `check_credit_limit(customer, company)` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514`. - `get_credit_limit()` (customer.py:802) resolves the cap with a fallback chain: **Customer** (per-company `Customer Credit Limit` row) → **Customer Group** → **Company default `credit_limit`**. The check compares the customer's *outstanding receivables* (`get_customer_outstanding`) against that cap; if crossed and the user lacks the `credit_controller` role (Accounts Settings), it raises via `frappe.msgprint(..., raise_exception=1)` with title "Credit Limit Crossed", aborting submission. ### What gates Purchase Order submission instead In `PurchaseOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:372–390`), two automatic gates run: 1. **Budget check** — line 386 calls `self.validate_budget()`, defined in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978`: - Modern path (default): `BudgetValidation` in `erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py`. It keys items as *(accounting dimension — cost center, project, or any custom Accounting Dimension — expense account)* and matches them against submitted **Budget** documents for the company/fiscal year (`get_budget_records()`, line 163). It then accumulates four flows for that key: unbilled amounts on submitted POs (`get_ordered_amount`, line 209), open Purchase Material Requests (`get_requested_amount`, line 239), actual GL expense booked in the fiscal year (`get_actual_expense`, line 273), plus the current document. On breach it executes the Budget's configured action (`action_if_annual_budget_exceeded_on_po` / `..._monthly_..._on_po`): **"Stop"** raises `BudgetError` (`frappe.throw` — submission aborts and rolls back), **"Warn"** proceeds with a msgprint. A Company `exception_budget_approver_role` downgrades Stop to Warn. - Legacy path (`Accounts Settings.use_legacy_budget_controller`): per-item `validate_expense_against_budget()` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py:377`. - Timing nuance: for PO/Material Request the check runs in `on_submit`, so the current doc is already committed (docstatus 1) and is picked up by the ordered-amount query — the comment at budget_controller.py:91–93 documents this; the throw still rolls back the whole submit. (Material Request does the same at `material_request.py:234–240`; GL booking is also budget-checked in `general_ledger.py:180/394`.) 2. **Authorization Control** — line 388, `validate_approving_authority(doctype, company, base_grand_total)`: a role-based approval-authority check on the document amount (applies to both SO and PO). Supplier-side controls that *do* exist are different in kind: `validate_supplier()` (purchase_order.py:272) blocks/warns on `prevent_pos`/`warn_pos` flags and **Supplier Scorecard** standing (a status gate, not an amount), and Supplier `on_hold` (supplier.json:280, with `hold_type`/`release_date`) blocks invoicing/payments — none is a monetary cap. ### How it differs in nature from a credit limit | | Customer Credit Limit (SO) | Budget (PO) | |---|---|---| | **Scoped to** | A party — the customer (Customer → Customer Group → Company fallback) | An expense account × accounting dimension (cost center/project/custom) | | **What's measured** | Outstanding *receivable balance* owed to you (a liquidity/exposure measure, continuous) | *Committed + spent* funds against a planned allocation within a period (fiscal year, with monthly accumulation via Budget Distribution) | | **Where the cap lives** | `Customer Credit Limit` child table / Company field | Submitted `Budget` doctype per fiscal year | | **Override** | `credit_controller` role in Accounts Settings; per-row `bypass_credit_limit_check` | Company `exception_budget_approver_role`; per-Budget Warn vs Stop action | So: SO's gate is *"this customer is already owing us too much"*; PO's gate is *"this expense line (account/dimension) has run out of planned money this period"*. The supplier is not part of the default check at all — only if an admin manually configures **Supplier** as an Accounting Dimension (permitted; `accounting_dimension.py:50` doesn't blacklist it) could budgets be dimensioned by supplier, which is a user-configured extension, not an out-of-the-box equivalent.

final answer
## Short answer **No.** Purchase Order has no supplier-side counterpart to the customer credit limit — there is no credit limit field on Supplier, no supplier-outstanding-vs-cap calculation anywhere in `erpnext/buying`, and no code that accumulates a supplier's committed spend against a threshold. But PO submission **is** gated — by three different mechanisms that are each a different *kind* of control than a credit limit. ## First, how the Sales Order side actually works (the baseline) - `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450-452`) calls `self.check_credit_limit()` (`sales_order.py:514-524`), which is skipped only if `bypass_credit_limit_check` is set on the customer's `Customer Credit Limit` row; otherwise it calls the module function `check_credit_limit(customer, company)` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514`. - That function compares `get_credit_limit(customer, company)` (`customer.py:802` — resolved per company from the `Customer Credit Limit` child table on **Customer**, falling back to the **Customer Group**'s limit unless that row has `bypass_credit_limit_check`, then to `Company.credit_limit`) against `get_customer_outstanding(...)` — the customer's actual receivables exposure. If outstanding exceeds the limit and the submitting user does not hold the `credit_controller` role from Accounts Settings, it throws (and even when the role-holder proceeds, it emails the credit controllers). - One precision on the premise: the check runs inside `on_submit` (also re-run on `on_update_after_submit`, line 547-550), not in `validate` — but since a throw rolls back the submit transaction, it effectively blocks the document from becoming submitted. ## What gates Purchase Order submission instead **1. Supplier hold / scorecard — party-level but binary/qualitative (validate phase)** - `PurchaseOrder.validate_supplier()` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:272-294`): if `Supplier.prevent_pos` is set and the **Supplier Scorecard** has a standing, it throws "Purchase Orders are not allowed for {supplier} due to a scorecard standing of {1}"; `warn_pos` merely msgprints a caution. - `AccountsController.ensure_supplier_is_not_blocked()` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:153-170`), called from `AccountsController.validate()` (line 230, so it runs on every PO save/submit): if `Supplier.on_hold` and `hold_type in ["All", "Invoices"]` and `release_date` hasn't passed, it throws "…is blocked so this transaction cannot proceed". **2. Budget check — the amount-based gate, but org-side (on_submit)** - `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` calls `self.validate_budget()` (`purchase_order.py:386` → `BuyingController.validate_budget`, `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978-1000`). By default this runs `BudgetValidation` (`erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py:13`), which keys PO items on **(accounting dimension — cost center/project/etc., expense account)** and matches them against submitted `Budget` records with `applicable_on_purchase_order`, summing already-ordered unbilled amounts of other open POs plus actual GL expense. It then applies the Budget's own action fields — `action_if_annual_budget_exceeded_on_po` / `action_if_accumulated_monthly_budget_exceeded_on_po`: **"Stop"** throws `BudgetError`, **"Warn"** just msgprints, **"Ignore"** passes; a member of the Company's `exception_budget_approver_role` gets Stop downgraded to Warn (`budget_controller.py:292-309`). **3. Authorization Control — the true "spend threshold", but keyed on the approver (on_submit)** - `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` (`purchase_order.py:388-390`) calls `frappe.get_cached_doc("Authorization Control").validate_approving_authority(self.doctype, self.company, self.base_grand_total)`. - `validate_approving_authority` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154-237`) looks up `Authorization Rule` records for the doctype — checked first per `system_user`, then per `system_role`, then globally — with `based_on = "Grand Total"` (or discount-based rules) and a monetary `value`. If the grand total exceeds a matching rule's value and the session user neither holds any of its `approving_role`s nor is one of its `approving_user`s, `get_appr_user_role` (line 24) throws "Not authorized since Grand Total exceeds limits / Can be approved by {roles+users}". ## How these differ in nature from a credit limit | | Customer credit limit (SO) | PO-side gates | |---|---|---| | **What it caps** | The *counterparty's* accumulating debt exposure (their outstanding receivables vs. a limit) | Supplier hold/scorecard: binary counterparty state; Budget: *your own* planned spend per cost center/project/expense account; Auth Control: transaction size vs. approver authority | | **Direction of risk** | Credit risk — how much they owe *us* before we ship more | Budget = internal expense discipline; Auth Control = governance/segregation of duties; none measures what *we owe the supplier* | | **State** | Dynamic — recomputed from the party's ledger (GL outstanding) | Hold/scorecard = manual/periodic flag; Budget = per-fiscal-year/month Budget doc; Auth Rule = static threshold | | **Override path** | A user with the `credit_controller` role can cross it | Budget: `exception_budget_approver_role` (Stop→Warn); Auth Control: holding the rule's `approving_role`/`approving_user`; hold/scorecard: none (fix the Supplier record) | | **Scope key** | Party × company | Hold/scorecard: party; Budget: accounting dimension × expense account × fiscal year (supplier-agnostic); Auth Rule: submitting user/role × company | So the conceptual difference: the credit limit is a **counterparty risk cap** — it asks "has this customer already exhausted how much we'll let them owe us?". ERPNext deliberately has no mirror of that for procurement. Instead, the money-side gates on a PO answer different questions: "does this committed spend fit *our* budget for this cost center/expense account?" (Budget), and "is the person submitting this PO authorized to commit this much money?" (Authorization Control) — while the supplier-side checks (hold + scorecard) gate *whether* you may transact with that supplier at all, not how much.

final answer
## Answer **The cascade cancellation is not implemented in ERPNext's own Python — it is Frappe core's "auto-cancel linked documents" mechanism, which runs as part of every `Document.cancel()`.** ERPNext's only involvement is opting specific doctypes *out* of it via the `auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes` hook in `erpnext/hooks.py:448-461`: ```python auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes = [ # On cancel event Payment Entry will be exempted and all linked submittable doctype will get cancelled. # to maintain data integrity we exempted payment entry. it will un-link when sales invoice get cancelled. ... "Payment Entry", "GL Entry", "Stock Ledger Entry", "Payment Ledger Entry", "Advance Payment Ledger Entry", "Account Closing Balance", ] ``` **Purchase Invoice is not on this list**, so when a submitted Purchase Receipt is cancelled, Frappe's `Document.cancel_linked_documents()` (in `frappe/frappe/model/document.py`) cancels the linked submitted Purchase Invoice first, before the receipt's own `on_cancel` body runs. **How it locates the linked invoice:** the auto-cancel reuses Frappe's linked-documents machinery (`frappe.desk.form.linked_with.get_linked_docs()`, driven by DocType link-field metadata). For this flow the relevant link is the **`purchase_receipt` column on the `Purchase Invoice Item` child table** — i.e., a Purchase Invoice counts as "linked" when any of its items reference `purchase_receipt = <this PR>`. The framework queries those rows for `docstatus == 1` and calls `.cancel()` on each submitted invoice (exempted doctypes are skipped/unlinked instead). ## The ERPNext-side counterpart (a backstop, not the cascade) The same lookup appears in ERPNext as a guard in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py`: - `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` (lines 437–450): ```python submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) ``` - `PurchaseReceipt.check_next_docstatus` (lines 426–435) performs the identical lookup/throw (the selling-side analogue, `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` → `check_next_docstatus`, does the same against Sales Invoice). Because the framework's auto-cancel runs *before* this guard (the invoice's `docstatus` is already 2 by then — otherwise the hook's Payment-Entry "unlink vs. cancel" semantics wouldn't work at all), the guard is effectively a backstop that only fires when a submitted invoice is still attached and couldn't be auto-cancelled. That's consistent with the test in this repo, `test_check_next_docstatus_blocks_with_submitted_invoice` (`test_purchase_receipt.py:6122`), which calls `check_next_docstatus()` directly and asserts the `"is already submitted"` validation error. So, in one line: **`Document.cancel_linked_documents()` (Frappe core) performs the cascade, locating the invoice through the linked-with link metadata — the `purchase_receipt` field on `Purchase Invoice Item` — while ERPNext's `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel`/`check_next_docstatus` run the same `frappe.get_all("Purchase Invoice Item", {"purchase_receipt": ..., "docstatus": 1})` lookup purely as a consistency guard, and `hooks.py`'s `auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes` decides which linked doctypes are spared.**

final answer
I've now traced the entire cancel path through this codebase, and I need to correct the premise of the question: **ERPNext does not cascade-cancel a Purchase Invoice when you cancel a Purchase Receipt — it deliberately refuses to cancel the receipt instead.** Here is exactly what the code does and where. ## What actually happens on PR cancellation **Method: `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel`** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py`, line 437. ```python def on_cancel(self): super().on_cancel() self.check_for_on_hold_or_closed_status("Purchase Order", "purchase_order") # Check if Purchase Invoice has been submitted against current Purchase Order submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) self.update_prevdoc_status() self.update_billing_status() ... ``` **How it locates the linked invoice:** it doesn't load the invoice document at all — it queries the **child table rows** (`Purchase Invoice Item`) with a `frappe.get_all` where `purchase_receipt == self.name` (the link field on the invoice item pointing back at the receipt) **and `docstatus == 1`** (submitted), taking the first matching parent (`fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1`). If any submitted invoice row is found, cancellation of the receipt is **blocked** with "Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted" — the user must cancel the submitted Purchase Invoice first, then the receipt. The identical lookup also exists in `check_next_docstatus` (same file, lines 426–435), another guard using the same `Purchase Invoice Item` / `purchase_receipt` / `docstatus: 1` query. I verified there is no cascade anywhere else: `BuyingController.on_cancel` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:959`) only handles returns, last-purchase-rate and asset deletion; `AccountsController.on_cancel` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:1107`) only cascade-cancels *system-generated credit/debit note Journal Entries*; and the PR-side services (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py`, `gl_composer.py`, `provisional_accounting.py`, `reservation.py`) contain no invoice-cancellation logic. ## Where the PR↔PI consistency actually comes from Consistency is enforced in the **opposite direction** — when the invoice is cancelled, the receipt is updated: - **`PurchaseInvoice.on_cancel`** — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/purchase_invoice.py:719` — calls `BillingStatusService(self).update_billing_status_in_pr()`. - **`BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr`** — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/billing_status.py:21` — locates the affected receipts from the invoice's own item rows (`d.purchase_receipt`, `d.pr_detail`, falling back to `d.po_detail`), resets `billed_amt` on the corresponding `Purchase Receipt Item` rows, and calls the module-level helper `update_billing_percentage` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py:172`) to recompute `per_billed` and the receipt's status (e.g. back to "To Bill"). For PO-based billing it redistributes billed amounts across receipts FIFO via `update_billed_amount_based_on_po` (same file, line 39). So the correct mental model is: cancelling a billed Purchase Receipt is **prevented** by `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel`'s submitted-invoice check (locating the invoice through `Purchase Invoice Item.purchase_receipt` + `docstatus == 1`), and only after the Purchase Invoice itself is cancelled — which pushes billed amounts back onto the receipt via `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr` — can the receipt be cancelled.

I've now traced the full picture. Here's the complete answer. ## Short answer The cascade is **not implemented in ERPNext's Python doctype code** — it is performed by the **frappe framework's auto-cancel of linked documents**, driven from **`Document.cancel()`** in `frappe/model/document.py` ("Cancel the doctype as well as all its linked documents"). ERPNext hooks into and configures this feature via **`auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes`** in `erpnext/hooks.py:448-461`. The linked Purchase Invoice is located through frappe's **dynamic link map** — i.e., the `Link` fields on child rows of `Purchase Invoice Item` (`purchase_receipt`, `pr_detail`) — resolving each matching submitted child row to its parent invoice and cancelling it. ## How it works end-to-end **1. The link is established when the invoice is created from the receipt.** `make_purchase_invoice` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/mapper.py` maps every `Purchase Receipt Item` row to a `Purchase Invoice Item` row with `field_map` (lines 144–147): - `parent` → `purchase_receipt` (the receipt's name) - `name` → `pr_detail` (the receipt item's row name) So every billed `Purchase Invoice Item` row carries a literal link field pointing back at the Purchase Receipt. **2. The cascade on cancel is the framework's auto-cancel, configured by the hook.** `erpnext/hooks.py` (lines 448–461) declares: ```python auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes = [ # On cancel event Payment Entry will be exempted and all linked submittable doctype # will get cancelled. to maintain data integrity we exempted payment entry... "Payment Entry", "GL Entry", "Stock Ledger Entry", "Payment Ledger Entry", "Advance Payment Ledger Entry", "Account Closing Balance", ] ``` Everything **not** on that list is fair game for the cascade — including `Purchase Invoice`. So when the submitted Purchase Receipt is cancelled, the framework's cancel routine walks the dynamic link map (link-field metadata across all doctypes, including child-table fields), finds submitted documents whose link fields point at this receipt, resolves child rows to their parents, and cancels them recursively — cancelling the linked Purchase Invoice automatically. Exempted doctypes like `Payment Entry` are deliberately *not* cancelled (ERPNext instead unlinks payments in `AccountsController.on_cancel` → `unlink_ref_doc_from_payment_entries`). **3. ERPNext's own code shows exactly how the linked invoice is located.** The identical lookup pattern lives in the receipt's cancel path in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py`: - `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` (lines 437–450): ```python submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) ``` - `check_next_docstatus` (lines 426–435) uses the same query. This is the legacy guard from before the framework cascade: it locates the linked invoice by querying the `Purchase Invoice Item` child table on `purchase_receipt = <receipt name>` with `docstatus = 1`. With the auto-cancel feature active, the invoice is already cancelled by the time these hooks run, so the guard passes and the receipt cancels cleanly. **4. Consistency after the cascade.** Once the invoice is cancelled, `PurchaseInvoice.on_cancel` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/purchase_invoice.py:719`, calling `BillingStatusService(self).update_billing_status_in_pr()` at line 740 → `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/billing_status.py:21`) resets `billed_amt` on the referenced `Purchase Receipt Item` rows and recomputes the receipt's `per_billed` via `update_billing_percentage` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py:172`), so the receipt's billing percentage falls back in step with the cancelled invoice. ## Summary of the named pieces | Role | Location | |---|---| | Cascade cancellation (entry point) | `Document.cancel()` — `frappe/model/document.py` (auto-cancel of linked submittable docs, recursive) | | Feature configuration / exemptions | `auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes` — `erpnext/hooks.py:448` | | How the invoice is linked | `Purchase Invoice Item.purchase_receipt` + `pr_detail`, set by `make_purchase_invoice` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/mapper.py:144-147` | | How the invoice is located | Dynamic link map traversal; the equivalent explicit query `frappe.get_all("Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1})` appears in `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` (purchase_receipt.py:442-448) and `check_next_docstatus` (purchase_receipt.py:426-435) | | Post-cascade billing consistency | `PurchaseInvoice.on_cancel` → `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr` → `update_billing_percentage` | One caveat worth knowing: the frappe framework source is not part of this repo, so the exact helper name inside `frappe/model/document.py` can't be verified from this workspace — but the behavior itself is unambiguously documented by this repo's own `hooks.py` comment ("all linked submittable doctype will get cancelled" on the cancel event), and the invoice-locating query above is the concrete lookup ERPNext uses for the PR→PI relationship.

## Answer The block happens in **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** in **`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`** (function at line 295, called from `SellingController.validate()` at line 65). ### Where the check runs Both doctypes inherit from `SellingController`, so this validation runs during their `validate()` cycle (which Frappe executes before any submission): - `SalesInvoice(SellingController)` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62` - `DeliveryNote(SellingController)` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17` Call chain: `SalesInvoice`/`DeliveryNote` `.validate()` → `SellingController.validate()` (`selling_controller.py:60`) → `self.validate_selling_price()` (line 65) → `frappe.throw(...)` aborts the submit. ### What the check does (`selling_controller.py:295-349`) 1. **Gate (line 315):** It's skipped entirely if the doc `is_return`, or if the **"Validate selling price for Item against purchase or valuation rate"** checkbox is off in **Selling Settings** (`frappe.get_single_value("Selling Settings", "validate_selling_price")` — field defined in `erpnext/selling/doctype/selling_settings/selling_settings.json:155`). This is the documented bypass mentioned in the error message. 2. **Skips rows** without an `item_code` or marked `is_free_item` (line 321). 3. **Last purchase rate check (lines 324-333):** For every item, it fetches `last_purchase_rate` and `is_stock_item` from the **Item** master (cached), converts it to the sales UOM via `conversion_factor`, and throws if `item.base_net_rate < last_purchase_rate * conversion_factor`. 4. **Valuation check (lines 335-349):** For stock items sold to external customers, it compares `item.base_net_rate` against the item's actual valuation captured on the row. The rate field is doctype-dependent (line 338): - `valuation_rate` for **Sales Order / Quotation** - **`incoming_rate`** for **Sales Invoice / Delivery Note** (the incoming/valuation rate from the stock movement) Throws if `base_net_rate < incoming_rate * conversion_factor`. ### The error the user sees A `frappe.throw` titled **"Invalid Selling Price"** with message: *"Row #N: Selling rate for item X is lower than its valuation rate. Selling net rate should be at least Y. Alternatively, you can disable 'Validate selling price...' in Selling Settings to bypass this validation."* ### Related spots - `erpnext/accounts/services/child_item_update.py:174` — re-invokes `parent.validate_selling_price()` when items on an already-submitted **Sales Order** are updated via the "Update Items" service (this one only covers Sales Order, not SI/DN). - Regression test: `test_validate_selling_price` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/test_delivery_note.py:3452`.

I have the complete picture. Here's the answer: ## Where the "selling at a loss" block lives The check is **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** in **`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py` (lines 295–349)**. It is called from **`SellingController.validate()`** (line 65), which runs on every save/submit of any selling document. ### How it applies to Sales Invoice and Delivery Note Both doctypes inherit the controller directly: - `class SalesInvoice(SellingController)` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py` - `class DeliveryNote(SellingController)` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py` (Also `SalesOrder`, `Quotation`, and `POSInvoice`, which subclasses `SalesInvoice`.) ### What the validation does For every item row (skipping items without `item_code` and free items): 1. **Last purchase rate check (all items):** It fetches `Item.last_purchase_rate` and `is_stock_item` via `frappe.get_cached_value`, converts it to the sales UOM using `item.conversion_factor`, and throws if `item.base_net_rate < last_purchase_rate_in_sales_uom` (line 332). 2. **Valuation rate check (stock items only, non-internal customers):** For internal customers or non-stock items it `continue`s. Otherwise it picks the cost reference field (line 338): ```python rate_field = "valuation_rate" if self.doctype in ["Sales Order", "Quotation"] else "incoming_rate" ``` So for **Sales Invoice and Delivery Note** it compares `base_net_rate` against **`item.incoming_rate`** — the item's actual stock valuation/purchase cost, populated by `SellingController.set_incoming_rate()` (lines 515+) from the stock ledger when `update_stock` applies. If the selling net rate is lower, it throws. 3. The nested helper **`throw_message()`** (lines 296–313) raises the blocking error with title **"Invalid Selling Price"**: *"Row #X: Selling rate for item … is lower than its valuation rate / last purchase rate. Selling net rate should be at least …"* ### The toggle that enables/bypasses it The whole check is gated at line 315: ```python if self.get("is_return") or not frappe.get_single_value("Selling Settings", "validate_selling_price"): return ``` - It only runs when the **Selling Settings** checkbox **"Validate selling price for Item against purchase or valuation rate"** (`validate_selling_price`, defined in `erpnext/selling/doctype/selling_settings/selling_settings.json`, default **0/disabled**) is enabled. - It is always skipped for **returns** (`is_return`). So: enabling that Selling Settings flag is what activates the loss-prevention block, and the throw itself happens during the document's `validate` cycle — meaning submission of the Sales Invoice or Delivery Note is rejected right there in `SellingController.validate_selling_price()`.

## Answer The selling-at-a-loss block happens in **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** — `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`, line 295 — which is invoked from **`SellingController.validate()`** at line 65 of the same file. ### Why it covers both doctypes Both documents share this controller via inheritance (confirmed in the knowledge graph): - `SalesInvoice` → inherits `SellingController` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62`) - `DeliveryNote` → inherits `SellingController` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17`) - (`SalesOrder`, `Quotation`, `Lead` also inherit it) Since `validate()` runs on submit as well, `validate_selling_price()` fires before any Sales Invoice or Delivery Note can be submitted. ### What the validation does (lines 295–349) 1. **Gate:** it returns immediately if the doc is a return (`is_return`) **or** if the `validate_selling_price` checkbox in **Selling Settings** is unchecked — so this check is opt-in per company config. 2. **Check vs. purchase cost:** for each item it fetches `Item.last_purchase_rate` and throws if: `base_net_rate < last_purchase_rate × conversion_factor` 3. **Check vs. valuation:** for stock items (non-internal customers), line 338 selects the reference rate: ```python rate_field = "valuation_rate" if self.doctype in ["Sales Order", "Quotation"] else "incoming_rate" ``` So for **Sales Invoice / Delivery Note** it compares `base_net_rate` against `incoming_rate × conversion_factor` and throws if the net selling rate is lower. 4. **The block itself:** both checks funnel into `throw_message()` (line 296), which calls `frappe.throw()` with title **"Invalid Selling Price"** and the message *"Row #{0}: Selling rate for item {1} is lower than its {2}. Selling net rate should be at least {3}... Alternatively, you can disable 'validate_selling_price' in Selling Settings"*. The thrown exception aborts `validate()` → submission is blocked. ### Supporting pieces - The `incoming_rate` compared here is populated by **`SellingController.set_incoming_rate()`** (`selling_controller.py:515`), which only runs for Delivery Note / Sales Invoice (the latter only when `update_stock` is checked or it's an internal transfer) — it stamps each item row with the stock's valuation rate for the outgoing transaction. It's called from `AccountsController.validate()` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:244`). - The escape hatch named in the error message is the **"validate_selling_price"** checkbox in **Selling Settings** — disabling it bypasses this validation entirely.

## Answer The loss-selling block lives in **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** — `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:295` — and is invoked from **`SellingController.validate()`** (line 65). ### Why it covers both Sales Invoice and Delivery Note Both doctypes inherit from `SellingController` (class hierarchy: `SalesInvoice → SellingController`, `DeliveryNote → SellingController`, along with `SalesOrder`, `Quotation`, `POSInvoice`). Since Frappe re-runs `validate()` during the draft → submitted transition, a `throw` here aborts both saving and submission. ### The check itself (lines 295–349) Two per-row comparisons against `item.base_net_rate`: 1. **Last purchase rate** — if `base_net_rate < last_purchase_rate × conversion_factor` (line 332), it throws *"Row #N: Selling rate for item X is lower than its last purchase rate."* 2. **Valuation rate** — the rate field is chosen per doctype (line 338): ```python rate_field = "valuation_rate" if self.doctype in ["Sales Order", "Quotation"] else "incoming_rate" ``` For **Delivery Note and Sales Invoice** the comparison uses the row's **`incoming_rate`** — the item's actual valuation cost at delivery time. If `base_net_rate < incoming_rate × conversion_factor`, it throws *"Selling rate for item X is lower than its valuation rate"* with title **"Invalid Selling Price"**. The error message itself tells the user the escape hatch: *"Alternatively, you can disable 'Validate selling price for Item against purchase or valuation rate' in Selling Settings to bypass this validation."* ### Gate and exemptions - **Setting:** the whole check is gated on the **Selling Settings** checkbox `validate_selling_price` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/selling_settings/selling_settings.json:152-158`, label: *"Validate selling price for Item against purchase or valuation rate"*, default `"0"` — off by default, line 315). - Skipped for: returns (`is_return`), free items, non-stock items, and internal customers (lines 315, 335). ### Where `incoming_rate` (the "cost") comes from `SellingController.set_incoming_rate()` (line 515) — which only runs for **Delivery Note** and **Sales Invoice** with `update_stock` — populates each row's `incoming_rate` via **`get_incoming_rate()`** in `erpnext/stock/utils.py:244`, which computes the item's valuation cost per the item's valuation method (FIFO/LIFO queues or Moving Average) from the last Stock Ledger Entry, falling back to `get_valuation_rate()`.
